3dmm-overview.title: 3D morphable models: survey
3dmm-overview.summary:
I wrote the 3DMM survey note (about 2,550 words), its sources file and its data file. Neither the harvest nor an earlier draft existed, so every claim comes from my own expert knowledge: 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 57 🧠 / 27 ↔️. The sources list is empty, and the note names 19 canonical references by name only. Where another library note has a sourced version of a related claim, I point to it by its path.

The note covers:
- **History:** from Blanz & Vetter 1999 through the Basel models (2009, 2017, 2019), FLAME (2017, 2020, 2023), LSFM, LYHM, UHM, Surrey, FaceWarehouse, FaceScape, ICT-FaceKit, FaceVerse and
algorithmic: Use one adapter per model, carrying mean (mm), U_id, sigma_id, optional U_exp/sigma_exp/joints/LBS, landmark embeddings as (face_idx, barycentric), region masks, UV, units, axis matrix, licence, commercial_ok and a population tag. Normalise at load so β ~ N(0, I).
Self-test the basis normalisation: +1 SD on component 1 should move vertices by an RMS of roughly 2–8 mm. Microns or metres means the σ vs σ² scaling or the units are wrong.
Prior: ½‖β‖² with residuals whitened by landmark σ, so λ = 1 gives the MAP estimate. For sitters outside the training population, scale σ_id by about 1.5 (a guess; tune on held-out views).

Choose K from the constraint count: 30–50 for sparse landmarks over 3–9 views, 100–300 for dense or photometric fitting, scheduled 10 → 50 → full. After that, use Laplacian or RBF per-vertex offsets (≲3–5 mm).

‖β‖² gate: flag fits above the χ²_K 99.9 % quantile (K=50: 86.7; K=100: 149.5; K=300: 381.5). A MAP fit falling well below the median is expected and only marks under-constrained modes. Also report per-region Mahalanobis distance using the marginal covariance U_R U_Rᵀ.

Expression and pose priors: on neutral-tagged views ψ ~ N(0, 0.3²) and jaw σ ≈ 2–3°. On expressive views, ψ ~ N(0, 1) per view with β shared. Treat eye rotations as nuisances bounded to ±30°. Fit global scale with prior N(1, 0.04–0.05²) only when a metric cue exists.

Exact basis transfer to our own template: x̄′ = W x̄ and U′ = (W ⊗ I₃) U, where W is a sparse barycentric map. The prior stays N(0, I). Compute this locally from files the user supplies, never ship it (it is a licence derivative), and never copy coefficients from one model to another.
Use a soft bilateral symmetry prior (1.5–3 mm), not a symmetric projection. Real asymmetric modes are part of the PCA bases.
takeaways: How many vertices a mesh has says nothing about how much shape it can express. The Basel Face Model (BFM) has 53,490 vertices but only 199 components learnt from 200 people. FLAME has 5,023 vertices but 300 components learnt from about 3,800 people.

Choose the model by licence first. BFM, FLAME, LSFM, LYHM, UHM, FaceScape and FaceWarehouse are non-commercial research only. ICT-FaceKit (MIT) is the main permissive option, and 'FLAME 2023 Open' is unconfirmed.

Every model is biased toward the people it was trained on. BFM, FLAME and LSFM lean European, FaceScape, FaceVerse and HIFI3D lean East Asian, and FLAME is adults only. Make the prior's mean selectable and widen σ for sitters outside the training population.

Do not sculpt on raw FLAME. Its edges are 3–6 mm long, so eyelid margins and the lip border get only 1–2 edges. Fit FLAME, move the fit to a quad template through a fixed barycentric correspondence, then add Multires.
FLAME has no mouth interior and only coarse eyeballs and ears. Swap in real eye assets, start from ICT-FaceKit if the mouth will be open, and treat ears and the scalp as placeholders.

Check vertex count, units and axes on import, then check face width (adult zygion–zygion ≈125–150 mm). Units are a frequent silent failure: FLAME is in metres, BFM 2009 stores coordinates in sub-mm units.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so every fact is unverified expert recall (🧠 or ↔️) and no URLs are cited.
Vertex counts not recalled for LSFM, LYHM, UHM, ICT-FaceKit and FaceVerse. Low-confidence integers for the BFM 2017 crops, FaceScape, HIFI3D++ and FaceWarehouse's expression dimension.
What BFM 2019 changed versus BFM 2017 (data, components, full-head topology) is not recalled.
What FLAME 2023 changes (eyelids?) and the terms of its 'Open' variant.
Whether LSFM, LYHM and UHM are still distributed in 2026, and their current licence terms. FaceVerse and HIFI3D/HIFI3D++ licences.
ICT-FaceKit training subject count, and whether the scan subjects' consent allows commercial derivatives.
No sourced compactness or generalisation curves (mm error vs K) comparing models on held-out scans. These would ground the choice of K.
No check of any 2025–2026 large-population, commercially licensable head model.

aging-face.title: Facial aging mechanics
aging-face.summary:
This topic had no harvest and no earlier draft, so I wrote the note from expert knowledge. It cites 22 real URLs taken from sibling harvests in the library (mouth-lips-teeth, facial-asymmetry, the muscles-* harvests, skull-osteology, soft-tissue-thickness and ear), following the precedent set by smas-ligaments.md, and the note says this in its Sources section. Body text is about 2,800 words. Evidence status: 3 ✅ / 14 📄 / 55 🧠 / 29 ↔️. The note covers:
- skeletal ageing of the orbit (superomedial and inferolateral rim recession), the maxilla and pyriform aperture (angles decrease), and the mand
algorithmic: Age basis kept separate from identity, with names matching smas-ligaments.md: laxity ~ N(clip((age-25)/50,0,1), 0.2); deep_cheek_volume mean -0.04*max(0,age-35) mm, sigma 1.5; orbital_fat_prolapse in [0,1]; temporal_hollow 0–4 mm, raised when BMI is low; orbit_rim_recession 0–3 mm, sigma 1; maxilla_retrusion 0–10 deg, sigma 3; gonial_opening 0–5 deg, sigma 2; alveolar_collapse gated by dental_status; skin_age affects texture only. All are placeholders to calibrate.

Age input: age_years from the subject has sigma 1 year. An estimated age has sigma about 6 years, widened for makeup, filters, harsh light or under-represented skin types. Sculpt the age the photos show; use chronological age only for priors on what photos cannot see, such as the bony orbit.

Landmark priors that change with age: ls–sto mu = 8.0 - 0.05*(age-25) mm, sigma 1.5; incisor display mu = max(0, 3 - 0.07*(age-25)) mm, sigma 1.2; ear length + 0.2*(age-25) mm, sigma 3; lid–cheek junction distance grows (sigma 3 mm); brow height N(young value, 4 mm) with no forced descent.
Total soft-tissue depth gets only a small, site-specific age term, N(0, 1.5 mm), larger at zygion and gonion. Age enters mainly through redistribution, not net loss.
The symmetry prior loosens with age: sigma_sym = sigma0*(1 + 0.01*(age-25)).

Fit the mesh on contours and landmarks. Down-weight photometric terms over fold and wrinkle regions. Detect fine lines with a ridge filter only in raking-light frames. Split static detail from expression-dependent detail (DECA-style) and store dynamic lines as corrective maps per action unit.

Apply edits in the order bone → deep fat → superficial fat → laxity → skin, and de-age in reverse. Clamp laxity so tissue never crosses ligament strips. Expose a single age slider that drives each layer through curves.
FLAME has no age parameter, so an age direction must be regressed from aged scans. BFM 2009 has linear attribute directions. Check data licences.
takeaways: Model age as separate anatomical layers, each with its own parameters: bone recession, fat deflation and growth, ligament-anchored laxity, and skin texture. A single 'old' blendshape or wrinkles alone give a young volume under old skin.

For a consenting subject, ask for age, dental status (dentures or implants), botulinum toxin, fillers and recent weight change. Use photo-based apparent-age estimation only as a fallback prior with sigma of about 6 years.

Sourced age numbers: upper vermilion falls from about 8.1 mm (20–29) to 6.6 mm (50–59); skin is 1.1–1.9 mm thick (✅); facial asymmetry increases with age; depressor pull moves the modiolus down and inward (✅).
The lateral face stays fixed while the anterior face deflates and moves inferomedially. The jowl sits between the masseteric and mandibular ligament lines, so never sag the whole face straight down.
Fine lines belong in normal or bump maps, expression wrinkles in Multires displacement, and folds (NLF, marionette, tear trough, jowl) in the base mesh and shape keys.
Edentulous collapse, nose and ear lengthening, a longer upper lip with thinner vermilion, and a smaller resting incisor display are age cues that are often forgotten.
BMI splits ageing into two paths: lean faces become skeletal, while heavy faces hide bone loss and gain jowl and submental mass.
gaps: This topic's own harvest and draft were missing. Every URL comes from sibling harvests, so no source in the library deals mainly with skeletal ageing, fat-compartment ageing or skin ageing.
Shaw/Kahn bone-ageing magnitudes, Gierloff fat CT, Darcy orbital MRI and Matros brow data are known only by name. Their numbers have not been extracted.
No per-compartment volume-versus-age curves and no longitudinal 3D dataset of the same people across decades with a usable licence.
Skeletal ageing data are mostly from cross-sectional Caucasian cohorts; East Asian, African and South Asian bone and fat ageing patterns are not quantified here.
Wrinkle depth classes (µm) are order-of-magnitude knowledge, not profilometry values.
Age-estimation accuracy, available models and their licences are time-sensitive and unverified.
The full table values of the Chinese 1174-adult layer study [13] and the Central Chinese study [14] were not extracted.

ai-assisted-sculpting.title: AI-assisted head creation: practitioner reviews
ai-assisted-sculpting.summary: Wrote the ai-assisted-sculpting note (about 2,660 words, not counting table markup), /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/ai-assisted-sculpting.json (no URLs; 17 references named from knowledge) and /home/user/minedesign/research/data/ai-assisted-sculpting.json (8 tables). Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so nothing could be cited by URL: every claim is marked 🧠 or ↔️ (48 🧠 / 21 ↔️, counted by script), with links to related notes (reddit-face-from-photos, blenderartists-forum, blender-face-addons, single-image-regression, identity-embeddings, reference-camera-setup). Th
algorithmic: New load_reference_mesh: GLB to OBJ on the Blender side, then read_obj; drop connected components with fewer than 1% of vertices; recompute normals.

Auto-orient the AI mesh: render orthographic views from 8-12 yaw angles, run the 2D landmark detector, pick the most confident and symmetric frontal view, then umeyama (with scale) to template landmarks; report procrustes_rmse in IOD units.
Scale from the metric multi-view solve (reconstruct_landmarks), else from IPD 63 ± 3.5 mm.

Point-to-plane AI-mesh term with Huber delta = 2 sigma, weighted by c = cos(normal, conditioning view direction): sigma 3-5 mm where c > 0.7, 6-10 mm where 0.3 < c <= 0.7; ≥15 mm or off where c <= 0.3; off on hair/beard masks, eyes, mouth interior and ears.

Priority order: photo landmarks (sigma 0.02-0.03 IOD) and fit_silhouettes, then anatomical priors, then the AI term; cap the AI term's total information per region at about 25% of the landmark information.

Non-rigid ICP: stiffness annealed from about 50 to 1 over 5-8 steps; reject pairs more than 10 mm apart, with normals more than 45° apart, or on a boundary; finish with laplacian_deform anchored at landmarks.

Depth-contradiction check: compare AI depth at glabella, pronasale, subnasale and pogonion with triangulate_points; if they differ by more than 3 sigma, turn the AI term off in that region and report it.
Close-up photo guard: if the source photo's 35 mm-equivalent focal length is under 35 mm (about 0.6 m or closer), multiply the AI depth weights by 0.25.
Never take eyes or lips from AI meshes: insert template eyeballs (24 mm, iris 11.7 mm); landmarks only from real photos.
Write ai_prior_weight and confidence vertex attributes to the Blender mesh for use as sculpt masks.
QA: compare face-recognition similarity on textured vs untextured renders through the solved cameras; a large gap means the geometry is not carrying the likeness.
takeaways: Practitioners agree that AI image-to-3D gives a plausible bust in minutes but almost never a likeness: identity comes mostly from the projected photo texture, so always judge in clay or matcap.

From one frontal photo the generator invents profile depth (nose and chin projection, eye depth, occiput); distinctive features regress toward the training average; eyes and lips come out fused and hair as a solid shell that inflates the cranium.
Selfie perspective is baked into the 3D shape; multi-view input helps only when the views are consistent, and AI-generated turnaround sheets make up the profile.

Topology consensus: neither raw triangle soup nor vendor quad remesh has proper edge loops; wrap a known base (FaceBuilder, Headshot 2 mesh mode, Mesh to MetaHuman, MPFB2 or our own template), then Multires.

Licences are a real constraint: Hunyuan3D's licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea; TRELLIS is MIT but has dependencies with non-commercial terms; free-tier service outputs may be public or CC BY. Uploading a real face also raises privacy, consent and GDPR questions.

Arithmetic: a 256³ grid on a 0.25 m head box is about 1 mm per voxel, roughly the size of likeness-bearing relief (0.5-5 mm); a full-body input image leaves the face about 37 px wide, so crop to the head.
Rule for the engine: AI output is a weak shape prior weighted by region, never landmark ground truth; photo landmarks and silhouettes always rank higher.
gaps: Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so no forum, video or social URL or quote is cited; all practitioner opinions are author synthesis.
No public benchmark gives mm error or recognition rate for Hunyuan3D, TRELLIS, Rodin, Meshy, Tripo, FaceBuilder or Headshot on real-person faces against scans.
Current versions (Hunyuan3D 3.x, TRELLIS.2, Rodin Gen-2, Tripo 3.x, Meshy 5/6), prices and free-tier output licences are unverified and change within months.
VRAM and timing figures are remembered from vendor READMEs, not checked.
The AI-prior sigmas, the 25% information cap and the 0.25 close-up down-weight are untested heuristics; they need calibration on a test set of real scans.
The eyelid crease, alar groove and philtrum relief sizes (0.5-5 mm) and the 0.13 m² head surface area are author estimates.
FaceBuilder, Headshot 2 and MetaHuman licence terms for exported meshes are not confirmed here (see sibling notes).

albedo-lighting-inverse-rendering.title: Albedo, lighting and inverse rendering for faces
albedo-lighting-inverse-rendering.summary:
I wrote the albedo, lighting and inverse-rendering note from expert knowledge only. Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so the note cites no URLs and /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/albedo-lighting-inverse-rendering.json has an empty sources list plus 27 references by name. The note has about 2,630 prose words; wc -w reports 3,081 because it counts table pipes, which is in line with sibling notes.

It covers:
- the image-formation model and its three ambiguities (albedo-vs-light scale, light colour vs skin hue, bas-relief shape vs light);
- order-2 spherical-harmonic
algorithmic: Forward model per view: Î_v = g_v ⊙ [a ⊙ E(R_v n)/π ⊙ V]. Albedo a is shared across views. E is shared in the head frame (photographer circles a still subject) or the world frame (subject turns), otherwise per view. Specular is masked in v1.
Gauge: fix g0 from the colour chart. Without a chart, set g0 = 1 and expose an 'absolute albedo unknown' flag with a tone slider instead of letting a PCA prior decide.

Stage B, with geometry fixed: alternate closed-form weighted least-squares SH (9×3 unknowns, Huber IRLS) with per-texel albedo a = I/(g·E·V/π) projected onto the prior, for 3–5 iterations. Optional stage C photometric shape refinement is accepted only if landmark and contour gates do not worsen.
Residual: r = log(I+ε) − log(Î+ε) with ε ≈ 0.01 linear and Huber δ ≈ 0.05, so dark and light skin carry equal weight.
Masks: skin parsing only; drop n·v < 0.3, AO < 0.7, any channel > 0.95, the brightest 2–5 % of skin, pixels below 3× the noise floor, and hair, brows, lips, eyes and nostrils.

Priors (normalised by L00, engineering values): log g_v σ 0.03 with a chart and 0.3 without; band-1/L00 σ 0.8; band-2/L00 σ 0.35; key elevation N(30°, 25°) and azimuth N(0°, 60°); SH chroma σ 0.05·L00; a radiance non-negativity hinge; global melanin uniform; low-pass log-albedo symmetry σ 0.05; log-albedo gradient Huber 0.05 per 5 mm; specular F0 fixed at 0.028.

SH→Blender: radiance L(ω) = Σ L_lm Y_lm (divide irradiance coefficients by Â_l first). Write an equirect EXR of at least 64×32 in z-up axes, clamp negatives and log the clamped energy. Cycles diffuse returns a·E/π.

Export the SH JSON with an explicit convention (radiance or irradiance, basis order, frame, units), together with the albedo EXR, AO, specular mask, per-view gains, an ITA report and a confidence map.
Fairness suite: sweep melanin over the 6 ITA groups × 5 light rigs × with and without a chart. Assert no monotone bias and |ΔITA| ≤ 5° per group, and report stratified results.
Ship no BFM or FLAME assets. Per-texel delighting with a melanin/haemoglobin chromophore prior avoids both the licences and the light-skinned PCA mean.
takeaways: Albedo and lighting cannot be separated from one uncalibrated photo: there is a per-channel scale and hue ambiguity, plus the bas-relief shape ambiguity. A colour chart in shot is the single highest-value addition; without one, the recovered skin tone is whatever the prior says.

SH9 (27 RGB coefficients) captures about 99 % of Lambertian shading but nothing about shadows, specular or how sharp the light is. SH coefficient vectors cannot be carried between codebases without converting the basis, the radiance/irradiance choice, the π folding and the frame.

BFM-family textures and FLAME's FFHQ texture space are not physical albedo: they carry residual or baked shading and a display encoding. AlbedoMM and TRUST's BalancedAlb are linear, but they come from small or curated samples.

Skin-tone bias comes from light-skewed PCA means, regularisation toward the mean, linear-RGB losses that under-weight dark pixels, exposure and JPEG crushing, and skin masks that miss pixels. Mitigate it with a chart-fixed gauge, a log-domain residual, a uniform tone prior and stratified ITA tests.

Practical delighting in Blender: project linearised photos into UV, bake white-mesh shading under the recovered SH world (Cycles Diffuse bake, Color off), divide, then fix tone against the chart-measured cheek ITA. Validate by relighting, not by re-rendering under the same light.
Contour makeup, brows and pigment are read as shading and get sculpted as form. Keep photometric weight subordinate to landmark and contour gates.
gaps: The topic had no harvest and no earlier draft, so the note has zero sourced or verified facts and no URLs.
There are no quantitative per-skin-tone albedo or ITA error numbers for DECA, Deep3D or TRUST; the TRUST paper tables need to be harvested.
Exact subject counts and licences are unconfirmed for AlbedoMM/3DRFE, BalancedAlb, the FLAME FFHQ texture space and FFHQ-UV.
There is no measured, tone-balanced, real (non-synthetic) face-albedo ground truth with an open licence to benchmark against.
There is no quantified comparison of linear vs sRGB vs log photometric losses on identity accuracy or tone fairness.
The worst-case per-pixel SH9 error bound and the Basri–Jacobs lower bound are not pinned down; the sources quoted differ.
There is no evidence on how accurate current AI delighters are (SwitchLight, RGB↔X, Substance 3D Sampler) or how they behave across skin tones, and their versions and licences are time-sensitive.
The bias that subsurface scattering introduces into Lambertian SH lighting estimates is unquantified.
Blender's current colour-space names (Linear Rec.709) and Cycles bake-panel options need checking against Blender 4.x/5.x.

anthropometric-norms.title: Quantitative facial anthropometry norms (Farkas and successors)
anthropometric-norms.summary:
I wrote the anthropometric-norms note from scratch because the earlier draft did not exist. It runs to about 2,900 words counting table text. Inputs were the harvest of 16 real URLs plus my own knowledge, and nothing has been through a verification pass yet. The note covers:
- Farkas's 1994 direct-anthropometry norms (N=2,326, North American White) and the Kolar critique.
- The 3D Facial Norms database (2,454 people aged 3–40, 952 M / 1,502 F; summary data open, individual data by access request; growth curves and a MATLAB toolbox).
- The 2011 inter-ethnic review (2,359 people, 27 groups) and
algorithmic: NormRecord schema: {id, a, b, distance: chord|proj_x|proj_y|proj_z|arc, frame: FH|camera, method: caliper|3d_surface|photo2d|ct, landmark_variant, population, sex, age_band, n, mean, sd, source_ids, status}; compare only when distance, method and landmark variant match, or after an explicit offset.

Log-normal priors log d ~ N(log mu, (k*CV)^2): k=1 when population, sex and method match; 1.5 for low-variance measures when population is unknown; ~2.5 or a population mixture for al–al and en–en when population is unknown; x1.2 default for Farkas-to-3D drift.

Use a multivariate prior (a 3D morphable model's scale-normalised shape covariance recentred on the chosen norm row) rather than independent Gaussians, or divide prior weight by the effective number of independent terms (widths and heights correlate r ~0.3–0.7).

Cap prior weight at ~10–20% of the objective when landmarks are seen in two or more pose-solved views; let priors dominate only unobserved directions (nose and chin depth with no profile, occiput with no rear view).
Global scale s ~ N(1, 0.035) from zy–zy or head breadth, combined with iris 11.7±0.5 mm or interpupillary 63±3.5 mm; a caliper measurement overrides all.
Chord consistency recovers depth: ex behind en = sqrt(ex–en^2 − ((ex–ex − en–en)/2)^2 − dy^2) ≈ 12.7 mm with NAW means.

Gates: |z|>2 amber and |z|>3 red mean a probable landmark, focal-length or definition error; refit focal length when al–al/zy–zy exceeds the population bound (perspective inflates it ~8–10% at 0.4 m).
Adult age drift terms centred at 25 y: ear length +~0.2 mm/yr, sn–sto up, ls–sto down, n–prn up.
Scale-free ratio priors (15 ratios, sigma_log 0.04–0.10) for single uncalibrated photos before absolute scale is fixed.
takeaways: Farkas's direct-anthropometry norms (N=2,326 North American White) remain the default mm reference, but 3DFN (2,454 people, 3D) differs considerably; always attach method, population, sex, age and landmark definition to any norm.
n–gn face height is the best-supported number: adult means ~120–126 mm (M) and ~112–116 mm (F), SD ~6–7 / ~4.5–5.5, across three sources.
Between-population differences in al–al and en–en are 3–5 within-group SDs, so nose-width and intercanthal priors are nearly useless without a population label; use a mixture or inflate sigma ~2.5x.
Head length, head breadth and zy–zy are tight (CV 3–4%) and make good priors for unseen depth and scale; vermilion heights, tip protrusion and philtrum width (CV 10–20%) must come from the photos.
Mouth corners on average align with the medial limbus, not the pupils; alae roughly sit below the inner canthi (al–al ≈ en–en) in North American White adults.
Norms are for sanity gates (|z|>3 means landmark, camera or definition error), scale and unobserved regions. Never pull observed features toward the mean: likeness lives in the deviations.
Caliper go–go, eu–eu and zy–zy are pressed onto bone and differ from photo silhouettes by mm to cm (masseter, fat, hair); never compare across definitions.
gaps: Full Farkas 1994 adult tables (means, SDs, per-cell n) not retrieved; Table 1 is recalled knowledge.
3DFN adult means by measurement not captured; the open summary data should replace the Table 1 defaults once downloaded.
Sample sizes missing for the Kosovo, Hong Kong and Malay studies; labels unclear in the 3D normotype paper.
Kolar 1993 critique not read; secular-trend magnitude since the 1970s unknown.
Mouth width, lip heights, ear length/width and head length/breadth have no sourced values in this library yet.
No Headspace-derived mm norms found; ANSUR II, NIOSH and SizeChina numbers are recall only.
Population-shift magnitudes (Table 5) are rough and contested.

art-anatomy-books.title: Classic art-anatomy references for heads
art-anatomy-books.summary: I rewrote the earlier draft, which had no sources, as a full reference on Loomis, Reilly, Asaro, Bridgman, Peck, Scott Spencer, Uldis Zarins, plus Goldfinger, Faigin, Winslow, Lanteri and Rubino. The dedicated art-anatomy harvest does not exist. I therefore cited 18 real URLs from this library's sibling harvests (facial-proportions-canons and anthropometric-norms), and the Sources section says so; those files sit outside the three inputs this step listed, so check whether that is acceptable. The cited sources are Proko and Fine Art Tutorials pages on Loomis construction, plus anthropometric pa
algorithmic: Store each canon as a prior record {name, landmarks_A, landmarks_B, stated_ratio, pop_mean, pop_sd, population, n, source_urls, status, weight}. The loader refuses a non-zero weight while status is 'knowledge'.

E_canon = Σ w_i((r_i − μ_i)/σ_i)² with w_i = w0·(1 − coverage_i) and w0 ≈ 0.05–0.1 relative to the landmark term. Canons are never hard constraints; they act mainly on depth dimensions that frontal-only photos leave unobserved.

Default priors (adult, to verify): eye line at 0.50 ± 0.02 of vertex–menton; en–en/en–ex 1.08 ± 0.10; al–al/en–en 1.05 ± 0.12; ch–ch/en–en 1.55 ± 0.12; ch–ch/IPD 0.83 ± 0.07; (g–sn)/(sn–me) 0.90 ± 0.08; (sn–sto)/(sn–me) 0.32 ± 0.03; (sa–sba)/(n–sn) 1.15 ± 0.12. Widen sigma by 1.5× when sex or population is unknown.
Gating: disable the vertical canons for children (eye line below 0.5). Tag every prior with its population. Give trichion (hairline) zero weight.

Loomis block-in initializer parameters: cranial radius R, side-plane offset of about 0.7–0.8 R, brow height, unit length, jaw width, chin projection and pitch, solved from 6–8 clicks across views, then handed to template warping or a PCA shape model (preferred, because it captures co-variation).

Author about 20–30 named plane-region vertex groups on the template (forehead front and sides, temple, brow ridge, orbit, lids, zygomatic front and side, nasal dorsum, sides, tip and alae, maxillary barrel, lips, mental, mandibular side and ramus). Use them for per-region regularization, single-light shading residuals and sculpt masks.

Separate expression layer: muscle → FACS AU → shape key, following the Zarins and Faigin tables. All AUs stay at 0 during the identity fit; flag residuals that look like expression and request a neutral photo.
Deviation report: rank per-canon |z| values and name them in art vocabulary in the UI ('wide-set eyes', 'long lower third').
takeaways: The art books fall into three families: construction canons (Loomis, Reilly, Bridgman), plane models (Asaro head, Reilly rhythms) and anatomical atlases (Peck, Goldfinger, Spencer, Zarins), with Faigin and Zarins covering expression.

Neoclassical canons fail for most measured individuals in several populations (Saudi, African American, Turkish). The orbital canon performs best but is met by only about a third of subjects or fewer. Treat canons as weak priors and a vocabulary, never as targets.

Loomis-type canons cite one idealized value with no variance. Sigma must come from anthropometry: linear facial dimensions vary by about 4–8% (n–gn SD 5–7 mm agrees across three sources), which gives sigma of about 8–12% for horizontal ratios.

Solve camera intrinsics and pose before checking any proportion. Perspective compresses thirds and halves, and selfies distort the nose and ears. Measure ratios only on the fitted 3D mesh in a Frankfort frame.
Plane models are best used as a check. A single-key-light render compared with the photo exposes errors in the cheek turn, brow and mouth barrel that landmark error misses.
Likeness lives in deviations from the canon. Report a z-score per canon and preserve large-|z| features instead of correcting them.

Bridgman's pre-1931 books appear to be public domain in the US; Loomis's status is disputed; the Asaro head and modern atlases are in copyright. Author your own plane regions rather than copying the Asaro facets.
gaps: No dedicated art-anatomy harvest exists. All book, author, year and publisher details for Loomis, Bridgman, Peck, Spencer, Zarins, Reilly and Asaro are expert knowledge and unverified.

The measured adult vertical levels normalized by vertex–menton (Table 2) and several horizontal ratio ranges are expert estimates, not taken from a cited dataset (ANSUR II, Farkas 1994 and 3DFN tables were not retrieved).
The exact Reilly rhythm-line set, the current Asaro head variants and their licence terms, and whether the Asaro planes have ever been compared quantitatively with scanned faces are all unknown.
The US copyright renewal status of Loomis's books and of Bridgman's Heads, Features and Faces (1932) is unresolved.
The claim that professionals recommend these books most is drawn from community knowledge; no forum threads (Reddit, Polycount, ZBrushCentral) were harvested.
The suggested prior sigmas are engineering derivations from a 4–8% coefficient of variation and have not been validated against 3D scan data.

artstation-likeness.title: ArtStation: likeness breakdowns and tutorials
artstation-likeness.summary:
Neither input existed: no harvest JSON and no earlier draft. So I wrote the note at /home/user/minedesign/research/community/artstation-likeness.md (about 2,750 words) entirely from expert knowledge and pinhole arithmetic. Evidence status is 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 57 🧠 / 26 ↔️.

It covers:
- the ArtStation platform and its content genres, all flagged as time-sensitive (Epic acquisition, Learning, Marketplace versus Fab, the anti-AI protest);
- the shared likeness process found across breakdowns: curation, scan or base mesh, low-resolution primary forms, cycling every view ("whack-a-mole"), symmetry off,
algorithmic: Per-photo metadata record: source_type, exif_f35, date, mirrored, anamorphic_desqueezed, expression, retouch_risk. Landmark σ = base σ (0.03×IOD interior, 0.06–0.08×IOD contour) × source multiplier (press 1.0, controlled 0.7–1.0, studio/magazine 2–3 or exclude, film 1.5–2, video 1.5–2.5, phone rear 1.2, selfie 3 or exclude).

Log-normal focal priors in f35 (σ_log = SD of ln f): controlled EXIF σ_log 0.02; selfie 26 mm σ_log 0.1; phone rear 26 mm σ_log 0.6; press 135 mm σ_log 0.5; studio 100 mm σ_log 0.4; film/video 50 mm σ_log 0.7. Perspective gives almost no depth beyond about 3 m, so require profile views.

Robust per-view noise scale (IRLS or Cauchy). Flag a view with a consistent signed jaw-contour/eye-size residual not explained by pose as likely liquify. Cap any single view at 40% or less of total data weight (no 'hero photo').
Coverage gate: at least 3 yaw bins and at least 1 view with |yaw| ≥ 60°, else warn that depth comes from the prior. Fix pixel aspect at 1.0 (σ 0.01) unless the frame is flagged anamorphic.
Phone lens-correction rule: inflate σ ×2 or exclude faces in f35 ≤ 16 mm shots, or beyond about 60% of the half-diagonal.

Brows (≥ 5 points each) and the hairline polyline are first-class fit targets, exported as Blender curves for groom guides and kept out of the skin-shape loss. User-clicked moles and scars seen in ≥ 2 views become bundle-adjustment tie points and texture anchors.
Fit neutral identity from neutral photos only. Offer an optional 'characteristic expression' shape key (0–1, default 0). Use an age-window outlier check on age-sensitive ratios (>3 robust SD).

Automated breakdown sheet per solved camera: photo, render, 50% overlay, difference, flipped, at full size and 64 px. Target primary-likeness tolerances (reprojection < 2–3% IOD, silhouette < 1–2 mm) within minutes.
takeaways: Pros curate references by source type: telephoto event photos are the main proportion source; liquified covers, anamorphic film stills, low-resolution interview frames and phone selfies each mislead in a known way.

The shared process is to curate one age window, block primary forms at low resolution, compare through matched cameras (or by eye), cycle all views, then do asymmetry, eyes, identity marks, brows and hair, and compare under photo-matched light.
Breakdowns consistently say the likeness clicks only once brows and hair exist, so add proxy brows and hairline early in Blender rather than 'fixing' correct geometry in bald grey clay.
Grooming and texturing take as much time as the sculpt (reported phase shares: groom 15–30%, primary likeness 20–35%). An engine that reaches primary likeness in minutes frees that time.
Professional realism usually starts from a licensed scan wrapped to clean topology. Production actor likeness is scan-based; hand-sculpted likeness dominates collectibles and portfolio work.
The ArtStation side-by-side shows the sculpt's best angle. Demand a held-out view, and automate a per-camera breakdown sheet (photo, render, overlay, difference, flipped, thumbnail).
There is no quantitative likeness tolerance anywhere in this genre: 'it clicked' has never been tied to millimetre residuals.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed. There are no sourced ArtStation breakdowns, quotes or URLs; every claim is 🧠 or ↔️.
No statement is attributed to any named artist; practitioner names are listed for orientation only and need checking.
Reported timelines and phase shares are self-reported heuristics with no sample, and so unverifiable as stated.
No source in this genre gives quantitative likeness tolerances (mm per feature) or ties 'it clicked' to measured residuals.
Platform facts are time-sensitive and unverified: Fab versus ArtStation Marketplace status, Learning availability, NoAI policy, and rules on depicting real people.
Prevalence and magnitude of liquify retouching in press photos, and smartphone face-warping behaviour, are unquantified.
Current Blender versus ZBrush high-resolution sculpt performance (5.x) is unverified.

awesome-lists-resources.title: Curated resource lists and communities
awesome-lists-resources.summary:
Neither input existed: there was no harvest file and no earlier draft. I wrote the note from expert knowledge, so it has 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 76 🧠 / 26 ↔️ and cites no URLs. It is about 2,740 words of prose, excluding markdown table syntax.

Main point: awesome lists (3D face/3DMM, talking head, Gaussian avatars, 3DGS) are self-submitted discovery indexes. They rarely record licences, weight terms, benchmark protocol or whether the code still runs, and they go stale within about 12 months.

The note covers:
- **Upstream assets the lists reuse:** FLAME, BFM, LSFM, LYHM/Headspace, FaceWarehouse, FaceScap
algorithmic: Ship an assets.toml registry with name, version, sha256, spdx_licence, commercial_ok (true/false/unknown), attribution, source_ref and retrieved. Bundle nothing that is non-commercial or unknown. Load FLAME and BFM only from user-supplied paths, and warn when the project is flagged commercial.

Default to a permissive template (MPFB2 CC0, or ICT-FaceKit once its licence is verified). Plug research 3DMMs in through one adapter interface: mean, basis, sigma, landmark_embedding (face index plus barycentric weights).

Store every landmark scheme (iBUG 68, WFLW 98, MediaPipe 478, ARKit 1,220, FLAME 51 static + 17 dynamic) as barycentric embeddings on the working template. Ship a 68↔478 correspondence so they share one levenberg_marquardt residual. Jaw contour points slide along the silhouette normal only.

Treat a single-specimen atlas skull as a weak prior: use it for region masks and placement, and if it enters the energy at all, use a similarity-aligned skull-to-template term with σ ≈ 4–6 mm. Licensed scan heads or AI meshes as shape priors: σ ≈ 3–5 mm per vertex after umeyama alignment, never as landmark ground truth.

Make the prior mean selectable to reduce population bias (BFM and FLAME skew European-descent, FaceScape East Asian). Widen σ by about 1.5× when the subject's ancestry is outside the prior's population (a guess; tune on held-out views).

Synthetic test harness: render CC0 or CC BY heads in Blender through 3–8 cameras (focal 24–135 mm equivalent, distance 0.4–3 m, yaw ±90°). Assert focal error under 5% and rotation error under 2° when views span at least 60° of yaw. Score shape with the NoW protocol (7-point rigid alignment, then vertex-to-surface distance in mm).
Keep the extension offline by default (the network permission must be declared): no list scraping or 'new methods' feed. Re-verify upstream licences at every release.
takeaways: Awesome lists are self-submitted discovery indexes. They almost never record code, weight or data licences, benchmark protocol or whether the code installs, and a list untouched for over 12 months misses most of a research generation. Read the surveys first (Zollhöfer 2018, Egger 2020, Morales 2021), then use lists only for papers published after them.

Nearly every listed face method sits on a few upstream assets (FLAME, BFM, LSFM/300-W, LYHM, FaceScape, MediaPipe, NeRSemble), and most are licensed for non-commercial research. The upstream licence, not the method's code licence, decides what an open-source add-on may ship.

dlib's 68-point model and InsightFace weights carry non-commercial terms despite permissive code. MediaPipe (Apache-2.0), 3DDFA_V2 (MIT), face-alignment (BSD-3) and eos (Apache-2.0) are the more shippable landmark and fitting references (all to verify).

For artists: anatomy atlases (Complete Anatomy, Zygote, Anatomy For Sculptors, open Z-Anatomy/BodyParts3D) each show one specimen or an idealised composite with no population variance. Use them for underlays and region labels, and take variance from anthropometric tables.

Licensed scan heads (3D Scan Store, Triplegangers) and Texturing.XYZ are for plane and volume comparison and for late micro-detail. Never use a scan as the base mesh, because it pulls the likeness toward the scanned person.
Discord is fast but cannot be searched or cited. Blender Stack Exchange, vendor forums and GitHub issue trackers hold the searchable fitting and tool lore.
gaps: No harvest file or earlier draft existed, so there are zero sourced or verified facts and no URLs. Every repo name, licence, dataset count and closure date is from memory.
Which 'awesome-3D-face', 'awesome-3DMM' and 'awesome-gaussian-avatars' repositories exist and are maintained in late 2026 is unknown.
Current prices and licence terms of 3D Scan Store, Texturing.XYZ, Triplegangers, Complete Anatomy, 3d.sk and Anatomy 360 were not checked.
The status of Papers with Code (reported shut down in 2025), the CGSociety forums (reported closed 2023–24) and the Sketchfab store's move into Fab is unconfirmed.
Exact dataset sizes are approximate: LYHM/Headspace subject counts, NeRSemble camera specs, Ava-256, LSFM, dense-landmark count.
No Discord server names or membership figures could be verified, so none are given.
The prior sigmas and test-harness acceptance thresholds are author-proposed engineering defaults, not measured values.
Licences for the Digital Emily 2.0 / Wikihuman release and the Smithsonian Lincoln life-mask scans are unconfirmed.

benchmarks-metrics.title: Benchmarks and metrics for face reconstruction accuracy
benchmarks-metrics.summary: Wrote the benchmarks-and-metrics note (about 2,500 words of prose plus 6 tables), its sources JSON (no URLs, 25 references by name) and a data JSON with 7 tables: benchmark cards, NoW anchors, REALY region ranges, nearest-vertex bias, error floors, acceptance targets and eval defaults. Neither input file existed (no harvest, no earlier draft), so every claim is expert knowledge (🧠) or contested (↔️). The NoW figures were checked against sibling notes, which cite sources for them, so the library stays consistent. Contents: NoW, REALY, Stirling/ESRC FG2018, FaceScape, Florence/MICC, AFLW2000-3D
algorithmic: Add face3d/eval/ (numpy only): closest_points(P,V,F) with a uniform-grid broad phase and Ericson's exact closest-point-on-triangle test; sign from the angle-weighted pseudo-normal; returns distance, signed distance, closest point and face id.

align(pred, gt, mode) with modes landmarks | rigid_icp | similarity_icp (NoW-compatible) | region, seeded by procrustes.umeyama on the 7 NoW landmarks or 6 stable ones (en×2, ex×2, n, sn). Point-to-plane ICP: 10 % trimming, 5–10 mm correspondence cap, 60° normal gate, ≤30 iterations, 1e-4 mm tolerance.
surface_report: area-weighted median, mean, std, RMS, p90, p95, F@0.5/1/2 mm and signed bias per template region label. Always print the Chamfer formula used.

Configuration metric: procrustes_rmse over 20–30 anatomical landmarks after landmark-only alignment, with per-landmark error vectors in a Frankfort frame. Scale metric: s − 1 plus % error of ex–ex, n–gn, zy–zy and t–t; flag |s − 1| > 3 %.
Normal metric after smoothing both surfaces to ≥9 mm wavelength. Likeness score = region-weighted RMS using face-perception weights, reported beside the NoW-style median, never inside the data term.

Priors derived from benchmarks (half-normal model): regressor shape prior σ ≈ 1.4 mm along the normal, raised to 2.5–3 mm at nose tip, chin and orbit depth; population prior σ ≈ 1.9 mm per surface point. Warn about prior dominance when the fit lies within 1 mm RMS of the mean face.
Held-out-view gate: accept a refinement only if held-out landmark (% IOD) and silhouette errors do not rise; flag a view whose held-out error exceeds 2× its in-sample error.
CI on face3d/synthetic.py subjects: assert median S2M, scale error and configuration RMS for each camera configuration.
takeaways: A face-reconstruction error number means nothing without its alignment (landmarks, ICP, with or without scale), its distance (scan-to-surface, Chamfer, nearest vertex) and its crop. Chamfer figures from different papers are not comparable.

NoW is near saturation. A scaled average FLAME face scores about 1.53 mm mean, MICA about 1.11 mm and the best entries about 0.95 mm, so single-image methods remove only about 27–38 % of the mean face's error. Gaps under 0.1 mm are noise.

NoW is blind to absolute size, local regions, lids, ears and likeness. REALY's per-region alignment fixes the regional blind spot but hides how far apart the features sit. Report both, plus a landmark-only alignment that keeps scale and configuration errors.

Measuring distance to the nearest vertex instead of the nearest surface adds about 0.35 × edge length of error, roughly 1–2 mm on FLAME's base mesh, which is larger than the signal. Always use point-to-triangle distances.
Ground-truth scans have a floor of about 0.3–1 mm between repeat captures of a live face. Scan each sitter twice and treat that difference as the deadband.

For the artist: show a signed heatmap built with Geometry Nodes (Geometry Proximity plus Sample Nearest Surface), ±2 mm range with a 0.3–0.5 mm deadband. Fix configuration first, then lids, brows and lips, then the nose profile, then broad planes.

Without a scan, the only real accuracy evidence is held-out views: leave-one-view-out reprojection and silhouette error. Add profile-contour mm, identity-embedding ceiling ratios on clay renders, and a blind lineup judged by people who know the sitter.
gaps: No input harvest or earlier draft existed, so no URL-cited sources; every item is 🧠 or ↔️.
The current (late-2026) NoW and REALY leaderboard leaders and their numbers are unknown.
Exact REALY correspondence and alignment rule, and per-method region values, were recalled only as ranges.
FaceScape benchmark bin edges, set sizes and Chamfer values were not recalled; licence terms need checking.
Stirling/ESRC FG2018 subject and image counts and 2018 result values are uncertain.
Florence/MICC 95 mm crop and the scale handling in its point-to-plane protocol are unverified.
No measured mapping from regional mm error to perceived likeness or lineup accuracy, and no 3D just-noticeable-displacement data.
No public benchmark for 3–9 consumer photos with perspective and metric scale; the acceptance targets in Table 6 are design defaults, not norms.
Blender Geometry Nodes node names (Geometry Proximity, Sample Nearest Surface) are version-sensitive and not checked against Blender 5.x.

biometric-privacy.title: Biometric privacy law and face geometry
biometric-privacy.summary: Wrote the biometric-privacy note (about 2,720 words) from author knowledge only. Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so the note cites no URLs and every claim carries 🧠 or ↔️. It covers BIPA (definitions, the photo exclusion versus geometry derived from photos, §15 duties, damages, Rosenbach, Tims, Cothron, the 2024 amendment, and BIPA's lack of a service-provider exemption). It also covers Texas CUBI (commercial-purpose scope, AG-only enforcement, the Meta and Google settlements, the TRAIGA amendment), Washington, Colorado and Virginia/Connecticut-style state laws, GDPR (Ar
algorithmic: Tag every stored object with a data class (PERSONAL_IMAGE, BIOMETRIC_GEOMETRY, BIOMETRIC_TEMPLATE, LIKENESS_ASSET, AGGREGATE_PRIOR) in a project manifest; purge operators act by class.

Make a consent datablock required: consent_id, subject_is_user, jurisdictions, scopes ⊆ {sculpt, texture, publish, commercial, animate, print, cloud, identity_check, train}, signed_at, expires_at, method. detect_landmarks, fit and export refuse to run without it unless subject_is_user; identity_score also needs identity_check; any network call needs cloud.

Retention defaults: cache_ttl_days = 0 (max 30); retention_after_purpose_days = 365; max_days_since_last_interaction = 730; warn 30 days before expiry; purge_biometrics() also deletes .blend1 files and autosaves.

Embeddings stay in RAM, are compared 1:1 only against the same project's reference photos, and are freed at once. Persist only cosine scores and the model hash. No 1:N search, gallery import or 'find this face' feature.
network_enabled = False by default, with per-call confirmation that names the host, data classes and consent scope. A CI test monkeypatches socket.socket.connect to raise during a full pipeline run.
No telemetry. Error reports strip images, arrays and file paths. The audit log is append-only JSONL (event, time, data class, SHA-256), never pixels or coordinates.

On import, an EXIF whitelist keeps FocalLength, FocalLengthIn35mmFilm, Make/Model, dimensions and Orientation in a sidecar for the camera solver, and drops GPS, serial numbers, owner names, MakerNote and thumbnails.

Bundle only aggregate shape priors whose dataset licence allows redistribution, and record each prior's licence and consent basis. Never ship per-person scans or templates. Offer no 'anonymise' toggle, because smoothing a likeness does not de-identify it.
takeaways: Photographs are excluded from BIPA's definition, but face geometry derived from photos has been treated as a 'scan of face geometry' (Rivera v. Google, the Facebook Tag Suggestions cases). A photo-to-3D pipeline therefore produces likely biometric identifiers.

Whether an identification-capable likeness mesh that is never used for recognition is regulated is contested. Under BIPA, Zellmer requires capability to identify, while some Illinois courts only ask whether geometry was scanned. Under GDPR, data is biometric by capability and Art. 9 applies by purpose. A high-likeness head is identifying by design, so treat it as biometric.
Recognition embeddings (ArcFace-style) are textbook biometric templates and the highest-risk artifact. Compute them in RAM, compare 1:1 only, and never persist them.

Local processing with no telemetry largely keeps the developer out of BIPA collection and GDPR processing. Every duty then falls on the artist or studio: written release, purpose, retention schedule and disclosure limits. BIPA's 'private entity' includes individuals and has no processor exemption.

Any cloud step (Mesh to MetaHuman, hosted generators, render farms, crash reports with image crops) is a disclosure that needs named consent. A developer-run backend makes the developer a collector or processor.
A BIPA-grade written release (specific purpose, artifacts, scopes, end date, withdrawal, guardian for minors) also meets CUBI and most GDPR explicit-consent tests. It is the cheapest risk control.

One retention default can satisfy the main laws: delete 365 days after the purpose ends (CUBI), with a hard cap of 730 days since last interaction (Colorado 24 months, inside BIPA's 3 years). Caches are session-only.
gaps: No harvest file or earlier draft existed. The note has no cited URLs, so every fact is author knowledge (🧠) or contested (↔️) until the verification pass.
The case-law status of 3D likeness meshes and virtual try-on geometry under BIPA is unresolved, and post-2024 rulings were not checked.
Retroactivity of BIPA's 2024 amendment, and whether the Seventh Circuit has ruled on it, is unknown.
The EU AI Act Art. 50 application date and Digital Omnibus outcome as of November 2026 are unverified.
The exact wording of TRAIGA's CUBI amendments and of Colorado's HB 24-1130 retention clauses is unverified.
The CPI-adjusted CCPA amounts for 2025 and the 2027 adjustment are unverified.
It is unknown what iris-texture resolution would count as an 'iris scan', or whether 3DMM coefficient vectors count as 'templates'.
Licence terms of common shape priors (FLAME, BFM) are noted only as typically non-commercial and need checking.
Non-US/EU regimes (Japan APPI, China PIPL and its 2025 facial-recognition measures, Brazil LGPD, Quebec, Australia) are covered in a single bullet.

blender-extensions-packaging.title: Packaging as a Blender extension
blender-extensions-packaging.summary: Wrote the extensions packaging note and its sources and data JSON files. Neither input existed: the harvest (/home/user/minedesign/research/_raw/harvests/blender-extensions-packaging.json) and the earlier draft were both missing. The core packaging knowledge is therefore expert knowledge (🧠): the manifest schema (blender_manifest.toml), permissions, wheels and platform tags, the CLI flags and the extensions.blender.org rules. The 23 cited URLs come from sibling harvests in the same library, marked 'via <harvest>' as earlier notes in the library do; a script check confirmed every URL appears in
algorithmic: Engine dependency contract: imports limited to numpy, math, json and tomllib; never imports bpy or its parent package; relative imports only, so the same code runs as bl_ext.<repo>.<id>.engine and under plain-CPython pytest.

Precision boundary: solve in float64 and convert to float32 only at foreach_set. Golden comparisons use rtol=1e-5, never bit-exact, because the 5.0 mathutils buffer path is float32 and BLAS differs across platforms.

A compat.py probe runs once at register() and returns {blender, python_tag, numpy, online_access, platform, has_onnxruntime}. A backend that fails the probe is disabled with a UI message, not a traceback.

Model registry stored as data: {name, url, sha256, bytes, licence, commercial_ok, needs_network}. Download only with online_access on and user confirmation, verify the hash before loading, refuse commercial_ok=false by default, and store files under extension_path_user.
Suggested budgets: core zip ≤5 MB (≤25 MB with a template mesh), optional platform zips ≤50 MB, register() <100 ms with lazy heavy imports.

Synthetic regression suite: s≈0.14 m, 3–5 cameras at 0.5–1.5 m, 50–85 mm-equivalent lenses, 68–100 landmarks. Noiseless runs need reprojection RMS <1e-6 px and vertex RMS <1e-6·s. With σ=1 px noise, expected RMS ≈ σ·sqrt(1−p/n); fail above 1.2σ. Seed with default_rng(seed).
Stamp every fit sidecar with {addon_version read via tomllib from blender_manifest.toml, blender, python, numpy, seed, solver_config}.
Licence as a solver constraint: a prior, template or table with commercial_ok=false can never be the default; fitting must succeed with the CC0 template alone.
takeaways: Ship the photo→head tool as a GPL-3.0-or-later Blender extension; every face extension in the library whose licence was captured (MPFB2, Face Shape Key Rig, CaptureForge) is GPL.

Keep the core free of compiled wheels: Blender bundles NumPy, so a float64 pure-NumPy engine needs no wheels, works on every platform from one zip and avoids cp311-vs-5.x Python ABI breakage. Never bundle numpy.

Never use a hard-coded package name: an installed extension imports as bl_ext.<repo>.<id>. Use __package__ and relative imports, never rename the id, and keep caches and models in bpy.utils.extension_path_user, not in the extension folder.

Permissions disclose but do not sandbox. Declare only 'files' for the core build, add 'network' only for an opt-in model downloader that checks bpy.app.online_access, and add 'camera' only for webcam capture. Face photos are biometric data: process them offline with no telemetry, and record consent in the sidecar.

Non-commercial models (FLAME, InsightFace weights, CC BY-NC trackers) are GPL-incompatible. Load them from a path the user supplies; never bundle them. Porting fSpy-style GPL code makes the engine GPL.

Headless CI must pass --python-exit-code 1, otherwise exceptions exit 0. Under -b there is no event loop, no 3D View and no GPU drawing, so the solve path must use only bpy.data, bmesh and foreach_get/set.
Test on 4.5 LTS (to Jul 2027), 5.2 LTS (to Jul 2028) and 5.3, and set blender_version_min to the oldest version CI actually tests.
gaps: The topic's own harvest and the earlier draft were both missing, so the manifest schema, the extensions.blender.org rules, wheel installation behaviour and the CLI flags are all unverified expert knowledge.
Bundled Python and NumPy versions for Blender 5.1–5.3 are unconfirmed, which decides cp311 vs cp313 for any wheel.
Unknown: whether Blender skips wheels with mismatched tags, and which version wins when two extensions bundle the same package.
The licences extensions.blender.org accepts for add-on code beyond GPL-3.0-or-later (MIT, BSD, GPL-2.0-or-later, multiple SPDX entries) are unverified.
The upload size limit on extensions.blender.org and the required listing media (icon and featured-image sizes) are unknown.
Unclear whether a listed extension may download model weights with non-free terms at runtime once the user consents.
Whether the manifest accepts windows-arm64 or linux-arm64, and whether 5.0 dropped Intel Mac builds, is unconfirmed.
The wheel sizes in Table 4 are order-of-magnitude recollections, not checked against current PyPI listings.

blender-face-addons.title: Blender add-ons for heads and faces
blender-face-addons.summary:
I rewrote the Blender face add-ons note (about 2,740 words of body text, not counting the source list). It keeps all 16 sourced citations and the earlier verification results: 468 landmarks is ✅, MPFB2 GPL-3.0-or-later is ✅, and the MPFB asset licence stays ↔️. The old ⚠️ badges are now 📄 and the outdated search-budget notes are gone. I added expert-knowledge (🧠) coverage of tools the draft had no evidence for:
- MediaPipe Face Landmarker blendshapes, the iris landmark indices, what the z coordinate means, and the canonical model.
- BlendArMocap.
- Faceit's workflow and why its bone-heat bindi
algorithmic: Input schema: LandmarkSet{scheme in {mp468, mp478}, xy_px[N], z_rel[N], image_wh, mirrored, exif_rotation}. Branch on N, and treat indices 468-477 as optional iris observations.

Each landmark class gets its own σ, as a fraction of IOD: anchors 1.5%, eyelid and lip contours 2.5% (sliding), face oval 4% as silhouette residuals re-associated every iteration, iris centre 1%. Use a Huber loss with δ = 2σ and drop points beyond 4σ after the first solve.
MediaPipe z weight: 0 with two or more views, at most 0.1·w_xy with one view.
Scale priors: horizontal iris diameter 11.7 ± 0.5 mm and IPD 63 ± 3.5 mm. A measured IPD or a ruler in frame overrides them with σ ≈ 1 mm. Never take scale from MediaPipe's canonical model.
Camera: focal-length prior from EXIF, f_px = f35·√(W²+H²)/43.27. Principal point fixed at the image centre, k1 only for wide lenses.

Shape priors: MPFB local targets N(0, 0.5²) with a hard box on [-1,1]. Macros are boxed to [0,1] and, when the user supplies values, pulled toward them with σ 0.15. FLAME β ~ N(0,1) over the first 50-100 components. The expression basis to absorb has σ ≈ 0.3 and is discarded after fitting.

Residual per-vertex warp after the parametric fit: Laplacian/ARAP regularisation annealed 10→1, offsets capped near 5 mm unless several views agree, and a soft symmetry prior with σ of 1-2 mm instead of hard mirroring.

Correspondence tables (landmark to vertex or barycentric point) are versioned by base mesh and version (MPFB2 2.0.18 hm08). Check the vertex count on load, and assert vertex count and order before every write-back.
Licence as data: each asset and prior carries {licence, attribution, commercial_ok}, and export refuses unknown or non-commercial items (FLAME by default).
Outputs: neutral identity mesh, optional ARKit-52-named shape keys, an MPFB .target, and OBJ with a stable vertex order.

Packaging: a Blender extension with SPDX:GPL-3.0-or-later and blender_version_min 4.2.0. MediaPipe runs out of process or as an optional wheel. Declare the camera permission only for webcam capture, and copy Blender 5.0 mathutils buffers explicitly into float64 numpy arrays.
takeaways: No Blender add-on in this evidence set fits one person's identity to photos with open code, open data and a licence that allows commercial use. That gap is what this project's numpy fitter is for.

MPFB2 is the best documented open base: its code is GPL-3.0-or-later (✅) and its assets are CC0 or CC-BY (↔️). Fit on its frozen hm08 topology and save the result as one neutral shape key or an MPFB .target via MakeTarget.

MediaPipe outputs 468 landmarks (✅), or 478 with refinement (📄). Its z is relative and pulled toward the average face, so take metric scale from multiple views plus iris and IPD priors, not from MediaPipe.

The expression layer is converging on ARKit 52. Faceit generates and bakes the shapes, CaptureForge converts a posed rig to them, and Face Shape Key Rig only drives keys that already exist. Output ARKit-named keys so all three can use them.

Version support conflicts: Faceit states 3.0 to 5.2, Face Shape Key Rig needs 5.2 or newer, MPFB2 needs 4.2 or newer. Only Blender 5.2 LTS satisfies all three, so test on 4.5 LTS, 5.2 LTS and the current 5.x.

Licences that can contaminate output: FLAME and the Basel Face Model are research-only, MetaHuman and Human Generator assets are proprietary, and FaceBuilder runs a closed core under an EULA. Store the licence as data and block export of anything unknown or non-commercial.
Shape keys need identical vertex count and order. Never Remesh, use Dyntopo, Decimate or merge-Symmetrize the delivery mesh, and add Multires only after the identity keys are final.
gaps: MB-Lab, CharMorph, Human Generator, Auto-Rig Pro, the FLAME Blender add-on, BlendArMocap and KeenTools FaceBuilder have no harvested sources. Every fact about them is 🧠: licence, price, maintenance and Blender 5.x status.
No accuracy benchmark (mm error compared with a scan) exists in this library for any Blender add-on's photo-to-head fit, FaceBuilder included.
Not captured for mozi1924/mediapipe-facecap-for-blender: its licence, Blender range, and whether raw landmarks are exposed. MediaPipe model-card usage terms were not captured either.
MPFB2 face target inventory (names and counts), the exact hm08 vertex counts, and MakeHuman's own asset licence files have not been checked against primary sources.
Faceit price and support beyond Blender 5.2, and the Blender range for CaptureForge, are unknown.

blender-python-ml-deps.title: Running MediaPipe / OpenCV / ONNX inside Blender
blender-python-ml-deps.summary: Neither the harvest (a) nor an earlier draft (b) existed for this topic, so I wrote the note from scratch. It cites only URLs that already appear in sibling harvests in this library. All 23 were checked by script against the harvest JSON files. The note covers how add-ons get compiled ML dependencies into Blender's Python. There are three ways to do it: runtime pip into a private --target folder (with --no-deps, --only-binary and PYTHONNOUSERSITE), per-platform wheels in a 4.2+ extension (which go into a shared site-packages directory), and an out-of-process worker. Precedents cited: mozi1924'
algorithmic: Backend contract: detect(rgb_uint8, meta) -> {points[N,2] px with top-left origin and y down, visibility[N], scheme, image_wh, exif_applied, mirrored, backend, backend_version, model_sha256}. Tiers: worker (default), then in-process ONNX Runtime, then imported JSON (always available).

Landmark sigma priors with u = face_width_px/256: inner features 0.6u, iris centre 0.4u, brows 1.0u. Contour points are point-to-curve with sigma_normal 1.5u and sigma_tangent >= 5u. 5-point detectors use 2-3% of inter-ocular distance. MediaPipe z gets weight 0 in multi-view solves.

Gates: request num_faces=2 and require exactly one face at confidence >= 0.6. Flag a view whose inner-point RMS reprojection exceeds 3 sigma (mirroring, EXIF or focal length errors). Flag points where two detectors disagree by more than 3 sigma.
ORT defaults: intra_op_num_threads = max(1, physical_cores-2), inter_op = 1, ORT_ENABLE_ALL, CPUExecutionProvider. MediaPipe: running_mode IMAGE; blendshapes on only for expression neutralisation.
Worker timeouts: 60 s on the first (cold) run, 10 s per image afterwards. Detect at a long side of <= 2048 px and map back with x = (x'+0.5)*s - 0.5.

Feature probes, never version branches: find_spec for each backend, the NumPy major version, the wheel tag from sys.version_info, and bpy.app.online_access. Disable a backend gracefully rather than failing at registration.
Reproducibility record per fit: Blender, Python, NumPy and package versions plus the model SHA-256. Golden tests allow about 0.05 px drift across machines (XNNPACK/MLAS ISA differences).
Packaging matrix: {win-x64, macos-arm64, linux-x64} x {cp311, cp313 if confirmed}. OpenCV abi3 covers every cp tag. Leave out mediapipe where no wheel exists and fall back to the ONNX conversion.
takeaways: Treat Blender's Python as off-limits for heavy ML stacks: keep the fitter pure NumPy in-process. Run the detector in an isolated worker (sys.executable -I with a private deps folder, or a separate venv), which also stops a native MediaPipe/absl crash from killing unsaved sculpt work.

Every compiled wheel must match Blender's CPython tag, the OS/arch and the NumPy ABI. Install with --target, --no-deps, --only-binary=:all: and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, and append (never prepend) the target to sys.path so Blender's NumPy wins.
OpenCV wheels are abi3 and survive a Python bump; onnxruntime and mediapipe are built per Python version. Never install two opencv variants; use opencv-python-headless inside Blender.
MediaPipe Face Mesh weights are available as community ONNX conversions, so onnxruntime plus NumPy can replace the whole mediapipe dependency tree (150-400 MB, protobuf pins, sometimes jax).

CPU is ample for still photos (tens of ms per image). Import time, install size, antivirus and wheel availability are the real constraints. Cap ORT at physical cores minus 2 so it doesn't fight Blender's TBB pool.
Landmark precision is bounded by the landmarker's 256-pixel crop: one model pixel is about face width / 256 image pixels, so sigma priors should scale with face size, not image size.
Feed the detector correctly: bake EXIF rotation, un-mirror selfies (L/R swaps), convert BGR to RGB, use 8-bit sRGB, flip bpy pixel rows, and map downscaled coordinates back with the half-pixel rule.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic. Every URL comes from sibling harvests, and nearly all install, packaging and OS-pitfall knowledge is expert knowledge (63 🧠).
The CPython and NumPy versions bundled in Blender 5.x are unconfirmed (3.11 vs 3.13; NumPy 1.26 vs 2.x).
The exact wording of the extensions.blender.org rules on runtime installs and downloads, and the upload size cap, were not captured.
Whether wheels in the shared extension site-packages are deduplicated or resolved by version when two extensions bundle the same package was not checked.
Current mediapipe wheel coverage (cp313, NumPy 2, win-arm64, linux-aarch64) and whether mp.solutions still exists are unknown.
No measured CPU benchmarks inside Blender: all latency, import-time and size figures are expert ranges, apart from 3DDFA_V2's 15 ms and Depth Anything V2's 60 ms on unstated hardware.
The licence terms of the MediaPipe Face Landmarker model card and of the community ONNX conversion (yakhyo) were not captured.

blender-sculpt-features-5x.title: Blender sculpt mode feature set (4.x-5.x)
blender-sculpt-features-5x.summary: Neither a harvest file nor an earlier draft existed for this topic, so the note at /home/user/minedesign/research/blender/blender-sculpt-features-5x.md (about 2,790 words) rests almost entirely on expert knowledge. It covers the sculpt toolset that keeps topology intact: masks, face sets, auto-masking, Expand, the mesh, cloth and mask filters, gesture and trim tools, the Pose, Elastic and Boundary deformers, and Multires. It also covers the three tools that rebuild topology (Dyntopo, voxel remesh and QuadriFlow) and why they must stay off the delivery mesh. The biggest change since 4.0 is that
algorithmic: Feature probes instead of version checks: hasattr(bpy.ops.brush,'asset_activate'); 'sculpt_brush_type' in Brush.bl_rna.properties; check that the .sculpt_mask/.sculpt_face_set attributes exist after a test fill; check that sculpt.mesh_filter runs without a modal event.

Face-set schema: fixed integer region IDs (1 = default skin, about 15–25 anatomical regions) written to .sculpt_face_set (FACE, INT) in OBJECT mode, with a fixed face_sets_color_seed for reproducible colours.

Mask as constraint: per-vertex weight on data and landmark terms = (1 − m), plus a pin term m·||x − x_artist||²/σ_pin² with σ_pin ≈ 0.1–0.3 mm; feather engine-written masks with a Gaussian σ ≈ 1.5–2.5 mm (2–4 edge rings).
Smoothing prior equivalent to Relax/Surface Smooth: HC or cotangent Laplacian with σ_lap ≈ 0.05–0.1 × local mean edge length, excluding open boundaries (eye openings, mouth slit).
Soft symmetry prior via a stored mirror map: σ_sym ≈ 1–2 mm on the lateral face, ≈0.5 mm along the upper-face midline; never hard-mirror.
Resolution defaults: fit on a 5k–25k-vertex base (edges ≈2–4 mm) and hand the artist Multires L2–L4. Faces = base·4^L and edge = base_edge/2^L.

Multires write path: subdivide a copy of the base with identical settings, foreach_set the fitted coordinates, then object.multires_reshape with the copy as source, and verify correspondence afterwards.

Mode discipline: switch to OBJECT mode before foreach_set (mesh or shape-key data), call mesh.update(), restore the mode, and wrap everything in one REGISTER/UNDO operator. Python writes made in SCULPT mode are overwritten.
Use mathutils.bvhtree/kdtree for closest-point and ray queries (SciPy is not bundled), and cast to float64 because of 5.0's float32 buffer views.
takeaways: Since 4.3, brushes are assets (Essentials library plus asset shelf). Scripts must activate them with bpy.ops.brush.asset_activate and detect the feature with a probe; pre-4.3 brush scripts, keymaps and tutorials do not carry over.

Keep the delivery topology fixed. The fit goes into a 'likeness' shape key and artist edits into an 'artist' key; Dyntopo, remesh, Decimate and merge-Symmetrize are banned on the delivery mesh, and Multires is added only after identity is final.

Real scale breaks defaults: a 0.1 voxel size wipes out a head. Use 1–2 mm for block-out and 0.3–0.5 mm for detail, a 1 mm viewport clip start, and scene-unit brush radii (20–40 mm grab, 3–8 mm detail).

Face sets (per-face integers) and masks (per-vertex 0–1, where 1 means protected) are the natural interface between the engine and the artist. Write anatomical region IDs and read masks back as fit weights.
Turn off 'Lock Camera to View' when sculpting through solved cameras, or the first orbit moves the solved camera; check every silhouette fix in every view.
Mirror only for block-out. Natural asymmetry (~0.8 mm RMS overall, 2–4 mm noticeable) carries likeness, so use a soft symmetry prior, never hard mirroring.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic: every sculpt-feature fact is expert knowledge (🧠), and only release-timeline and mathutils facts are cited, from sibling harvests.
The sculpt changes in Blender 5.0, 5.1, 5.2 LTS and 5.3 are entirely unestablished (Plane brush timing, new brushes and filters, API changes).
Exact attribute names (.sculpt_mask from ≈4.1, .sculpt_face_set) and the brush.asset_activate identifier format need confirming per version.
Version attributions for 4.2 (polyline and line gestures, random mask, grow/shrink visibility) and 4.4–4.5 items are moderate to low confidence.
Hotkeys, especially per-brush keys after the 4.3 asset remap, and the asset-shelf popup key are unverified.
The size of the 4.x sculpt refactor speed-ups and the practical polygon budgets are hardware-dependent estimates, not benchmarks.
It is unknown whether extensions can register asset libraries (needed to ship brush presets cleanly) and whether Python can access multires displacement in 5.x.

blender-version-status-2026.title: Blender release status and roadmap as of late 2026
blender-version-status-2026.summary:
I rewrote the Blender release-status note. It now runs about 2,620 words before the source list, follows the required structure, and keeps all 13 citations from the earlier draft.

**Release status as of Nov 2026.** Blender ships on two tracks.
- 5.3 is the current feature release, dated 10 Nov 2026. It is now marked ✅ because the developer-docs index agrees with two manual pages from other harvests that are titled "Blender 5.3 Manual"; all three are Blender's own pages.
- 5.2 LTS came out on 14 Jul 2026 and is supported to Jul 2028. Two third-party add-ons that list 5.2 compatibility confirm
algorithmic: Support policy: manifest blender_version_min '4.2.0' with a runtime warning below 4.5; CI on 4.5 LTS, 5.2 LTS, the latest feature release and the daily alpha during each beta.
Precision boundary: foreach_get into a float32 buffer of matching dtype, convert to float64 once, solve in float64, write back with astype(float32), foreach_set and mesh.update().

Scale-relative tolerances with s = head scale (bizygomatic about 0.13-0.15 m): round-trip atol 1e-6*s, convergence on relative cost change below 1e-10 or step below 1e-8*s, golden-file rtol 1e-5; no finite differences on float32-round-tripped data.
NumPy 1/2-neutral subset: no np.float_, np.NaN, np.Inf, np.product, np.in1d; explicit dtypes (NEP 50); lstsq(rcond=None); default_rng(seed).
Threading: solve in a worker thread on copied arrays and apply results on the main thread via bpy.app.timers.
Dependencies: pure-NumPy core; detectors run out of process via JSON; any wheels built per platform and per CPython tag; never bundle numpy; gate network access on bpy.app.online_access.

Camera exchange: S = max(W,H) for AUTO sensor fit; f_px = lens*S/sensor; cx = W/2 - shift_x*S; cy = H/2 + shift_y*S; OpenCV camera = Blender camera * diag(1,-1,-1); write cameras with sensor_fit HORIZONTAL.
Record blender/python/numpy/add-on versions, the seed and the solver config with every fit.
takeaways: Two release tracks in Nov 2026: 5.3 is the current feature release (10 Nov 2026, current-release status corroborated by the manual) and 5.2 LTS is supported to Jul 2028; 4.5 LTS runs to Jul 2027, and 4.2 LTS is out of support since Jul 2026.
No source confirms the Python or NumPy bundled with 5.x. Read sys.version_info and numpy.__version__ at runtime and test the core on both Python 3.11 + NumPy 1.26 and Python 3.13 + NumPy 2.x.
Since 5.0, np.asarray(mathutils object) gives a float32, non-contiguous view. Always use np.array(x, dtype=np.float64) and keep the solver in float64.
Probe for features, never branch on version numbers. Avoid bgl and obj['prop'] access, set the EEVEE engine id inside try/except, and activate brushes through the asset system.
For a sculpt-ready likeness, freeze topology while landmark steps run, write the fit as a shape key, add detail with Multires afterwards, and leave Dyntopo/remesh until last.
Photo hygiene matters: bake EXIF orientation into the pixels (Blender ignores it) and handle the scene-wide render resolution when there is one camera per photo, or landmarks shift.
gaps: Bundled Python version for 5.0, 5.1, 5.2 LTS and 5.3 is unconfirmed.
Bundled NumPy version for 5.x, and whether any 5.x moved to NumPy 2.x, is unknown.
The full list of breaking changes from 5.0 to 5.3 is not retrieved; all 5.0 removals except the mathutils change rest on my own knowledge.
Sculpt and modeling content of the 2026 roadmap post and the 5.3 release notes was not extracted.
The version number of the July 2027 LTS and the next roadmap are unknown.
Whether 5.0 dropped Intel Macs, which affects the macos-x64 wheels, is unconfirmed.
Size limits on extensions.blender.org for bundled wheels are unknown.
The exact 5.2.4 release date is contested (10, 16 or 17 Nov 2026).

blenderartists-forum.title: BlenderArtists forum knowledge on faces
blenderartists-forum.summary:
I rewrote the BlenderArtists note. It keeps every sourced fact and all 9 forum URLs from the earlier draft, converts the old ⚠️ marks to the new badges, and drops the notes about the search budget. The forum material itself is qualitative:
- FaceBuilder 2021.1 places pins automatically with neural networks, and the vendor says those pins are not always accurate.
- The "Revamped" thread says focal length and sensor size are estimated for each photo.
- Expressive photos are accepted, but neutral photos fit better.
- Users describe FaceBuilder as paid, with a 30-day trial.
- MetahumanModeler and
algorithmic: Pin trust in two levels, in ViewObs.weights: detector pins get σ ≈ 0.03×IOD for interior points and 0.06-0.08×IOD for contour points, with point-to-curve residuals on the contour. User pins get σ ≈ 1-2 screen pixels converted at the current zoom, with a Huber loss.

Solve one f_px per photo and never optimize sensor size. Initialize from EXIF via focal_px_from_35mm (diagonal convention). Use f_prior_log_sigma 0.05-0.10 when EXIF is present and 0.35 when it is not. Tie photos from the same lens with a log-difference σ of about 0.02. Flag a disagreement of more than 10-15% from EXIF or from same-lens photos.

Perspective guard: if the solved camera-to-nose distance is under about 0.8 m, warn that the mid-face is inflated by about 12% or more, and down-weight that view's depth-sensitive landmarks or ask for a profile photo.
Absolute scale: default to an interpupillary-distance prior of 63 ± 3.5 mm (1σ), overridden by a measurement the user enters (for example the PD on a glasses prescription).
Mirroring: when EXIF shows a front camera, ask whether the image is mirrored and offer a flip. Keep sigma_sym at about 2 mm (1.5-3 mm) and never force symmetry.

Identity vs expression: one identity vector for the whole photo set, plus one expression vector per photo with a prior centred on zero. Photos flagged neutral get zero expression. Drop lip landmarks from open-mouth photos and lid landmarks from squinting photos.
Depth confidence: compute the posterior covariance from the LM solver's JᵀJ and write the per-vertex depth σ to a Blender color attribute, so the user can see which areas come mostly from the prior.

Template transfer: RBFWarp followed by laplacian_deform onto the target topology, with a versioned landmark-to-vertex correspondence table for each base mesh. Attach licence metadata ({licence, commercial_ok}) to every prior and block FLAME-derived exports until its licence is verified.
Automated critique output: per-landmark reprojection error as a percentage of IOD, per-view RMSE, and an overlay render through each solved camera.
takeaways: The vendor itself says FaceBuilder's neural auto-pins are only a draft. Any photo-fitting tool needs a review-and-fix pin loop, with re-solving after every edit [1].
Expressive photos are accepted, but neutral photos give a better identity fit. Separate identity from per-photo expression, and fix expression at zero for photos marked neutral [1][2].

Perspective is set by camera distance, not focal length. The nose-tip plane appears about 1.20× larger than the ear plane at 0.5 m, about 1.10× at 1 m and about 1.05× at 2 m, so for likeness photos shoot from 1.5-3 m.

Orthographic front and side image planes, the method BA teaches most often, are geometrically wrong for close photos. Use camera-matched Background Images with render resolution equal to the photo's pixel size, sensor_fit set to HORIZONTAL, and a focal length converted from EXIF using the diagonal convention.

BA likeness critiques only mean something through a matched camera. Overlay the render on the photo at 50% or with a Difference blend, compare profile silhouettes, and flip and blur the images. The most common errors are a short cranium, wrong eye spacing or size, lids without thickness, flat lips, narrow alae, low ears and too much symmetry.
A single photo gives no depth measurement. Depth from single-photo tools (MetahumanModeler, AutoFace) is prior-driven and unmeasured, so it is suitable for blocking only [5][6].
gaps: None of the harvested BA threads gives accuracy figures (millimetre error, reprojection error) for FaceBuilder, AutoFace or MetahumanModeler.

MPFB2/MakeHuman likeness threads, discussion of FLAME add-ons, Focused Critique likeness threads and shared bpy scripts (camera matching, MediaPipe or dlib landmark import, shape-key fitting) were never harvested.
The answers in the beginner threads [7][8][9] were not retrieved, only their titles.
Thread posting dates are estimated from Discourse topic IDs, except for [1].
FaceBuilder's current price, licence and Blender 5.x support were not checked against a primary source.
Every number in the tables (anthropometric ranges, model vertex counts, solver defaults) is expert knowledge or derived geometry, not taken from sources in this library.

bpy-mesh-api.title: Blender Python API for procedural heads
bpy-mesh-api.summary:
I wrote the bpy-mesh-api note at /home/user/minedesign/research/blender/bpy-mesh-api.md (about 2,500 words of prose plus 4 tables and a code sketch). I also wrote /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/bpy-mesh-api.json, which has no URL sources and 12 references named in words, and /home/user/minedesign/research/data/bpy-mesh-api.json with 6 tables.

Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed. As a result, every claim carries the 🧠 or ↔️ badge and no URLs are cited. I kept the note consistent with the sibling notes blender-version-status-2026.md and reference-camera-setup.md and re
algorithmic: Only one bridge module imports bpy; the engine exchanges float64 arrays and never sees an ID.

Add a CSR face representation to the engine (offsets plus corner_verts as int32) that maps one-to-one onto loop_start and loop vertex_index, and drop the Python loops in Mesh.triangles() and Mesh.edges().
