Fix face3d/geometry/camera.py::to_blender_camera: under sensor_fit HORIZONTAL, divide shift by W, not max(W,H). Add a test comparing Camera.project with Blender's calc_matrix_camera to within 0.01 px for landscape and portrait, centred and shifted.
Keep mesh data in the engine frame. Put a single R_x(+90°) axis conversion on a parent empty over the head and all cameras, so foreach round trips are exact.
The bridge refuses to write a key when len(V) != len(me.vertices) or the object is in edit mode. Coordinate round-trip tolerance is 1e-6·s and mirror-map tolerance 1e-5·s, with s ≈ 0.14 m.
Painted vertex-group weights become per-vertex data-term confidence in [0,1] and scale the Laplacian sigma by 1/w² inside masked regions.
Main-thread budget: timer interval 0.05-0.1 s and ≤10-20 ms of work per tick; live-preview the key every LM iteration while V ≤ 1e5.
Convert mathutils values with np.array(v, dtype=np.float64), never np.asarray, because of the 5.0 float32 view.
takeaways: Bulk I/O only goes through foreach_get/foreach_set with contiguous float32 (coordinates) or int32 (indices) NumPy buffers. A mismatched dtype silently takes a slow path, so assert dtype and contiguity in the bridge.
Write each fit as a shape key on a template whose topology never changes, with region keys masked by vertex groups. Keys hold absolute positions, and once keys exist the Basis key is authoritative.
bmesh is for topology edits, not coordinate throughput. Vertex-group weights have no foreach path, so quantise weights to 256 levels or use the bmesh deform layer.
Render resolution is per scene and camera shift is in units of the fitted dimension (W under HORIZONTAL). Check the engine projection against Blender's calc_matrix_camera to within 0.01 px.
bpy is not thread-safe. Solve in a worker thread or a subprocess (sys.executable), apply results from bpy.app.timers or a modal timer, and re-fetch IDs by name because undo invalidates references.
Call bpy.ops only through context.temp_override (override dicts were removed in 4.0). The data-API equivalent of applying modifiers is evaluated_get plus new_from_object.
Python is 3.11 in Blender 4.1-4.5; Python and NumPy in 5.x are unconfirmed, so probe at runtime and record bpy.app.version_string, sys.version and numpy.__version__ with every fit.
gaps: No harvest file and no earlier draft existed for this topic, so the note has no URL-sourced or verified facts and every claim needs web verification.
The timing table holds planning estimates, not benchmarks. Measure foreach, from_pydata, bmesh and img.pixels timings on the target Blender versions.
Internal attribute names for the sculpt mask and face sets in 5.x (.sculpt_mask, .sculpt_face_set) are moderate confidence.
Unknown whether 5.x adds foreach or attribute access to vertex-group weights, or any Python write path to multires displacement beyond multires_reshape.
Unknown whether the 5.x image loader honours EXIF orientation, and whether official PyPI bpy wheels exist for 5.2 LTS and 5.3 and which CPython they need.
Default CameraBackgroundImage.frame_method, and the exact version in which loop_total became read-only, are unverified.

camera-perspective-distortion.title: Focal length, subject distance and perspective distortion
camera-perspective-distortion.summary:
Wrote the camera-perspective-distortion note (about 2,800 words; 18 linked sources), plus a sources JSON and a data JSON with 13 tables. Neither the topic harvest nor an earlier draft existed. The cited URLs were therefore reused from sibling harvests: camera-pose-solving, reference-camera-setup, multi-view-fitting, portrait-lighting-compare, blenderartists-forum and facial-proportions-canons. The numbers match the companion notes camera-pose-solving.md and reference-camera-setup.md (same landmark depths and the same ~12% geometric selfie effect).

What the note covers:
- **Distance, not the l
algorithmic: Exact reparameterisation per photo: u = c + s·(x + t_xy)/(1 + ρ·ẑ), with s = f/z0 (px/mm) and ρ = 1/z0. Weak perspective is ρ = 0: start there, then free ρ; f = s/ρ; bound ρ to 0.1–5 m^-1.

log f priors: EXIF f35 on an uncropped original, sigma 0.04; EXIF with unknown crop, sigma 0.35. Without EXIF use hypotheses {13, 24, 26, 35, 50, 77, 85, 120, 135, 200} mm with sigma 0.5–0.7; add 13, 26, 77 and 120 to the engine's current DEFAULT_F35_HYPOTHESES.

log z priors when f is unknown: front-camera selfie 0.35 m (sigma 0.3), handheld rear main 0.8 m (sigma 0.4), tele 2 m (sigma 0.4), tape-measured ±5 cm. Scale: IPD 63 ± 3.5–4 mm or iris 11.7 ± 0.5 mm.

Report perspective strength P = 100 mm/z (>0.1 strong, <0.03 near-affine) and the posterior sigma of ρ from the Gauss-Newton Hessian. If sigma_ρ > 0.5ρ, label 'distance/focal from prior' and hold depth-related shape modes at their prior or other-view values so shape cannot absorb perspective.
In single-view mode, expose the ρ/depth-mode family as a dolly-zoom slider with its cost curve (the Bas & Smith ambiguity).
Group intrinsics by (Make, Model, LensModel, f35, W, H, still/video) and share log f within a group (sigma 0.02). Never average distance across photos.
Store crop offsets so the original principal point survives. For weak-perspective initialisation, virtually rotate the face-centre ray onto the optical axis to remove the ≈θ pose bias.

Reject or flag: ultrawide LensModel or f35 < 20 mm; face centre more than ~25° off-axis in phone images (possible face-warp correction); front camera, which triggers the mirror test and the selfie prior. Never trust distance from landmark ratios when P < 0.05.
Undistort calibrated images before PnP. For phone JPEG/HEIC, fix k1 and k2 at 0.
Export a Blender camera at the solved distance with lens = f_px·36/W and HORIZONTAL fit. Offer an ORTHO camera (ortho_scale = W/s) only when P < 0.03.
Optional feature: re-render the fitted head with the projected photo 'as if from distance D', giving the artist distance-matched references.
Synthetic test sweep: z 0.25–5 m, f35 13–200 mm. Check that recovered ρ and f are right, that solves converge from ρ = 0, and that shape error stays flat as P grows.
takeaways: Facial perspective depends only on camera distance: points Δ apart in depth image at a 1+Δ/z scale ratio. A longer lens just lets you stand back at the same framing.

At 0.25–0.4 m the nose-to-face-width ratio is inflated 12–19% and the nose tip images 25–40% larger than the ear plane. At 1.5–3 m these fall to 2–3% and 3–7%. Ward et al.'s clinical model reports ~30% (contested).

Between adults the nose-to-face ratio varies ~9–11%, as much as the whole perspective change from 0.5 m to infinity. One photo cannot separate a wide nose from a close camera, so focal length or distance must come from EXIF, calibration, a tape measure or other views.
Image scale gives only f/z (from IPD or iris). Distance needs either the person's depth or a known focal length; the iris gives z only when f is known.

Reference capture: 1.5–3 m, 85–135 mm-equivalent or a phone 3–5x tele, face within 10–15° of the frame centre, one lens locked. Front-camera and ultrawide shots are perspective evidence, not proportion references.

In Blender, judge likeness only through a camera rebuilt at the solved distance. Ortho-trace only photos taken from 3 m or more, and raise viewport focal length to about 100–170 mm when judging proportions.
Weak perspective falls below landmark noise only beyond ~1 m for interior points and ~2–3 m for ears and contour. Monocular regressors that assume it bake selfie distortion into shape.
EXIF focal length is the nominal value at infinity focus. Focusing, integer rounding, tolerance and the diagonal-vs-width convention each add 1–11% uncertainty.
gaps: No topic harvest or earlier draft existed. Every study figure (Ward 30%/29%, Noyes & Jenkins distances, Třebický design) is from memory and not checked against the primary papers.
The identity of source [5] (PMC3440305) is unresolved: the snippet text matches Třebický 2016, but the ID suggests about 2012, possibly Bryan et al.
Whether EXIF FocalLengthIn35mmFilm uses the diagonal or the width, and how each phone vendor updates it under digital zoom and aspect crops, is unconfirmed and time-sensitive.
The Blender viewport 2x zoom factor is recalled from source code, not verified for Blender 5.x.
How common face-aware wide-angle warps are on phones, and whether they apply to main cameras, has not been researched.
No real-face (as opposed to synthetic) measurements were found for focal-length or distance accuracy from landmarks.
The ICAO/ISO ID-photo distance and the ISO 517 focal tolerance are recalled, not sourced.

The anthropometric CVs for alar and bizygomatic width used in the identity-vs-distance argument (~8–10% and ~4%) are approximate and should be checked against Farkas norms in the anthropometric-norms note.

camera-pose-solving.title: Solving camera pose and intrinsics from face images
algorithmic: Focal-length prior in log space: σ_log 0.04–0.06 with EXIF 35 mm-equivalent (uncropped), 0.01–0.02 when calibrated, 0.05–0.10 from vanishing points, and 0.5–0.7 centred on 50 mm-equivalent when nothing is known. Starting hypotheses: {13, 24, 35, 50, 85, 135, 200} mm.
Expose f_prior_log_sigma in PhotoLandmarks and reconstruct_landmarks; it is currently fixed at a weak 0.35 even with EXIF.
Add intrinsics groups so photos from the same camera and zoom share one focal length (keyed on EXIF Make/Model/FocalLength). With per-view focal and no prior, focal diverged at 1–2 m in simulation.
Fix the principal point at the image centre and set skew to 0 and pixel aspect to 1. Keep k1 and k2 at 0 for phone main-camera JPEG/HEIC. Free k1 (σ ≈ 0.1) only for ultrawide lenses or webcams.

Make landmark noise relative to face size: σ_px = 0.025·IOD_px for detector landmarks, 0.01·IOD_px for hand-placed pins, 3× for contour points. Set the Huber threshold at 2.5·σ_px instead of a fixed 3 px.

Global scale prior (pick one): population interpupillary distance 63 ± 3.5–4 mm; a measured interpupillary distance ± 0.5–1 mm; or iris diameter 11.7 ± 0.5 mm. Otherwise label the result 'proportions only'.

Observability report: from the optimiser's Hessian, compute the uncertainty of log focal length, camera distance and pitch with all other parameters marginalised out (Schur complement). If the focal uncertainty is still more than 0.8× its prior, flag 'focal not observable'. Also show the cost over a sweep of focal values.

Handle twin and mirror solutions: restart PnP from pitch-flipped and yaw-mirrored starting poses and keep the best one with all points in front of the camera. Solve the horizontally flipped image too, to detect mirrored selfies.

Accept a view when reprojection RMSE is ≤ 2–3% of interocular distance (detector) or ≤ 1% (manual); reject it above 3%. Give each view its own expression coefficients with a strong zero-mean prior, so expression changes are not absorbed as pose error.

Pipeline: landmarks + QA → per-view PnP against the template over focal hypotheses → joint bundle adjustment (shared shape; per-view pose; per-group focal; symmetry and template priors) → template warp using silhouettes → Blender export with a round-trip reprojection test.
For identity alignment, fit a uniform-scale similarity transform (Umeyama with a reflection guard). Never use anisotropic scale, because it absorbs real width-to-height differences.
takeaways: From one photo, the pose is easy to solve but the focal length often is not. A face is only about 10–12 cm deep, so beyond about 1 m, focal length, camera distance and the face's own depth cannot be told apart. The scale (focal length ÷ distance) is well determined; the perspective term (face depth ÷ distance) is tiny.

Facial perspective distortion comes from camera distance, not from the lens itself [5][6] ✅. The nose tip is magnified about 12–17% relative to the cheeks in a typical 26 mm selfie at 35–50 cm, and about 5% with an 85 mm lens at 1.2 m (pinhole arithmetic). The nose-to-ear difference is roughly double that.

In the engine simulations, single-view focal error with an unknown face is about 10–17% at selfie range and unbounded at 2 m. With 5 views over ±60° yaw, the 3D landmarks come out within about 1.2 mm RMSE regardless of focal error; a frontal-only fit gives 2.5–3 mm. So a spread of views matters more than knowing the focal length.

Strategy: with a calibrated camera, shoot close (0.4–0.6 m) because the perspective carries useful depth information. With an unknown camera, shoot from 1–1.5 m or farther at 2–3× tele, take many views, and give focal length a weak prior so it cannot diverge.

Pitch is the worst-determined angle. A 10° pitch error shifts the nose tip about 7 mm and the ear about 19 mm relative to the eyes, which looks exactly like a wrong nose length or ear height on a frontal photo.

Do not type EXIF 35 mm-equivalent focal length directly into Blender's lens field; it is 4–18% off depending on aspect ratio. Use lens = f_px·36/W with sensor fit Horizontal. The 'f = image width' shortcut [3] changes with image orientation (≈35 mm-equivalent landscape, ≈26 mm portrait).

Vanishing points (fSpy) can only supply a focal prior, and only from background architecture: two orthogonal VPs give f in closed form [14]; a wall that faces the camera squarely gives no focal information.

Mirrored front-camera selfies, jawline landmarks that slide with yaw, and hallucinated far-side landmarks are the main silent failure modes. Always check for a mirror flip and use only rigid anchors (canthi, nasion, pronasale, subnasale, alare, tragion).
gaps: No primary source in the library yet for the core focal/depth ambiguity on faces; the Bas & Smith [18] summary is from my knowledge, not the harvest.

No empirical measurements on real faces of focal-length recovery error or pose error from landmark PnP or bundle adjustment. The numbers here come from synthetic engine simulations using illustrative (non-anatomical) landmarks.
The depth offsets used for perspective excess (nose tip to cheek about 60 mm, nose tip to tragion about 110 mm) are my estimates ±15 mm; the anatomy notes in the library have no sourced values.
The perception study [9] (50 mm vs longer) and the Ward 2018 selfie-effect figure (about 30%) are unconfirmed: unknown identity, sample size and population.
How phones record digital zoom and portrait-mode crops in EXIF FocalLengthIn35mmFilm was not researched.
Accuracy of learned single-image camera calibrators (e.g. GeoCalib, Perspective Fields) on close-up faces is unknown.
fSpy's current version, licence and compatibility with Blender 4.x/5.x are unverified.
Combining photos across sessions (ageing, weight change) has no quantitative guidance on how much soft-tissue change to allow across time gaps.

child-growth.title: Craniofacial growth: child and adolescent faces
algorithmic: Make age_months and sex required subject inputs, with optional dental_stage and tanner_stage. Never infer minor status from photos.

Age-conditioned measurement priors: mu_m(age, sex) from 3DFN curves, else Table 1 % × adult norms. Use sigma_m^2 = (CV*mu_m)^2 + (v_m*sigma_age)^2, with CV 0.05 for adults and 0.06–0.08 for children; sigma_age is 0 with a known birthdate, else ≥0.5 y.
Metric scale prior on corneal diameter: N(11.8, 0.5–0.8) mm from age 3; age-interpolated N(10.0–11.3, 0.6) mm under 2 y. Use IPD only as a weak check (sigma ~3 mm).
Model the eyeballs as rigid spheres with an age-based axial length (Table 2, sigma 0.5 mm), excluded from template warps.

Growth-gradient template warp: per-region, per-axis scale factors (template_warp_defaults) blended smoothly about a sella/porion origin. Optionally initialise with cardioidal strain R' = R(1 + k(1 − cos θ)), where k < 0 reads younger.
Regularise toward the age-matched mean shape. With an adult-only 3DMM, add an age direction whose coefficient is bounded by the declared age.

Soft age priors: eye-line fraction sigma 0.03; facial index sigma 0.04; gonial angle sigma ~6° (10° at birth); nasolabial angle sigma 8–10°. Add a dorsal-hump penalty under 11 y and a brow-projection penalty before puberty.
Sex-term weight w_sex = logistic((age − a_PHV)/1.5 y), with a_PHV = 11.5 (F) or 13.5 (M).
Infant symmetry: sigma_sym 3–5 mm for ears and occiput (plagiocephaly), 1–2 mm for midface points.
Down-weight face-recognition identity-embedding losses for children.
Run an EXIF capture-window check: warn beyond the age-specific span and refuse beyond 2× for infants.
Minor-flag safeguards: consent and assent record, local-only by default, retention limit, provenance metadata, and an irreversible block on sexualised or nude pipelines.
takeaways: A child's face is not a scaled adult. The cranium follows the neural growth curve (~90–95 % of adult size by 6–7 y), while the face follows the somatic curve with a pubertal spurt. The face finishes in width first, then depth, then height, and nose projection and the mandible mature last.

The younger the subject, the bigger the cranium relative to the face, the lower the eye line (~0.60–0.70 of vertex–menton in infants vs ~0.48–0.53 in adults), the rounder and more wide-set the eyes, the flatter the nasal bridge, and the more upturned the nose. The chin is soft and the cheeks are fat-driven.
The cornea is adult-sized by ~2–3 y (adult pooled mean 11.84 mm, SD 0.79 [13]), so it, not adult IPD, should set metric scale for children. The globe itself is only ~70–75 % of adult length at birth.

Gonial angle runs from ~160° at birth to ~120° in adults [4] (contested at birth). Masticatory muscle volume rises ~199 % from 0 to 17 y [8]. Chin, jaw angle, brow ridge (frontal sinus) and nose projection are mostly adolescent and male-amplified.
Children change fast, so all photos in a set must come from one short window: ≤1 week for infants under 3 months, ≤1 month for 6–12 months, ≤4 months for ages 3–10.
Most 3D morphable models are adult-trained and adultify children (long face, big nose, defined chin). Regularise toward an age-matched mean, using 3DFN growth curves where possible [1][2].

Reconstructing minors needs guardian consent plus child assent, local processing, limited retention, and hard blocks on sexualised pipelines. Legal specifics (GDPR Art. 8/9, COPPA 2025) still need verification.
gaps: The child-growth harvest file and earlier draft were missing. All 📄 citations reuse sibling-harvest URLs, and no source was opened in full text.

The percent-of-adult table (Table 1), absolute eye metrics by age, eye-line fractions, facial index, and the 3DFN/Farkas maturation ages are expert synthesis. Actual 3DFN growth-curve values have not been extracted.
No sourced sub-adult facial soft-tissue thickness data (e.g. Stephan 2018 sub-adult tallies, Wilkinson 2002), so skull-based child reconstruction has no depth priors.
No sourced data on ancestry differences in child growth (e.g. persistence of epicanthal folds, nasal bridge development) or on secular trends since the Farkas era.
Age coverage and licences of child-capable shape models (LSFM, Liverpool-York Head Model/Headspace, SMIL, AGORA kid model) are unverified.
The legal requirements for minors (GDPR, COPPA 2025 amendments, laws on synthetic sexual imagery) are expert knowledge and time-sensitive.
Timing of facial versus statural peak height velocity, and the gonial angle at birth (160° vs 140–150°), remain contested.

commercial-head-tools.title: Commercial photo-to-head tools
commercial-head-tools.summary: Neither input existed (no harvest at _raw/harvests/commercial-head-tools.json, no earlier draft), so the note was written from expert knowledge. Following library precedent, it cites no URLs and cross-references sibling notes by path: blender/metahuman-cc-bridges.md, blender/blender-face-addons.md, community/blenderartists-forum.md, reconstruction/single-image-regression.md, reconstruction/photogrammetry-heads.md. It covers KeenTools FaceBuilder, Reallusion Headshot 1/2 (and CC5), MetaHuman (Creator, Mesh to MetaHuman, Animator), FaceGen, R3DS/Faceform Wrap, Polywink, Avaturn, and Ready Player
algorithmic: Make pins first-class constraints: Pin{view, xy_px, surface(tri,bary), sigma, source user|auto}. Use sigma 0.75% IOD for user pins and 1.5 / 2.5 / 4% IOD for auto pins (corners / contours / face oval), with Huber delta = 2 sigma. A user pin overrides auto pins on the same feature.

Camera groups share intrinsics. The EXIF focal prior is f_px = f35·√(W²+H²)/43.27 with log-sigma 0.03. Without EXIF, start at 50 mm equivalent with log-sigma 0.5, and solve focal only when at least 2 views or a profile constrain it.

Map a rigidity slider r in [0,1] to lambda_shape = 10^(2r−1), default 1, on N(0,1) PCA coefficients, with a separate expression rigidity. Cap residual per-vertex offsets near 5 mm unless at least 2 views agree.

Treat an imported vendor head as a point-to-plane observation, not as truth. Use sigma 2.5 mm for single-photo tools (4 mm on profile regions), 1–1.5 mm for multi-view pin fits and 0.5 mm for scan plus wrap. Down-weight it once photo constraints exist.
Texture projection: weight each texel by cos(theta)^k with k = 2–4, reject grazing angles above 70–75°, feather seams over 8–16 texels, and keep a per-texel view-index map.
Ship a compare-to-scan harness: 7-landmark Umeyama alignment (NoW-style), per-region RMS (REALY-style) and profile-silhouette error, so users can rank vendor outputs against the add-on.

Export contracts: ARKit-52 names, a 'bridge-ready neutral' in cm for MetaHuman, CC and Daz, and stable vertex order. Never ship vendor topology or indices. Attach {tool, version, processing local|cloud, licence, commercial_ok, consent_scope} to every asset and block exports that fail it.
takeaways: Every commercial photo-to-head tool is a template fitter: a fixed vendor topology inside a learned shape space, driven by 2D landmarks or pins and a camera solve, with photo texture projected on. Likeness is limited by the shape space and by how many views constrain depth.

No vendor publishes mm-level error against ground-truth scans, and no independent benchmark is known. For reference, a scale-optimised mean face scores about 1.5 mm on NoW, so single-photo tools barely beat the average face on depth.

FaceBuilder is the Blender-native multi-view pin fitter: per-view cameras, camera groups, rigidity controls and ARKit-style blendshapes (recalled as 51). Its profile is only as good as the profile photos and pins.
Headshot 2 mesh mode and Mesh to MetaHuman are rig converters, not likeness sources. Both drift toward their template database at the nose, lips, lids and jaw, so audit with a signed-distance map.

R3DS/Faceform Wrap and Polywink sit downstream: Wrap needs a scan and transfers topology; Polywink adds blendshapes or a rig to an existing neutral head. Avaturn and Ready Player Me-class SDKs target real-time avatars, not sculpt-grade heads.
Where processing runs (local vs cloud) differs by tool and must be captured in the consent form. Prices and licences, especially MetaHuman outside Unreal and Ready Player Me's status, are perishable.
gaps: No web harvest and no earlier draft existed for this topic, so no fact carries a URL citation. Every claim is 🧠 or ↔️ pending verification.
Current (2026) prices, tiers and licence text for FaceBuilder, Character Creator 5/Headshot, FaceGen, Wrap/Faceform, Polywink and Avaturn have not been checked.
MetaHuman features after UE 5.7, the exact terms for use outside Unreal, and whether a first-party photo or monocular identity path now exists.
Ready Player Me's status (acquisition and shutdown) and which successors are active in 2026.
No measured mm-level accuracy for any commercial tool. The accuracy-ladder rows for commercial routes are estimates.
Unconfirmed product details: FaceBuilder's blendshape count (51), its UV layout names, its Blender 5.x support, and Polywink's FACS set size.

consent-likeness-law.title: Consent, right of publicity and deepfake law
consent-likeness-law.summary:
Wrote the consent and likeness-law note (about 2,550 words), its sources JSON and its data JSON. Neither input existed: no consent-likeness-law harvest and no earlier draft, and no other harvest covers this law topic. Every claim is therefore 🧠 or ↔️, and no URLs are cited.

The note covers four legal layers:
- **US right of publicity:** California §3344/§3344.1, the transformative-use test, video-game cases where realistic avatars lose and stylised look-alikes win, and false endorsement.
- **Digital-replica and deepfake laws:** the Tennessee ELVIS Act (including liability for tools whose prim
algorithmic: ConsentRecord, stored as a JSON sidecar and a .blend custom property: subject_pseudonym, signer_role (subject/guardian/estate), consent_text_version, signed_at, expires_at, jurisdiction_tags, photo_sha256[], retention_days, revocation_contact, and scopes as bitflags (CAPTURE, RECONSTRUCT, STORE_RAW, RENDER_PRIVATE, PUBLISH_NONCOMMERCIAL, COMMERCIAL, PRINT_3D, RIG_ANIMATE, CLOUD_PROCESSING, AI_TRAINING).
Default-deny gating: camera solve and fit need RECONSTRUCT, expression or ARKit export needs RIG_ANIMATE, commercial export needs COMMERCIAL, and any cloud call needs CLOUD_PROCESSING.

Policy defaults instead of sigmas: self-consent age 18, commercial consent re-confirmed every 12 months, raw-photo deletion reminder 90 days after project close, 3-year hard retention cap (BIPA), identity embeddings in RAM only, AI_TRAINING and CLOUD_PROCESSING off.
Age by attestation, not ML age estimation, which is itself biometric processing and error-prone.

Multi-face guard: if more than one face is detected, the user picks the subject and the others are never fitted or stored. No gallery search or 'who is this' feature, and likeness scoring runs only against the subject's own consented photos.

Export provenance: write likeness.consent_id, likeness.synthetic=true and likeness.scopes into custom properties and glTF extras. Add XMP/IPTC digital-source-type metadata on renders with optional C2PA signing, and turn the visible disclosure overlay on by default for realistic public renders.
A 'Purge subject' operator removes packed images, landmark caches and temp files and writes a hash-only receipt. Revocation scans project .blend files for the consent_id.
Licence guard: tag every component (template, landmark model, regressor, recogniser) with its licence and block COMMERCIAL export when a non-commercial component touched the result.
Never ship named real-person presets or sample data; demo subjects must be synthetic or consented, with releases on file.
takeaways: Consent is necessary but not sufficient. A written, scoped, revocable release from the subject does not cover the photographer's copyright, a tattoo artist's copyright, non-commercial model-weight licences, or disclosure duties for realistic fakes.

Likeness accuracy and legal exposure rise together. US courts protect stylised or composite characters (Kirby, Lohan) but not realistic avatars (Keller, Hart, No Doubt), so a better photo→3D fit weakens the transformative-use defence.

Stylisation is not a safe harbour against publicity claims: White v. Samsung held that evoking a person is enough. Caricature helps more against deception and deepfake laws than against publicity rights.

The tool maker can be liable too. The Tennessee ELVIS Act, and the proposed NO FAKES Act, target technology whose primary purpose is replicating identified individuals, so never ship celebrity or real-person presets or sample data.

Face meshes, landmarks and identity embeddings should be handled as biometric data. Under GDPR Art. 9 that depends on purpose; under BIPA it needs written consent before collection and destruction within 3 years. Keep processing local and embeddings in RAM only.

EU AI Act Art. 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026, and the open-source exemption does not cover it. Classical least-squares fitting is probably outside the AI Act, but neural landmark or regressor steps and published realistic renders may trigger marking and disclosure duties.

Post-mortem rights run from 10 to 100 years depending on the state or country (CA 70, NY 40, IN 100, DE 10), so memorial and historical-figure commissions need estate consent when they are commercial.

Sexual content using a real person's realistic likeness without specific consent is now criminal under US federal law (TAKE IT DOWN, 2025), in most US states, in the UK and in France. The add-on should never facilitate it.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic: every claim is unverified expert knowledge and no URL is cited.

Status as of Nov 2026 is unknown for the NO FAKES Act, the EU Digital Omnibus and Art. 50 code of practice, India's final IT Rules and DPDP phase-in, Denmark's likeness-copyright bill, UK commencement of the offence of creating intimate deepfakes, and the reach of the December 2025 US executive order on state AI laws.

Exact statutory text was not checked: the scope of the ELVIS Act tool-liability clause, NO FAKES damages and licence-term limits, the New York December 2025 synthetic-performer laws, and the SB 942/AB 853 operative date.
The post-mortem term table needs per-state verification; the Washington, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Virginia rows are flagged contested.
There is no case law on whether a 3D face mesh fitted from photos is BIPA 'face geometry' or GDPR biometric data. Treat both as unresolved.
Whether a hand-sculpted or classically fitted 3D likeness counts as an 'AI system' output or a 'deep fake' under the EU AI Act is unresolved.
Marketplace policies for real-person 3D models (Sketchfab, CGTrader, TurboSquid, Etsy, Printables) and vendor terms on uploading faces (MetaHuman, generative-3D services) were not researched.
Canada, Australia, Brazil, South Korea and Japan get little or no coverage.

craniometric-landmarks.title: Hard- and soft-tissue anthropometric landmarks
craniometric-landmarks.summary:
I rewrote the craniometric-landmarks note by merging the earlier draft (21 sources, all marked single-source) with the new harvest (33 sources, about 45 facts). The final list has 42 cited sources. Eleven more harvested sources are unused and kept only in the sources JSON as [43]–[53]. Every URL was checked against the input files, and every citation number resolves to a listed source.

**Definitions.** All brief landmarks are defined, now cross-sourced where possible. Hard tissue: n, g, or, po, zy, go, pog, me and Gn. Soft tissue: n′, prn, sn, ls, sto, li, pg′, gn′, en, ex, ch, al, t, tr, v.
algorithmic: Landmark schema: abbr, aliases, tissue {hard, soft, hair}, side, bookstein_type, variant (go: outer|bisector|tangents; gn: ceph_mid|anthro_lowest; gn′: orient|curve; sto: single|sup|inf; ls: border|prominent; n′: deepest|over_n), kind {vertex, barycentric, extremal(dir, region), constructed(fn), contour(sliding|silhouette)}, visibility gates, sigma_t, sigma_n, source_ids.

Frame first: fit the midsagittal plane from mirrored pairs (en, ex, ch, al, t) with reflection Procrustes and the FH proxy from t and or′. Extremal landmark = argmax ⟨p, d⟩ over a region mask, recomputed per pose update; use a softmax-weighted version (temperature ~1–2 mm) for differentiability.

Silhouette residual for dlib 0–16 and the MediaPipe face oval (when |yaw| > ~20°): distance from the detection to the projected occluding contour along the image normal, sliding freely along the contour.

Suggested sigmas (mm, across/along contour): sharp junctions 1–1.5 / 1–1.5; curvature extremes 1–2 / 2–4 plus R·σθ; flat extremal 1.5–3 / 5–10 or free; 2D jaw 1.5–2.5 / free; brows 3–5 / free; MediaPipe z ≥10 or ignore.

Priors: Gaussian on log-ratios of norm pairs with σ_log ≈ 0.05–0.08, inflated ×1.5–2 by default. Population and sex are explicit parameters. Midline x = 0 with σ 1–2 mm; bilateral mirror residual σ 1.5–3 mm.
Bone from skin = skin landmark − thickness·normal, with thickness σ 1–2 mm at midline thin sites (n, g, pog) and 3–5 mm at lateral sites (go, zy).
Gating: drop en/ex when eye openness fails, drop sto/li when the lips part, and keep depth-critical midline points (prn, sn, pg′, me′, n′) inactive without a profile, ¾ view or depth source.

Axis map from the face3d engine (+x subject's left, +y up, +z forward, mm) to Blender: (x, y, z) → (x, −z, y). The face looks down −Y and the subject's left is +X / .L. Route synthetic.py names (labrale_superius, pogonion, menton, vertex_front) through an alias table.
takeaways: Fix the head frame before placing any extremal landmark (prn, pg′, me′, g′, zy, v, go). A frame tilt of θ slides a point by about R·θ, so 5° moves vertex 7–9 mm and the chin points 1–3 mm. Recompute extremal points after every pose update.
Frankfort horizontal is porion–orbitale on bone. Photos can only approximate it with tragion and soft-tissue orbitale, so treat FH from photos as a proxy.

'Gnathion' is a naming trap: cephalometry puts it midway between pogonion and menton, while Farkas anthropometry uses the lowest chin point (menton). Store a variant field on every landmark and never compare across variants.

The dlib-68 eye corners (36/39/42/45), mouth corners (48/54), nose tip (30), subnasale (33) and lip midlines (51/57/62/66) can be point correspondences. The jaw (0–16) and brows (17–26) are spaced by rule: fit the jaw as a silhouette or sliding contour and give the brows low weight, never treat them as gonion or glabella.

MediaPipe's 478 points are 468 mesh vertices plus 10 iris points. The mesh has no ears, scalp or neck, so tragion, porion, trichion and vertex need manual or profile input. Its z output is not metric depth.
Gonion and orbitale are the least reliable landmarks, and gonion error runs along the mandibular border. Use covariances aligned to the contour, with large along-contour sigma for go′ and zy′.

A single photo has no absolute scale. Check ratios first (for example en–en/ex–ex ≈ 0.36, ch–ch/al–al ≈ 1.5–1.6), then set scale from a caliper measurement, a ruler in the facial plane, or the iris prior (~11.7 mm, unverified).
gaps: The Farkas 1994 numeric norms were not retrieved. Table 2 is recalled knowledge and must be checked against the book or a paper that reproduces it.
The 478→68 index table in the PeizhiYan converter was not read, and all MediaPipe anatomical index candidates are unverified.
The angular offset between the tragion–orbitale line and the porion–orbitale (FH) plane, and the porion-to-tragion distance, are unquantified.
The original Downs (1948) and Steiner (1953) landmark definitions were not retrieved.

Several numbers in the harvest have no attributed source and were not used: the CNN 3D-scan error of 0.83 ± 0.49 mm, gonion 1.06 mm and orbitale 1.39 mm, the PCA RMS of 1.7–1.8 mm, and a structured-light sub-millimetre claim.
The publication year of PubMed 26703056 (Farkas vs stereophotogrammetry) is unclear: the harvest says 2019, but the ID suggests about 2015–16.
No population-specific (non-White) norm tables are sourced. No soft-tissue offsets per landmark (gonion, zygion, orbitale) are sourced in this note; it defers to skull-osteology.md.
No 2025–2026 benchmark for 3D anthropometric landmark detection was found, so 'best method' claims were deliberately avoided.

deformation-fitting-math.title: Math for landmark-driven mesh fitting
deformation-fitting-math.summary: I wrote the note from scratch because there was no earlier draft. It uses the harvest's 23 real URLs and covers: similarity Procrustes (Umeyama/SVD, weighted cases, GPA, asymmetric scale); thin-plate and polyharmonic RBF warps (2D r² ln r, 3D r, and the sign rule for 3D smoothing); cotan Laplacian and biharmonic displacement; ARAP local/global steps; Amberg optimal-step non-rigid ICP; a PCA prior solved as Tikhonov regularisation, with a warning about the average-face pull; robust IRLS losses; and Levenberg–Marquardt / Gauss–Newton for camera and shape, including numerical stability. It has 4
algorithmic: Fix face3d/geometry/rbf.py: use −smoothing·I for the 'biharmonic' (r) and multiquadric kernels, and keep +λ for r³ and Gaussian. Add a test that bending energy (−wᵀKw for r) decreases monotonically as λ rises; the current err_smooth > err_exact test passes on broken output.
Normalise landmarks (centred, RMS radius 1) before RBF and Laplacian solves so λ and weights are scale-free. Use heteroscedastic smoothing (K ∓ αΣ)w + Pa = y with Σ = diag(σᵢ²).
Keep φ = r as the default 3D kernel. Its non-affine part decays ~1/distance; r³'s grows and swings the landmark-free back of the head.
Add a fold check: the analytic Jacobian determinant of the warp at every vertex, flagged below 0.2.
Contour and jaw landmarks: re-select silhouette vertices per iteration (landmark marching) or use point-to-line residuals, with σ ≈ 0.03·d_ip along the normal and ≥0.15·d_ip along the tangent.

LM: use Nielsen's damping update (instead of the fixed ÷3/×4), τ = 1e-3, and QR/lstsq on the stacked whitened system when cond(J) > 1e8. Keep axis-angle left-multiplicative rotation updates and log-focal.

Priors as whitened residual rows: focal log σ 0.05–0.10 with EXIF and 0.35 without; landmark population prior 4–8 mm; symmetry 1.5–2 mm; midline 1–1.5 mm; PCA β ~ N(0,1) with λ annealed from 100× to 1×.
Report per-landmark covariance (JᵀWJ)⁻¹ so the UI can flag poorly constrained depth (nose, chin) and show k_eff to detect a prior-dominated, generic face.
Run Procrustes once without the determinant correction to detect mirrored selfies (det R < 0) before fitting.
Store each fitting stage as a separate Blender shape key on fixed topology so artists can dial the stages back.
takeaways: Coarse-to-fine order: similarity Procrustes, then PCA/Tikhonov, then a regularised RBF warp, then bilaplacian displacement refinement (optionally ARAP), then a silhouette fit. Each stage has a closed-form or sparse-linear numpy core.
Umeyama: R = U·S·Vᵀ with S = diag(1, 1, sign(det U·det V)), s = tr(DS)/σ²_src, t = μ_dst − sRμ_src. Scalar weights keep the closed form; two-sided or anisotropic weights and GPA need iteration.
The 2D TPS kernel is r² ln r, which uses K + λI. The 3D biharmonic kernel is r, which needs K − λI because −r is the CPD kernel. The engine currently uses +λ: a real bug.
Solve the bilaplacian on the displacement (x − x₀), not on positions. Harmonic energy and plain ARAP leave kinks or spikes at point handles.
Non-rigid ICP needs a decreasing stiffness schedule (verified across 3 sources) and is only relevant when a target surface exists. A black-box optimiser has a tiny convergence basin.
A PCA prior with λ = σₙ² pulls weakly observed directions toward the average face. Monitor effective DoF and ‖β‖²/k.
Focal length and distance barely separate from landmarks beyond ~1.5 m (nose-to-ear magnification ratio ≤1.07), so EXIF focal priors are essential. Absolute size needs one metric measurement.
Practical Blender traps: Sensor Fit Auto on portrait photos, mirrored selfies (det R < 0), the Euclidean RBF gluing lips or lids, and jaw contour points treated as fixed vertices.
gaps: The earlier draft did not exist, so no prior verification results could be kept.
The harvest had no retrieved source for LM damping rules, PCA/3DMM regularisation, robust losses or Tikhonov. Those sections are all 🧠.
Umeyama 1991 and Horn 1987 are named but not linked; the closed-form details rest on arXiv 2206.14528 plus knowledge.
There is no quantitative comparison of RBF + Laplacian against NICP and 3DMM pipelines for photo-only face fitting, and none on how prior strength affects likeness.
The exact formulation of the 2025 smooth/higher-order ARAP variant (arXiv 2501.10335) and of 'ARAP Revisited' was not retrieved.
The title of arXiv 2003.08583 and the exact title of the jacobson12fast PDF were not confirmed.
The landmark-detector error distributions behind the suggested 2D σ values are not sourced.
The Blender built-in tool claims (Laplacian Deform, Surface Deform, Elastic Deform with Kelvinlets, numpy-only Python) are version-sensitive and unverified.

ear.title: External ear
ear.summary:
I rewrote the external-ear note. It is about 2,680 words of body text, about 3,090 with the source list. It keeps all 17 harvested sources and every sourced fact from the earlier draft. The draft's ⚠️ badges are now 📄 (single source). I dropped the notes about the search budget running out. The earlier draft had no verification results to keep, and nothing has been refuted yet.

Corrections to the draft:
- The antihelix crura enclose the triangular fossa; they do not bound the conchal bowl. The inferior crus also forms the upper wall of the cymba conchae.
- Ears keep lengthening slowly through
algorithmic: Express ear parameters per side in a head frame aligned to the Frankfort horizontal and anchored at tragion: tragion_xyz, length_mm, width_ratio, tilt_deg, flare_deg or auriculocephalic_deg, three derived helix_mastoid_mm values, and a low-dimensional shape code (helix roll, antihelix and crura prominence, concha depth, lobule size and attachment).

Priors: length N(61, 4.5) mm, +2 if male, +0.2*max(0, age-25), hard bounds 45-85. width_ratio N(0.50, 0.05), bounds 0.38-0.65. tilt N(20 deg, 7), bounds -5 to 45. Tragion height vs orbitale N(0, 5 mm). auriculocephalic N(25 deg, 8), warning above 35.
Soft left-right symmetry with sigmas of 2 mm for length, 4 deg for tilt, 3 mm for tragion position and 3 mm for protrusion. Never hard-mirror the ears.
Treat the canons (brow and subnasale alignment, axis parallel to the nasal dorsum, ear length = nose length) as UI warnings beyond about 12 mm or 15 deg, never as energy terms.
Weight ear-contour residuals by max(0, cos(camera ray, ear-plane normal))^2. Frontal views constrain only silhouette and protrusion. Always use full perspective, never weak perspective.
Gate ear landmarks with a hair and accessory segmentation mask, use a Huber or Cauchy loss, and allow a small per-photo elastic nuisance deformation for glasses and hats.
Treat ears as rigid relative to the cranium across expressions. Visible tragion and helix points then serve as extra head-pose anchors.

Landmarks: superaurale, subaurale, preaurale, postaurale, otobasion superius and inferius, tragion, intertragal notch and lobule low point. Optionally a dense 55-point ear contour. Store each measurement with its definition, source_url, n and status.

Model the ear as a separate part with its own PCA or morphable model (York Ear Model or the ear part of the Universal Head Model, licences permitting), blended into the head at a ring around the ear root. Head models like FLAME carry coarse ears.
Add an explicit ear-contour identity term (Chamfer distance in the ear-normal and profile views), because face embeddings largely ignore ears.
takeaways: Anchor the ear to the skull, not to facial canons. Put tragion on the Frankfort horizontal (about the level of the lower orbital rim), just behind the mandibular condyle. Brow-to-subnasale alignment then becomes a check, not a rule.

Adult ear length is about 57-63 mm in the harvested means (sourced, 95% of values roughly 50-72 mm), and width is about 0.47-0.54 of length. Males are reliably longer (verified). Width differences by sex are inconsistent (contested), and length grows slowly through adult life (expert knowledge).
The ear's long axis leans back about 10-30 degrees from vertical (typical 20). The 'parallel to the nasal dorsum' and 'ear length = nose length' canons hold only in a minority of people.

Camera geometry causes larger ear errors than anatomy does. A frontal selfie at 0.3 m renders ears at about 0.73 of nose scale. A profile at 1 m inflates the near ear by about 9% against midline features. A 10 degree nod moves the ear about 17 mm against the brow. Solve full perspective and level the head to Frankfort horizontal before measuring.

Protrusion norms conflict (20-30 degrees vs under 25 degrees with 20 mm or less projection; McDowell's 3 mm symmetry goal is called too strict). Protrusion is also the commonest likeness failure. Use warnings, not clamps, and measure from front and back views.

Ears are a biometric (verified) that face-recognition embeddings largely ignore. Add an explicit ear-contour term, weighted by view angle to the ear plane, and capture a shot about 20-35 degrees behind true profile.
gaps: No sourced population norms yet for ear height relative to the brow and subnasale, or for long-axis tilt. Both come from expert knowledge only.
The measurement points behind the 2011 prominent-ear thresholds (PubMed 22067874) are unknown.
Which source holds the 20-30 degree auriculocephalic norm is unconfirmed.
The North Indian and Sundanese studies have no stated sample sizes. Titles are unconfirmed for PMC7580430 and the Sundanese study (pubmed.gov/36217409).
The adolescence to mid-adulthood morphometry paper (PubMed 10731092) was never read, so adult age-change data is missing from the sourced set.
The sub-feature dimensions (lobule, concha depth, rim thickness) are rough expert planning ranges only.
Availability and licences of ear morphable models and landmark datasets are unchecked.
No sources yet from Blender, Polycount or BlenderArtists practitioners on ear topology and sculpting.
Data from non-European, non-South-Asian populations (East Asian, African, Indigenous American) is thin. The only Chinese source covers growth, not adult norms.

expression-neutralization.title: Separating identity from expression
expression-neutralization.summary:
I wrote the note from scratch: neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed. So nothing in it is web-sourced, and it cites no URLs. Every claim is marked 🧠 (49) or ↔️ (13). Where a sibling note in the library already cites a source for the same claim, the note says so by name: single-image-regression, identity-embeddings, multi-view-fitting and facs-expressions.

It covers:
- **How 3D face models split identity from expression.** BFM plus FaceWarehouse, FLAME with its separate jaw joint, multilinear models, implicit models (NPHM, ImFace) and FACS-style blendshapes.
- **Why the split i
algorithmic: Extend bundle.py to X_v = X + D·psi_v + J(theta_v): a shared landmark set X, a per-view expression term with a low-rank landmark-space basis D (K≈10–20, sampled from FLAME expression at the landmarks), and a per-view jaw hinge about the condylar axis.
Gauge anchor: soft-constrain the mean expression of neutral-tagged views to 0 with sigma≈0.1 SD. If no view is tagged neutral, warn and do not report sub-mm mouth or eyelid measurements.

Priors: expression N(0,0.3²) on neutral views and N(0,1) on expressive ones; eyelids sigma≈0.2; identity N(0,1), flagged above 3; jaw on neutral views mean 0, sigma 1–1.5° (≈2–2.6 mm at the incisors; looser than the 2–3° in multi-view-fitting.md).

Per-landmark sigma multipliers via ViewObs.weights: rigid 1 / 1 / 1–1.5; semi-mobile 1 / 1.5–2 / 2–3; mobile 1 / 3 / 5–10 or drop; jaw-dependent landmarks free when the per-view jaw is fitted (values for neutral / mild / expressive views).

View tagging loop: tag from MediaPipe blendshape scores (neutral below ≈0.1–0.15, expressive above 0.4), fit, re-tag by the size of the fitted expression (below 0.5 / 0.5–1.5 / above 1.5 SD), refit; at most 3 rounds; log the thresholds.

Confound diagnostic: take the principal angles between the whitened identity and expression bases at the landmarks. Singular values near 1 mark directions only neutral capture can fix; report per-measurement uncertainty to the artist.
Do not orthogonalise the expression basis against identity, because that forces all shared variation into identity.

Fitting order: rigid pose from rigid landmarks; identity from neutral views; add expressive views with free per-view expression and jaw; silhouette and dense terms; hand off with expression 0, jaw 0, eyelids at rest. Take detail maps only from neutral views (or split them DECA-style into static and expression-driven parts).
takeaways: The identity/expression split in a 3D face model is a statistical convention, not anatomy. The two bases overlap along mouth width, lip vermilion height, lower-face height, eye opening, brow height and cheek fullness.

With one shared identity and a per-photo expression, a constant expression offset (a habitual smile in every photo) cannot be separated from identity. Only a photo tagged neutral, with a tight expression prior, anchors it.
Extra expressive photos improve identity only when expression and jaw are fitted per photo. A static-shape fitter (face3d's current bundle.py) averages the expressions into the identity.

A true neutral means no active action units, jaw at rest (2–4 mm gap between the incisors), lips lightly touching without chin-muscle (mentalis) strain, eyes level, and the upper lid about 1–2 mm over the iris edge.
On expressive photos, trust the nasal bridge and dorsum, forehead, orbital rims, ears and cranial outline. Distrust mouth width, lip fullness, nasolabial fold, cheek volume, lower lid and chin pad.

In Blender, keep Basis as the neutral identity and add one diagnostic shape key per photo holding its fitted expression. Sculpt identity only in Basis. A smile neutralised by hand is an estimate and should be labelled as one.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic, so every claim is unverified expert knowledge and no URLs are cited.
No quantified evidence of how much expression-diverse photo sets improve identity accuracy over 3–5 neutral views.
The magnitudes of each expression's effect (smile width, eye-opening reduction, alar widening, brow excursion) are order-of-magnitude estimates; primary anthropometric sources are needed.
The error left after reversing a smile with linear deltas (fat-pad sliding, fold formation) is unquantified.
Thresholds for the lip-incompetence gap and incisor display at rest need primary orthodontic or prosthodontic sources.
The FaceWarehouse bilinear truncation sizes and the BFM 2017 expression model details are unconfirmed.
Neutral-versus-expression subset errors on NoW for current regressors (expression leakage) were not retrieved.
The MediaPipe blendshape thresholds for tagging photos are uncalibrated design defaults.

eye-region.title: Eye, eyelids and orbit
eye-region.summary: Neither input existed: there was no eye-region harvest and no earlier draft. I wrote the note from scratch. The sourced facts come from sibling-topic harvests in research/_raw/harvests, the same practice the forehead-brow note follows, and I cited only the atomic facts those harvests attach to each URL. That is 41 sources, covering globe CT dimensions, corneal diameter and radii, levator and orbicularis anatomy, orbital rim and foramina, en/ex and orbitale definitions, intercanthal widths for Kosovo, Malay and Hong Kong samples, asymmetry thresholds, MediaPipe and dlib eye indices, and the can
algorithmic: Globe priors: globe_r N(12.0, 0.5), cornea_d N(11.8, 0.6), cornea_R N(7.8, 0.27), iris_depth N(3.0, 0.3) mm. Shared left and right with asymmetry σ 0.2; fixed unless the evidence is strong.

Globe placement: IPD N(63, 3.8); Hertel by population N(16|18|14, 2) for white, Black and East Asian; L-R difference σ 0.7 and vertical dystopia σ 1.0, flagged above 2 mm; globe centre ~1.5 ± 1.5 mm superolateral to the aperture centre on the bone layer.

Lids as parametric margin curves on the globe+cornea offset surface: fissure_len N(30, 1.6), fissure_h N(9.5, 1.0), tilt N(+5, 3) or N(+8, 3.5) for East Asian, MRD1 N(4.5, 0.8), MRD2 N(5.25, 0.8), peak offsets ±1 mm, ex_depth_behind_en N(10.5, 2.5).

Crease and fold as a mixture prior {absent, low 3-6, standard}: crease_h N(9, 1.5) for women and N(7, 1.2) for men (Western); fold_overhang 0-4 mm; epicanthus in [0, 1] shifting the visible en by up to 4 mm and hiding the caruncle.
Hard constraints: no lid-globe penetration; margin thickness 1.5-2.5 mm; margins meet only at the canthi; ex at least 3 mm inside the bony lateral rim.

Observation sigmas: ex 0.7 mm; en 1.0 mm (2.5 with epicanthus); lid contours as point-to-curve residuals with σ 0.5 normal and a free tangent; limbus edges 0.3 mm using horizontal extremes only; brow 3-5 mm for bone and 1 mm for the hair curve.

Gates: model lid-gaze coupling (upper lid ~0.8-1.0, lower ~0.3 in downgaze) or drop frames with gaze pitch beyond 10-15°. Drop lid residuals when eyeBlink, eyeSquint or eyeWide exceeds 0.2-0.3, and lower-lid and tear-trough residuals when cheekSquint does.
Scale fusion: inverse-variance combination of iris (±4-7%), IPD (±6%) and any caliper value, with the caliper value dominating. Brow hair and tear trough are separate layers anchored to bone.
takeaways: Globe and cornea are near-constant in adults (globe ~24 mm, cornea 11.84 ± 0.79 mm, anterior radius ~7.8 mm). Fix them on tight priors and use the iris as the metric ruler; never enlarge the globe to make eyes look bigger.
Eye likeness lives in the lids: fissure length and height, canthal tilt, MRD1/MRD2, lid-peak position (upper just nasal, lower just temporal to the pupil), crease versus fold, epicanthus and brow.
Measure tilt, MRD and crease in a pose-solved head frame (Frankfort horizontal). Head roll, pitch, gaze direction and smiling all fake lid changes, so gate those frames out.
The epicanthal fold moves the visible en ~1-4 mm laterally. Detectors label the visible corner, so en-en, fissure length and tilt need an epicanthus parameter.
Build lids as ~2 mm thick shells over the globe and corneal bulge. ex sits well behind en in depth and 5-7 mm inside the lateral orbital rim, and a forward ex is the classic flat-eye error.
Eyelid position is the most asymmetry-sensitive facial feature (~2 mm threshold), so keep a measured asymmetry layer rather than mirroring.
gaps: No eye-region harvest existed. All 41 URLs come from sibling-topic harvests, and lid, orbit and brow norms remain unsourced.
No source in the library for canthal depth (ex versus en versus corneal apex), crease height by population, tarsal dimensions, Hertel norms, MRD norms or canthal tilt norms.
No sourced data on epicanthus prevalence, single-eyelid prevalence, tear-trough geometry, lash geometry, caruncle or tear-meniscus size.
Palpebral fissure length values in the corneal-diameter forensic review [2] were not in the harvest facts; only its corneal figures were cited.
The Hong Kong periocular norms paper [18] probably has fissure, crease and tilt data, but only its intercanthal values were harvested.
The globe-in-orbit position (superolateral offset, corneal-tangent rule) needs the primary forensic papers (Stephan & Davidson 2008; Wilkinson 2004).

eyes-modeling-blender.title: Modeling and shading realistic eyes in Blender
eyes-modeling-blender.summary:
I wrote the eyes-modeling note from scratch because the earlier draft did not exist. It also has a sources JSON (16 sources, all URLs taken from the harvest, plus 18 references named by title) and a data JSON with 9 tables.

**Sourced content:**
- Globe and cornea geometry: globe about 24.2 × 23.7 × 22.0–24.8 mm; corneal diameter 11.84 ± 0.79 mm; corneal radii about 7.8 mm anterior and 6.4–6.5 mm posterior, where four sources agree (✅).
- The usual tutorial method: two spheres, the iris pushed inward, a convex glass cornea.

**Expert knowledge (🧠), clearly marked:**
- Optics: refractive indice
algorithmic: Each eye is a rigid sub-model. Its centre is fixed in the head frame and shared across views; gaze (yaw, pitch) is solved per view, with torsion from Listing's law. Template warps move eyeballs rigidly and never scale them.

Default eye geometry, with the front of the cornea at z=0 and +z backward: cornea radius 7.8 mm, asphericity −0.25, limbus radius 5.85 mm (giving a 2.49 mm bulge); sclera ellipsoid semi-axes 12.1 / 11.85 / 11.47 mm, centred at z=12.53; iris plane at z≈3.2; centre of rotation at z=13.3. The iris circle's centre therefore sits 10.7 mm in front of the centre of rotation (sigma 0.6).

Priors (mean, sigma): globe width 24.2 (0.9) mm; corneal radius front 7.8 (0.27) and back 6.45 (0.30) mm; asphericity −0.25 (0.12); iris diameter 11.8 (0.6) mm; outward kappa offset 5 (2) degrees; cornea front ahead of the outer orbital rim 16 (2.5) mm; upper-lid coverage 1.5 (1.0) mm; lower-lid show 0.3 (0.7) mm; distance-gaze IPD 63 (3.8) mm; left-right shape difference 0 (0.3) mm. Axial length is fixed at 24 mm because photos cannot observe it.

Iris outline residual: the distance from detected edge points to the projected 3D iris circle (radius = iris diameter / 2), using the inner and outer side arcs only. Refraction at the limbus can be ignored. The pupil needs refraction, or the shortcut of scaling by 1.13 and moving it 0.5 mm forward.
Vergence: each eye's line of sight passes through that view's fixation point, by default the camera centre. Gaze is solved per view when the subject followed each camera.

Hard constraints: the inner lid margin's signed distance to the eye surface (cornea bulge included) stays within 0-0.3 mm, enforced by projection; lash roots stay on the front lid margin, at least 0.2 mm clear of the cornea.
An optional catchlight residual uses a corneal sphere of radius 7.8 mm to check the light direction and gaze.

Output contract: separate closed objects Eye_L/R, Cornea_L/R, TearLine_L/R and Lashes (curves). Materials are generated per Blender version, with sockets looked up by identifier. An iris texture is treated as biometric data: kept local, opt-in, deletable.
takeaways: Do not fit globe size to the photo. It is about 24 mm with a spread of only about ±1 mm. 'Big eyes' come from the lid opening and lid position, so fit lids, eyeball position and gaze instead.

The visible iris/corneal diameter (about 11.8 mm, SD 0.5-0.8 mm) is the best metric ruler on the face. Fit the iris ellipse using only its inner and outer side arcs, because the lids hide the top and bottom.

Corneal radius of about 7.8 mm is the most solid number in the note: four sources agree. A single cornea shell with IOR about 1.336-1.3375 reproduces the eye's real corneal power; the tissue value 1.376 over-magnifies the iris slightly.
In Cycles, turn off the cornea's shadow visibility or use shadow caustics (MNEE). Otherwise the glass cornea darkens the iris.
Model the 1.5-2 mm lid margin, a tear-line strip and the caruncle. Paper-thin lids and a missing tear line make eyes look pasted on.

Rig each eye at its centre of rotation (about 13.3 mm behind the front of the cornea), using Damped Track (which follows Listing's law) plus a 4-5 degree outward offset for angle kappa. This avoids a cross-eyed look.
gaps: No primary source in the inputs for caruncle size, eyelash counts and lengths, tear meniscus height, or lid-margin thickness; all are expert knowledge.
No source for the eye's refractive indices, front chamber depth, angle kappa, centre of rotation or Hertel norms; all are expert knowledge.
The individual corneal radius figures were tied to specific papers only at search-summary level in the harvest. One cohort description (25 eyes aged 60-80) may be misattributed to PubMed 16266736.
Blender 5.x specifics are unverified: shadow-caustics (MNEE) limits and UI paths, EEVEE Next refraction options and sockets, and whether Cycles supports nested-dielectric priority.
No measured sclera colour or reflectance values, and no iris light-scattering data; the shading values are practice defaults only.
Palpebral fissure and Hertel norms by population or ethnicity are not researched.
The licence and availability of public eye-shape datasets or parametric eye models (e.g. Bérard et al.) are unknown.
Inputs [2], [6], [7] and [11] were harvested but no specific claims were extracted from them.

face-perception-likeness.title: Psychology of face recognition and likeness
algorithmic: Keep three weights separate. Measurement noise goes in the data term (ViewObs.sigma_px and weights) and population spread in the prior (Priors.sigma). Perceptual importance (Table B) is used only for evaluation, user guidance and view requests, never in the data term.
Shrinkage audit: k_i = 1 − σ²_post,i/σ²_prior,i from diag((JᵀJ)⁻¹) after LM in face3d/solve/bundle.py. Show it as a heatmap, and flag k < 0.8 on rank 1–5 regions by asking for another view.

Replace the scalar Priors.sigma = 8.0 with per-landmark, per-axis arrays of 1.0–1.5 × the population SD. Use a Student-t prior (ν ≈ 4) so distinctive features (|z| > 2) survive, with sex- and ancestry-matched means and no default European mean.

Optional distinctiveness restore: X_out = μ + α(X_fit − μ) per region, default α = 1. An 'unbiased' mode sets α = 1/k only where k ≥ 0.5, capped at 1.5. Lower-k regions are flagged rather than amplified.

Likeness metric: Umeyama similarity alignment on en, ex, n, glabella and sn, then a low-pass to wavelengths of about 9 mm or more and a region-weighted RMS (weights 1.0 eyelids, 0.9 brows, 0.8 lips, 0.7 eye spacing and depth, 0.7 nose, 0.6 vertical proportions, 0.6 outline and hair, 0.5 age state, 0.1–0.2 ears and cranium). Report detail residuals, global scale and aspect ratio separately.

Distinctiveness vector: about 17 IPD-normalised relational measures, z-scored against matched norms, with D = √(Σz²/n). The top-k |z| features need 2 or more views at least 30° apart and are surfaced as a protect list.

Expression-aware view weights: in non-neutral views, multiply confidence by 0.2–0.3 for raised brows, for the mouth (cheilion, stomion, vermilion) in smiles, and for the lower lid in Duchenne smiles. Rigid landmarks (nasion, endocanthion, tragion) stay at 1.0.
Fit multiple sessions with per-session cameras and shared identity, and use a robust loss on per-session residuals so one atypical photo cannot set a feature.
Extend the landmark set (synthetic.py and the detector map) with brow peak, upper-lid peak, lower-lid low point, crease height and the lower vermilion border.

Tests: with 3 or more views at least 30° apart, require |dev_fit|/|dev_true| in 0.9–1.1 and a cosine of 0.95 or more on rank 1–5 landmarks. A frontal-only fit must flag depth shrinkage rather than pass silently.
takeaways: Identity is coded as deviation from an average, so a regularised (MAP) fit acts as an anti-caricature. With the engine's σp = 8 mm, a coordinate with 8 mm data error keeps only 50% of the sitter's deviation, and frontal-only depth keeps about 20–40%. This is the main reason auto-fits look like 'a relative'.

The eye region dominates identity, and the brows count at least as much as the eyes. Lid margin and peak, fissure, canthal tilt, brow height, tilt and thickness, and lip vermilion thickness should get the tightest tolerances (about 0.5–1.5 mm).

Shape and pigmentation contribute roughly equally. Judging a blank-eyed, browless, bald clay head against colour photos is unfair, so add eyes, brow mask, vermilion boundary and a hair cap, and compare against desaturated photos.

Familiar viewers tolerate global scale and stretch but not errors in internal feature shape or relations. Unfamiliar viewers (the artist, the developer, most testers) are poor judges swayed by hair, lighting and camera distance. Validate with people who know the sitter, using a blind 1+5 lineup.
Identity is carried by mid-scale form (about 9–18 mm wavelength on a 140 mm face). Get the 64–128 px thumbnail right before any pores or wrinkles.

The sitter is a biased judge: they prefer the mirrored and more flattering version. The other-race effect affects artists, reviewers, detectors and population priors alike, so use ancestry-matched priors and same-group reviewers.
gaps: No harvest file or earlier draft existed. Every claim is recalled expert knowledge with no linked source, and the reference names and years need confirming in the verification pass.

There is no measured millimetre just-noticeable difference for 3D feature displacement in a familiar face. The tolerances in Table B are design values derived from asymmetry-visibility thresholds and detector noise.

Exact effect sizes are uncertain: the best-likeness caricature level, the stretch-tolerance limit, the own-race-bias odds ratios, the low-resolution recognition threshold and the shape-versus-pigmentation split.
No evidence was found on whether MAP or unbiased (de-shrunk) shape estimates are perceived as better likenesses in 3D sculpts.
No evidence was found on whether DCNN identity embeddings track human likeness judgements of untextured clay renders.
The Abudarham & Yovel critical-feature list is recalled with moderate confidence and conflicts with the second-order spacing literature.
The lineup protocol (1+5 foils, 80% target) and the expression weight multipliers are untested design proposals.

face-retopology.title: Face retopology and edge flow
face-retopology.summary:
I wrote a new face-retopology note: neither input existed (no harvest JSON, no earlier draft), so every claim is expert knowledge (74 🧠, 13 ↔️, 0 ✅/📄) and it cites no URLs. Library sibling notes are cross-referenced by file path only. The note covers six areas:
- **Edge-loop systems:** lid-margin pair and lid loops (orbicularis oculi), vermilion loops, white-roll support and mouth bag (orbicularis oris), nasolabial and mask loop, nose and nostril rings, forehead, jaw, ear and a symmetric midline.
- **Poles:** an Euler-formula argument that poles cannot be removed (net Σ(4−valence) = 8 on a clo
algorithmic: Template sidecar: named ordered loops (closed or open), poles, feature_curves mapped to 2D contours, regions, symmetry_map and midline. After every operation, assert that vertex count and order are unchanged, loops are still closed, and no pole sits in a forbidden zone.

Fit feature loops with point-to-curve residuals and free tangential sliding. σ normal to the curve: lid margin and vermilion 0.5-1.0 mm, alar rim 1-1.5 mm, nasolabial fold 2-3 mm (down-weighted on neutral photos), jaw silhouette 1.5-2.5 mm.

Edge-flow regularisers: ARAP or Laplacian against the template with σ at 5-15% of rest edge length; a second-difference smoothness term along each named loop (σ 0.2-0.5 mm per vertex); tangential relaxation projected to the surface, excluding feature loops; barriers on quad angles outside 30-150°, aspect ratios above 4, and normal flips.

If the deliverable will be subdivided, compute residuals on the limit surface S·V (sparse Catmull-Clark limit stencils, or Blender's evaluated level 2 as an approximation) to avoid systematic shrinkage of e²/(6R).
Pole QA: forbidden zones are geodesic rings of at least 2 around the feature loops. Report each violation and the net Σ(4−valence): 8 for a closed surface, 4 with an open neck.
For auto-retopology of arbitrary user meshes, export a per-region density field as vertex colour for Quad Remesher, and feature loops as edge constraints for Instant Meshes or as group boundaries.

Cross-topology mapping: embed the quad delivery template barycentrically in the fitting template (for example FLAME) once, then map each subject's fit through that embedding plus a normal offset, so retopology happens once per template.
Keep the topology exactly symmetric and model shape asymmetry with a prior of σ 1.5-3 mm. Never force symmetry.
takeaways: Never retopologise the likeness mesh. Design one quad template with proper loops, fit it per subject, and move detail across with Shrinkwrap and Multires Reshape. Remeshing loses correspondence, shape keys, UVs and landmarks.

The loops that matter are the lid-margin pair plus 3-5 upper-lid loops, 3-5 loops per vermilion with a support loop outside the border, a nasolabial loop lying on the crease, nostril rings, and an exact x=0 midline.

Poles are mathematically unavoidable (net Σ(4−valence) = 8 on a closed all-quad head, 4 with an open neck). Place them in the cheek, temple, glabella, alar crease, chin sides and behind the ear, at least 2 rings from the lid margins, vermilion, commissure, alar rim and canthi.
Auto-remeshers (QuadriFlow, Instant Meshes, Quad Remesher) make good sculpt proxies but not rig-grade facial flow. Quad Remesher with region groups and painted density comes closest.
A sensible default is an 8-12k-quad head with edges of about 1-2 mm across lid and lip loops, 4-7 mm on cheeks and forehead and 6-12 mm on the scalp, which gives about 2-3M quads at Multires L4.
Catmull-Clark pulls convex features inward by about e²/(6R), roughly 0.1-0.4 mm on lips, nose tip and chin, so fit the subdivision limit surface or compensate with Apply Base.
gaps: No web sources: neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so every claim is unverified 🧠 or ↔️ and the note cites no URLs.
No quantitative study is known that compares face topologies by deformation error. The loop counts and densities are practitioner heuristics.
The status of RetopoFlow, Quad Remesher and LoopTools on Blender 5.x is unknown, as is whether 5.x added native retopology tools.
The performance on faces of learned quad remeshers from 2024-2026 is unknown.
The licence of the delivery template is unresolved: FLAME is non-commercial, while MPFB2 hm08 is believed CC0 (contested).
The game polygon budgets (mobile and LOD0) and the MetaHuman vertex count are recalled, not sourced.

face-rigging.title: Face rigging for a reconstructed head
face-rigging.summary:
Neither input file existed: there was no face-rigging harvest and no earlier draft. The new note borrows URLs from the library's blender-face-addons and facs-expressions harvests and marks where each came from. I checked all 22 URLs against the harvest files; none were invented. Evidence status: 8 ✅ / 22 📄 / 71 🧠 / 13 ↔️.

What the note covers:
- **Bone rigs.** Rigify, including its modular "skin" face since Blender 3.0, and Auto-Rig Pro.
- **Shape-key rigs.** Faceit, Face Shape Key Rig and CaptureForge, with sourced versions and licences.
- **Expression vocabularies.** FACS, ARKit and MediaPi
algorithmic: RigProfile shipped with each template: {template_id, topology_hash, bones[{name, head, tail, roll_ref}], weights by index, ARKit52 deltas}. Each joint is a barycentric surface point plus a normal offset, a combination of landmarks, or an interior point. Refuse to rig if the topology hash does not match.

Interior pivots: warp with a thin-plate spline from at least 30 surface correspondences, then pull toward priors. Eye centre = fitted globe centre, σ 0.5 mm. Condyle ≈10–15 mm anterior and 0–10 mm inferior to tragion, 15–20 mm deep, σ 3–4 mm. Head pivot ≈ midpoint of the mastoid tips, σ 6 mm. Then rebuild edit_bones and call pose.rigify_generate().

Weight checks: per-vertex sum 1 ± 1e-4; at most 4 influences for engine export; bleed across lips or lids ≤ 0.02; rig rest pose equals the neutral within 1e-5 × head size; eyelid-to-eyeball gap ≤ 0.5 mm.

Expression transfer: express each template delta in its vertex's (normal, tangent, bitangent) frame, scale by √(one-ring area ratio), and re-apply on the fitted head. Optionally run deformation transfer with matrix-free conjugate gradients in pure NumPy (Blender has no SciPy). Reject a key whose main displacement departs more than 30° from the direction its muscle pulls.

Personalisation (Li, Weise & Pauly 2010): fit ARKit weights to each expression photo with identity fixed, then minimise Σ‖(B+ΔB)w_e − X_e‖² + λ‖ΔB‖², starting from λ≈10 (relative) and annealing down. Correct only keys whose weight exceeds 0.3 in at least one photo.

Jaw model: rotation θ = θmax·w with θmax ≈ 25°; condylar translation d = dmax·max(0, (w − w0)/(1 − w0)) with w0 ≈ 0.4–0.5 and dmax ≈ 10–15 mm. Clamp mouthClose ≤ jawOpen and add an eyeBlink × eyeLookDown corrective.

Mocap: per key, w' = clip((w − n)/(m − n), 0, 1)·g, where n = neutral median, m = 98th percentile of the range-of-motion take, and g = gain. Deadzone 0.02–0.05. Map names through a 52×K matrix. One Euro min_cutoff 1.0–1.5 Hz for mouth and brows, 3–5 Hz for blink and gaze, 0.5–1 Hz for head rotation (filtered on quaternions). Read a non-blocking UDP socket from bpy.app.timers.
Expression-likeness metric: landmark RMS between the rig's best fit and each expression photo, as % of inter-ocular distance. Targets: anchor points ≤ 1.5%, contour points ≤ 2.5%.
takeaways: Rig the fitting template once, not each scan. Fitted heads keep the template's vertex count and order, so weights and ARKit keys copy over by index. Only bone positions (thin-plate-spline warp plus anatomical pivot priors) and expression deltas (tangent-frame or deformation transfer) need recomputing.

Use a hybrid rig by default: bones for head, neck, jaw and eyes, because shape keys move in straight lines and cannot follow the arcs of the jaw and eyelids; ARKit-52-named shape keys plus correctives for everything else, so iPhone and MediaPipe capture drive them directly.

A photo-fitted neutral is not rig-ready. It needs open eyelids with thickness, separate eyeballs (radius about 12 mm, pivot about 13–14 mm behind the corneal apex), a cut lip line with a mouth bag, and teeth and tongue parented to head and jaw. It must also be neutralised first, or any leftover expression gets baked into the rest pose.

Blender's automatic weights fail on non-manifold or very small real-scale meshes. On a closed-mouth neutral they bleed across the lips and eyelids, so always strip upper-lip and upper-lid bone groups from the lower lip and lower lid.

Likeness in motion comes from personalised keys (the subject's own smile, blink and brows fitted from expression photos), not from mocap. Mocap needs per-performer neutral and range-of-motion calibration and blink-aware One Euro filtering.

Shape-key animation is stored on the Key datablock, not the object. On Blender 4.4+/5.x, F-curves go through slotted-Action channelbags (to verify). Write keyframes in bulk with keyframe_points.add plus foreach_set.
Face Shape Key Rig only controls keys it is given; Faceit and CaptureForge generate them. Faceit is listed up to Blender 5.2 and FSKR needs 5.2+, so 5.2 LTS is the safe overlap.
gaps: No face-rigging harvest or draft existed, so Rigify internals, Auto-Rig Pro features, prices and versions, and the Face Cap, iFacialMocap, Rokoko and Live Link Face details are unsourced expert knowledge.
The ARKit 52 name list and the semantics of individual keys (especially mouthClose) were not read from Apple's BlendShapeLocation page [7].
The Live Link Face packet and CSV layout, rotation units and default port are unverified.
There is no millimetre-level benchmark comparing ARKit TrueDepth and MediaPipe webcam blendshape accuracy, and no benchmark of how well a rig reproduces a person's expressions.
The adult jaw-motion and eyelid numbers used as rig limits and priors come from memory, not anatomical or clinical sources.
Rigify changes from 4.x to 5.3, Auto-Rig Pro and Faceit support beyond Blender 5.2, and whether Multires detail behaves well on a shape-keyed base all remain unverified.
Time-sensitive items were not checked: MetaHuman Animator input from webcams and Android since UE 5.6, the reported 2025 open-sourcing of NVIDIA Audio2Face, and Face Cap pricing.
Two leads were never read: TalkingHead's FACEIT.md and wk FaceRig.

face-scan-datasets.title: Public 3D face scan datasets
algorithmic: Dataset adapter schema: every loader declares units, up/forward axes, handedness, topology_id, landmark_convention (68 iBUG / 74 FaceWarehouse / 83 BU-3DFE / 7 NoW), licence_id, commercial_ok, redistribution_ok, population_tags and capture_tech. A licence gate blocks exporting a prior whose provenance includes commercial_ok=false.

Unit auto-detection: measure the outer-eye-corner distance (or the inner-corner distance, about 28-36 mm), snap the scale to {1e-6, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1, 1e3}, and abort if the result falls outside 0.6-1.4x the expected value. Y-up to Blender Z-up is (x, y, z) -> (x, -z, y).

Ground-truth noise model: sigma_gt per capture_tech (3dMD 0.2-0.5 mm, DSLR multi-view stereo 0.1-0.4, Kinect 1-4, whole-body laser 2-5); robust Huber or Geman-McClure residual with scale about 2*sigma_gt; benchmarks report sigma_gt beside the error.

Region weights for fitting to scans: skin core 1.0, lips 0.7 (seam 0.3), brows 0.3, lids/lashes 0.2, ears 0.2, inner mouth/eyes/nostrils 0, scalp 0 (Headspace: 0.5 with a one-sided outward cap offset of 1-5 mm).

Landmark prior σ after Procrustes alignment with scale removed: about 1.5-3 mm for tight points (inner eye corners, alae), 2-4 mm in-plane and 3-6 mm in depth for nose tip, chin, glabella and gonion. Use a population mixture chosen by fit likelihood, and widen 1.3-1.5x when no component fits.

Validation harness: subsets of 3, 5 and 9 calibrated views; 7-landmark similarity plus ICP alignment; per-region scan-to-mesh error. Expect about 1-1.5 mm for a 3DMM fit from 5 or more views and 0.3-0.7 mm for photogrammetry. A leakage guard blocks evaluation on subjects used in any prior (for example REALY/Headspace vs LYHM or HIFI3D++).
Store each loader's licence-text hash and download date; datasets get withdrawn or relicensed.
takeaways: Use public scan datasets to test and calibrate the fitting engine, never as shipped assets: nearly all are non-commercial research-only, and their licences usually cover trained models and PCA bases too.

Multiface (CC BY-NC, open download, calibrated, tracked meshes) and the MPI sets (CoMA, VOCASET, FaMoS, NoW; account plus click-through) are the most reachable for unaffiliated developers; FaceScape, Headspace and the Binghamton sets need an institutional signatory.
Only Headspace (tight caps) shows the cranium; every other set loses the back of the head under hair, so back-of-head priors must come from LYHM/UHM or head-length and head-breadth norms.

Scans are not perfect ground truth: σ is about 0.2-0.5 mm for 3dMD and DSLR multi-view stereo and 1-4 mm for Kinect, with spikes at lashes and brows, holes at eyes and nostrils, and no inner mouth. Errors below about 1.5x σ_gt cannot be resolved.

Populations are narrow (FaceScape mostly Chinese; Headspace mostly white British; MPI and TUM sets mostly young European), so priors need population mixtures and wider σ for under-represented subjects.
AFLW2000-3D and 300W-LP are 3DMM pseudo-ground-truth, and the NeRSemble, RenderMe-360 and Ava-256 geometry is reconstructed; none are millimetre ground truth.

Units and axes vary (FLAME in metres and Y-up; 3dMD exports in mm; BFM files in µm or mm depending on version), so detect scale from the outer-eye-corner distance (adult about 85-100 mm) rather than trusting the file.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so every fact is unverified expert knowledge with no URLs.

Exact counts are uncertain for FaMoS frames, Multiface camera counts and size, NeRSemble sequences, RenderMe-360 and Ava-256 specs, and the FaceScape camera count, age range and base-mesh vertex count.
Current (late-2026) availability and terms are unknown for D3DFACS, the Binghamton sets (fees), the FaceScape server and Headspace.
Units and axis conventions per dataset (FaceScape, BFM 2009, Multiface, Headspace) need checking against the actual files.
Region weights, landmark prior σ and validation targets are expert estimates with no published source.
It is legally unresolved whether non-commercial research licences allow personal artistic use, and whether PCA statistics derived from the data inherit its licence.
It is not known whether a permissively licensed (CC BY or CC0) metric head-scan dataset exists as of 2026.

facebuilder-blender.title: KeenTools FaceBuilder for Blender in practice
facebuilder-blender.summary: The topic harvest and the earlier draft did not exist, so I wrote the note from scratch: about 2,700 words, plus a sources JSON with 4 sources and a data JSON with 9 tables. The only sourced facts come from four BlenderArtists FaceBuilder release threads. I reused their URLs from the library's sibling harvest `_raw/harvests/blenderartists-forum.json`, and the Sources section says so.
