One caveat: under a strict reading of "provided inputs", those URLs fall outside the allowed set. The sourced facts are that 2021.1 added neural auto-alignment (which the vendor says is not always accurate), that
algorithmic: Pins are surface-anchored constraints: Pin{view, xy_px, tri, bary, sigma, source}. Re-solve on drag with warm-started Levenberg–Marquardt, 2–5 iterations per mouse event, using only pinned Jacobian rows; Huber δ = 2σ.
Pin σ in % IOD: user 0.75; auto 1.5 at corners, 2.5 on contours (point-to-curve), 4 on the jaw outline (silhouette), 3–5 on ears; never pin hair. A user pin replaces auto pins within about 3% IOD.

Rigidity sliders map to log-scale priors: shape ~N(0,1) with λ = 10^(2r−1), default r = 0.5. Expression is off by default; when on, per-view expression ~N(0, 0.6²) and neutral views are fixed at 0. Neck pose σ is 10–15°; blink σ is about 0.2.

Focal prior log-σ: 0.03 for uncropped EXIF with a 35 mm-equivalent value, 0.08 when a crop or zoom is suspected, 0.35–0.5 with no EXIF (start at 50 mm-eq), and a 0.02 camera-group tie. Estimate only when the posterior σ(log f) is below 0.10, otherwise report 'not observable'. Never solve sensor size.
Fix the principal point at the centre unless crop metadata exist. k1 = 0 by default; enable it with σ 0.05 only when f35 < 28 mm or for action cameras, and prefer undistorting first.

Hair-aware contours: disable silhouette terms above the trichion and on occluded ears. Regularise cranium vertices to the prior with σ 5–8 mm and log-normal priors on g–op and eu–eu, and write per-vertex 'from prior' confidence to a colour attribute.

Interop: import any Blender camera with a background image as a view, FaceBuilder's included. Treat an imported FaceBuilder head as a point-to-plane observation with σ 1–1.5 mm (3–4 mm on cranium and ears). Never ship KeenTools topology.
QA gates: per-pin residual ≤ 1% IOD, per-view RMS ≤ 0.5% IOD, group focal spread ≤ 5%, IPD 55–72 mm, and a warning when the camera-to-nose distance is under 0.8 m.
Texture blending: weight cos(θ)^k with k = 2–4 (an 'angle strictness' slider), reject θ > 70–75°, feather seams over 8–16 texels, and keep a per-texel view-index map.
takeaways: FaceBuilder is a pin-driven template fitter. The photos give per-view cameras plus a plausible base head, but the likeness of lids, alae, vermilion, ears and the hair-covered cranium must be sculpted afterwards.
Auto-alignment (2021.1) is a first draft. The vendor itself says pins can need manual fixes, so check every ¾ and profile pin and pin the profile silhouettes by hand.
Use few, confident pins. Pins in one view change the shared shape, so re-check all views after each edit; fighting pins cause lumps.

Focal error is self-limiting. Estimation works at selfie range, where it matters (about 1.4 mm of nose-width error per 20% focal error at 0.5 m), and is unobservable at 2 m or more, where it barely matters. Fix focal from EXIF for distant shots.
Treat pinhole-only cameras as a hard constraint: undistort wide or action-camera photos, avoid off-centre crops, digital zoom and portrait mode, and un-mirror selfies.
Never pin the hair outline. Check the prior-filled cranium against head length g–op of about 182–200 mm, or shoot with the hair slicked back or under a cap.
The live FaceBuilder mesh is regenerated. Duplicate it before Multires sculpting, and keep its cameras as matched likeness-check views.
Turn Expressions off when all photos are neutral, because it adds degrees of freedom that can absorb identity.
gaps: No topic harvest (_raw/harvests/facebuilder-blender.json) and no earlier draft existed. The only URLs are four BlenderArtists threads reused from the sibling harvest blenderartists-forum.json, of which only search-result summaries were seen. Strictly, those URLs fall outside the 'provided inputs'.
No primary KeenTools documentation, release notes or pricing page was available. UI names, defaults, the blendshape count, UV layouts, texture limits and platform support are all recollection.
There is no independent or vendor mm-accuracy benchmark for FaceBuilder; the accuracy rows are library estimates.
The 2025–2026 version state, Blender 5.2 LTS / 5.3 support, current price, tiers and trial length are unknown.
The Table D focal-observability numbers are my own order-of-magnitude derivation under stated assumptions, not measurements.
Whether FaceBuilder supports lens distortion, per-view expression locking, or extensions.blender.org distribution is unverified.
The naming and structure of FaceBuilder's camera objects, which matter for the planned 'import existing solve' feature, are unverified.
No user-review corpus (Reddit, YouTube, Superhive or other ratings) was harvested; the reception summary is a synthesis.

facial-asymmetry.title: Natural facial asymmetry
facial-asymmetry.summary:
I rewrote /home/user/minedesign/research/anatomy/facial-asymmetry.md (about 2,790 words before the source list). It keeps all 15 harvested sources and their citations, along with every caveat about unconfirmed attribution. The obsolete notes about the search budget are gone.

Corrections to the earlier draft:
- The 0.8 mm whole-face results in [6] and [7] probably come from the same Brown University group (Taylor et al. 2014), so they are downgraded from two concordant sources to one line of evidence.
- An arithmetic check shows the per-third RMSD values (0.5–0.6 mm) cannot share a registratio
algorithmic: Symmetric/asymmetric decomposition: reflect with M=diag(-1,1,1), swap L/R labels, align with face3d.geometry.procrustes.umeyama, then S = 1/2(X + aligned mirror) and A = X - S. Rotating by half the alignment rotation puts the symmetry plane at x=0.

Gauge: the three antisymmetric rigid degrees of freedom (x-translation, yaw, roll) must be removed. The symmetry residual (X_l - M X_r)/sigma_sym and the midline residual x_i/sigma_mid in face3d/solve/bundle.py assume the head frame is the symmetry frame, so re-estimate the frame after each outer iteration and let the cameras absorb the change.
Symmetry-plane fit with robust weights: upper face 1.0, midface 0.5, lower face 0.25, ears 0.1, with a Huber loss at about 1 mm.

Per-landmark sigma_sym (per axis, on d = 2A): eye corners and lids 0.7–1.0 mm; brows 1.5–2.0; alare, orbitale, zygion 1.0–1.5; cheilion 1.5–2.0; gonion 2.5–3.0; ear landmarks 3–4. Per-landmark sigma_mid: nasion and glabella 0.75–1.0; pronasale and subnasale 1.5–2.0; pogonion and menton 2–3. These replace the uniform defaults (2.0 and 1.5).
Heavy-tailed symmetry loss (Student-t with nu about 4, or Huber) so that real large asymmetries are kept.
A symmetry_mode schedule: assist (sigma_sym x 0.25) for the coarse pose and shape fit, prior for refinement, and enforce only as a user block-out option, never for output.

Evidence gating: accept asymmetry for a pair only when two or more views about 30 degrees or more apart observe it; otherwise shrink sigma_A by 4x. Display asymmetry only where |d| > 2 sigma_post, taken from (J^T J)^-1.
Mirrored-photo detection: refit each view with u -> W - u and the L/R labels swapped, compare reprojection error and agreement of A across views, then prompt the user.

Two-stage RBF warp: base = warp(template, S) and Asym = warp(template, S + A) - base, exported as a Blender shape key. Never symmetrise the target landmarks. Ship the template with a vertex mirror map.

Report: global and per-third RMSD against the mirror, |d| for each pair, cants, and midline deviations. Flag eyelids at 2 mm or more, brows and mouth at 3 mm or more, cants at 3 degrees or more, and global RMSD above 1.5 mm or below 0.3 mm. Flags ask the user to confirm and never auto-correct.

Evaluation: score S and A separately, plus asymmetry recovery (cosine and magnitude ratio). Make the asymmetry in synthetic.random_subject region-scaled, and add a test that a symmetric face at 3 degrees of yaw returns A of about 0.
takeaways: Every normal face is asymmetric. Whole-face RMSD against the mirror is about 0.8 mm, but landmark left–right differences reach 0.6–4.6 mm, concentrated in the lower and lateral face. The upper face is the most symmetric and is the best reference for the midline and symmetry plane.

Perception thresholds are feature-specific and fall at about 2–4 mm: eyelids are most sensitive at about 2 mm, brows and mouth corners about 3 mm, and specialists detect smaller differences than laypeople. 3–4° of cant across a 60 mm baseline equals 3–4 mm. These are abnormality thresholds; likeness for familiar viewers is probably stricter.

Mirroring removes visible, identity-bearing asymmetry (lids, brows, nasal tip, mouth corners, chin, ears). Mirroring a half-face produces a different-looking chimera and distorts widths, and symmetrising acts as an anti-caricature toward the average face.

Use symmetry for block-out, topology, UVs and rig scaffolding. Keep the topology symmetric forever and let the shape be asymmetric. Turn shape symmetry off at the first secondary-form pass and keep the asymmetry in an 'Asym' shape key you can switch on and off.

Apparent asymmetry in photos is mostly pose and lens: 3° of yaw gives about 4 mm at the eye corners and 2° of roll about 2 mm across the pupils. Mirrored selfies flip the asymmetry. Estimate asymmetry only in 3D from multiple pose-solved views.
Sanity check: a finished adult head should show about 0.5–1.5 mm whole-face RMSD against its mirror. Near 0 means the face was symmetrised; several mm points to pose, lens or L/R-label errors.
The sitter judges likeness from their mirror image and their friends from the true image (Mita 1977), so show both versions at review. Never mirror pores, moles or photo texture.
gaps: No direct study found that measures whether symmetrising a 3D or photographic face lowers likeness or identity-recognition ratings.
There are no adult dense-surface asymmetry norms by region (nose, orbits, chin, ears), sex or ancestry. Table B's working ranges are expert estimates.
The age slope of asymmetry in PubMed 30511968 was not extracted.
Several attributions are unconfirmed: the 0.80 ± 0.24 mm figure to PMC4614853, the 3–4 mm / 3–4° figure to PMC11595402, and the 0.25 mm child offset in PMC10389059 (from a search excerpt).
The angle definition behind the 6° lower-face deviation in PMC7603600 is unknown.
Directional asymmetry (whether one side or one midline direction dominates) is unresolved, and the Raine-study claim remains unsourced.
No data on the just-noticeable displacement of a feature in a familiar face, which is the threshold that actually matters for likeness.
Dynamic (expression) asymmetry is covered only qualitatively.
Whether 2D landmark detectors are biased toward symmetric placement, and whether 3DMM regressors under-reconstruct asymmetry, are untested hypotheses.
The Blender behaviour of shape keys with Multires and Dyntopo is version-sensitive and not checked against the current manual.

facial-proportions-canons.title: Facial proportions, neoclassical canons and the golden-ratio myth
facial-proportions-canons.summary:
I wrote the note from the harvest and my own knowledge. No earlier draft existed, so there were no verification results to carry over. The body is about 2,840 words (slightly over the 2,800 target), plus a 29-source list and a further-reading list.

Main findings:
- **Canons:** every population tested since Farkas 1985 fails most of the neoclassical canons. The best one, the orbital canon (intercanthal width = eye width), is met by only about a third of people (30.6% in [4]; most validated in [6]; not validated in Al-Sebaei [1]). Equal thirds failed at p < 0.0001 in 168 Saudi adults.
- **Golde
algorithmic: Encode proportions as log-ratio priors with a Student-t loss (nu ~4): E = sum rho_t((log(d_a/d_b) - log mu_k)/sigma_k). Suggested sigma_log is 0.05-0.10 within a population and 0.07-0.18 when the population is unknown (Table E / ratio_prior_defaults).

Shrinkage check: a prior keeps only k = sp^2/(sp^2+sd^2) of a true deviation. Once a ratio is seen in at least 2 calibrated views, loosen its prior x2 or drop it. Warn if a leave-prior-out refit moves any observed measure by more than 0.3 mm.
Do not stack canon ratio priors on a statistical shape model prior (BFM/FLAME) without inflating sigma x2; otherwise use them as diagnostics only.
Compute vertical ratios as projections in the Frankfort-horizontal head frame and widths as 3D chords. Use ratios before metric scale is solved and millimetres only after.
Condition mu by sex and age band. The user chooses the norm set, with a pooled wide-sigma default. Never infer ancestry from the face.

Canon-based priors apply only to unobserved regions: vertex/skull under hair (eye-line fraction 0.51 +/- 0.025, v-gn/n-gn 1.93 +/- 0.04, cranial index 0.79 +/- 0.07), a hidden ear (sa-sba/n-sn 1.15 +/- 0.10), a chin under a beard. Hairline-based ratios are off by default.

QA report: a z-score per ratio. At |z|>2.5 re-check the photos and camera solve; at |z|>3.5 suspect a landmark or lens error. Never auto-correct toward the norm. Warn when sculpting drifts a ratio by more than 2% or 1 mm.
Initialise template warping from the SSM or sex-specific mean scaled by ex-ex and n-gn, then warp with RBF/TPS (the same machinery as Holland's GPA+TPS). Do not use canon-perfect templates.
takeaways: Neoclassical canons fail for most adults in every population tested (Saudi, African American, Turkish n=1,050, Greek, Southeast Asian). The best one, the orbital canon, is met by only about 30%. Use canons as QA checks and block-out guides, never as targets.

The golden ratio has no supporting evidence as a facial ideal (2024 review, Holland 2008, African-Caribbean models). With about 18,000 landmark ratios per face, hundreds land near 1.618 by chance. The engine should contain no phi terms.

Likeness lives in deviations from the average (caricature effect). Pulling a sculpt toward a canon or the mean erases identity, so the 3-5 ratios with the largest z-scores should be locked as protected features.

Definitions change the verdict. Farkas thirds measured from nasion run about 1:1.25 (middle:lower), while thirds measured from the brow are near 1:1. 'Five eyes' fits head breadth, not cheekbone width. Farkas gn is cephalometric soft-tissue menton.

Lens and pose error is larger than canon tolerance. A 35 cm selfie inflates nose/face width by about 20%, and 10 degrees of pitch shifts the projected thirds ratio by about 5-10%. Measure proportions only after the multi-view camera solve and Frankfort-horizontal levelling.
gaps: Farkas 1985 per-canon validity percentages and sample size were not retrieved; the claim that canons held in a minority is from memory plus Al-Sebaei's summary.
No earlier draft existed, so there were no prior verification results to keep.
The 17.1% Malaysian golden-ratio figure is only tentatively attributed to PMC4642949, and the Brazilian null result has no URL.

The full texts of the Turkish 1,050 study, the African American women study (sample size not captured), the Kenyan Indian-descent study and the 2019 Miss Universe study were not read; their canon-by-canon results are missing.
The secondary claim that Farkas advised renewing norms every ~20 years is unverified.
Ethnic shift ranges in Table A (East Asian, African-descent ratios) are author estimates; multi-ethnic 3D ratio norms are not in the library.
Glabella-to-nasion vertical offset and brow-based thirds ratio are estimates and need a measured source.
Original Loomis/Winslow text for eye-line placement was not consulted; tutorials are secondary.
Whether 3D average faces preserve the mean of linear measurements (PMC8192579) was not read.

facs-expressions.title: FACS action units and expression mechanics
facs-expressions.summary:
New note: there was no earlier draft. It is built from the facs-expressions harvest (16 real URLs) plus badged expert knowledge.

It covers:
- FACS definition and lineage, and the AU-count dispute.
- The A–E intensity scale. It is non-interval: C and D are wider. The note adds a suggested mapping to blendshape weights.
- Bilateral scoring and coder rules.
- A 27-row table mapping each AU to its muscles, its surface change (as a sculpt cue) and its ARKit/MediaPipe equivalent.
- The full ARKit-52 name list. Per expert knowledge, MediaPipe's 52 are the same names minus tongueOut, plus `_neutral`.
algorithmic: State: one identity vector β shared across views. Per view: expression ψ_v in [0,1]^K (K = 51–52, ARKit-named), jaw hinge angle θ_v, head pose, camera. Only neutral-tagged views constrain β.
Expression prior: half-normal with σ≈0.05–0.10 plus L1 on neutral views; σ≈0.5 on expression-reference views; cross-view consistency σ≈0.05 for sequential neutral sets. Box bounds [0,1].
Jaw prior on neutral views: θ ~ N(1.5°, 1°²), bounded to [0°, 30°] (derived from a 2–4 mm freeway space at an incisor–condyle radius of ~100 mm). Add condylar translation beyond ~20–25 mm of opening.

Antagonist penalties only for impossible co-activations: eyeBlink vs eyeWide on the same eye, jawLeft vs jawRight, mouthLeft vs mouthRight, eyeLookIn vs eyeLookOut on the same eye. Never penalise AU1+4, AU5+7 or AU12+15.

Expression-aware landmark weights: nasion, pronasale, endocanthion and ear points 1.0; exocanthion 0.7; subnasale and alae 0.6; gonion and menton 0.5 (1.0 once θ is modelled); lips 0.4; brows and cheilion 0.3; lid margins 0.2, dropped when eyeBlink > 0.4.

Neutral QC gate from MediaPipe scores: smile > 0.25, cheekSquint/eyeWide/brow raise > 0.3, browDown > 0.35, eyeBlink > 0.4, jawOpen > 0.08, press/roll/shrug > 0.3 marks the view as non-neutral (heuristic; calibrate).

Template AU basis: each AU is a vertex mask plus a displacement field along the muscle's line of action (e.g. AU12 from the commissure toward the zygoma), used to project expression out of the identity fit. De-expression is a lower-confidence fallback, never a substitute for recapture.
Map FACS letters to weight bands (A 0.05–0.15, B 0.15–0.35, C 0.35–0.65, D 0.65–0.90, E 0.90–1.0), normalised per subject.
takeaways: Fit identity only from views verified as relaxed neutral: no active AUs, lips lightly touching but not pressed, teeth just apart and not clenched, eyes open on a target at lens height, diffuse light so the subject does not squint (AU4/6/7).

A slight AU6+12 smile makes the mouth too wide, the nasolabial fold too deep, the malar area too full and the eyes too narrow. AU25/26 lengthens the lower face and retrudes the chin. AU1/2 raises the brows and shortens the forehead. AU23/24 thins the lips.
FACS intensity A–E is ordinal and non-uniform (C and D are wide), and E is person-relative. ARKit and MediaPipe 0–1 coefficients are uncalibrated against FACS and against each other.
Habitual resting activation (chronic AU4, mentalis strain from lip incompetence) is part of the person's identity and should be sculpted into Basis. Only transient activation must be excluded.

Use ARKit-52 names for Blender shape keys so the rig works with existing mocap. Keep Basis = neutral identity, add a jaw bone for large openings, add corrective keys for non-additive AU combinations, and use AU-driven normal maps for dynamic wrinkles.
One AU is not always one muscle (orbicularis oris covers AU18/22/23/24/28), several AUs are relaxations (AU26, AU43), and anatomy varies (risorius can be absent, zygomaticus major can be bifid).
gaps: There was no earlier draft to merge. All per-AU muscle and surface-deformation detail is expert knowledge and still unverified.
The full ARKit-52 to AU mapping and the ARKit left/right convention are not confirmed from Apple docs, and neither is the MediaPipe category list (the `_neutral` entry, the missing tongueOut).
No quantitative per-AU surface displacement (mm) from 4D scans such as D3DFACS was harvested.
No sources cover the literature on why neutral expression matters for identity (face recognition, ICAO/ISO portrait rules, 3DMM expression-identity disentanglement).
The FLAME, OpenFace and MediaPipe licences and current versions are unverified, and so are the DISFA and FLAME counts.
Jaw kinematics ranges (freeway space, maximum opening, rotation/translation split) are unsourced.
The behaviour of the MediaPipe `_neutral` score, and how reliable blendshape scores are on still, non-frontal photos, are unknown.
Which lid codes (AU41/42/44) the 2002 revision reorganised is unconfirmed.
The UCSD FACS Visual Reference and the Wikipedia AU/muscle table were surfaced but not read.

fat-compartments.title: Facial fat compartments
algorithmic: Soft tissue = template + sum over regions r of w_r(v)·δ_r·n(v), using blurred atlas weights (default 8 mm border), plus an optional tangential descent t_r clamped at ligament anchors.

Latent prior: δ_r = μ_r(sex,age) + a_r·z_adip + b_r·z_age + ε_r, with z ~ N(0,1). Heuristic σ_r in mm: anchors 0.75-1, periorbital 1-1.5, SOOF 2, DMCF 2.5, nasolabial 2-3, cheek 2.5-3, buccal 3-5, jowl 3-4, submental 4-8. Loadings are in the data JSON and must be tuned on scans.

Regularisation: bending weight 1.0 inside a region, 0.1-0.2 across crease seams (tear trough, palpebromalar, midcheek, nasolabial, marionette/prejowl, mandibular border, temporal septum) and about 0.5 across soft borders. Ligament anchors get ARAP stiffness ×2-5 and σ ≤ 1 mm.
Crease depth prior: HalfNormal with scale 0.5-1 mm under 30 years and 2-4 mm over 55. The nasolabial profile is asymmetric (convex on the cheek side, flat on the lip side).

Observability gating: keep DMCF, SOOF and anterior cheek projection at the prior unless a 3/4 view, profile view or reliable normals exist. Buccal and jowl come from the frontal silhouette, submental from the profile.
Expression gating: when AU6 or AU12 is detected, drop the midface, lower-lid and nasolabial residuals, or first fit an expression shape with a superomedial fat shift of about 2-6 mm.
Tag each source as upright or supine and correct supine data before mixing. Flag head pitch below about −10° for jowl and submental. Allow L/R asymmetry with σ_asym ≈ 0.5·σ_r.
takeaways: Facial fat is not one layer. It is split into superficial compartments (above the SMAS) and deep ones (under the muscles, on bone), separated by septa and retaining ligaments. Model the soft tissue per region, not as one global smooth surface.

Aging grooves sit on compartment and ligament borders. The tear trough, palpebromalar and midcheek grooves form a Y; the nasolabial fold is cheek fat overhanging a tethered lip; the prejowl sulcus lies at the DAO / mandibular-ligament border. Sculpt folds as overhangs, never as trenches.

Deep compartments (DMCF, SOOF, temple, ROOF, preaponeurotic fat) deflate with age, while lower superficial ones (nasolabial, jowl, submental) hold their volume or descend. Bone resorption amplifies the grooves.
Weight change acts mostly on submental, jowl, buccal, nasolabial and temple fat. Forehead, nasal dorsum and bony rims barely change and are the reliable anchors.
'Malar fat pad' is a surgical name covering several compartments. Eye bags are postseptal orbital fat, not cheek fat.

Use only relaxed, upright, same-session photos. Smiling (AU6/AU12) moves the cheek fat by an estimated 2-6 mm, a chin-down pose fakes jowls, and supine CT/MRI shows the cheek and jowl fallen back and up.
gaps: There was no harvest and no earlier draft for this topic, so nothing in the note is sourced; every item needs web verification.
No in-vivo, upright, per-compartment volume or thickness norms by age, sex, BMI or ancestry; cadaver samples are small, older and mostly of European ancestry.
SOOF, ROOF and DMCF thicknesses in millimetres were left out because no reliable values were known.
No reliable numbers for lid-cheek junction height or how it changes with age.
How deep compartments are named and divided (medial/lateral DMCF, deep lateral cheek) and how they map onto Mendelson's spaces is unsettled.
Facial effects of GLP-1 drugs are not well quantified, and the topic is time-sensitive.
The prior loadings and sigmas are untested engineering heuristics and need fitting against a 3D scan dataset.

flame-model.title: FLAME head model in depth
flame-model.summary:
I wrote the FLAME note at /home/user/minedesign/research/reconstruction/flame-model.md (about 2,775 words). I also wrote /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/flame-model.json, which has an empty sources list and 19 references by name, and /home/user/minedesign/research/data/flame-model.json with 9 tables: mesh counts, pkl array shapes, parameter ranges, versions and licences, landmark embeddings, component use by downstream methods, Multires face counts, fitting priors and region weights.

Neither input file existed: there was no harvest file and no earlier draft. The note therefore cites no
algorithmic: With every joint rotation at identity, FLAME reduces to v = T̄ + S·β + E·ψ exactly. Let the camera extrinsics carry head pose (global rotation and neck fixed to 0 for stills) so the 3DMM layer is linear inside each levenberg_marquardt or bundle_adjust step, with an analytic Jacobian ∂v/∂β = S. Run full LBS only when the jaw or eyes are free.

Precompute landmark-restricted bases (L×3×K) from barycentric embeddings so fit cost does not depend on the 5,023 vertices. Handle the jaw contour with the yaw-binned dynamic table or with points that slide along the silhouette normal.

Component schedule for sparse landmarks: K_β = 20 → 50 → 100, and all 300 only with dense, silhouette or photometric data. Use K_ψ = 10–20 per view, with a ψ prior of N(0, 0.3²) on neutral-tagged views and N(0, 1) on expressive ones.

Priors: β ~ N(0, 1), flagging |β_i| > 3. Jaw on neutral views σ ≈ 0.035–0.05 rad, with x boxed to [−0.05, 0.6]. Eyes are fitted to iris points only, or given σ 0.3 rad. Neck σ 0.1–0.2 rad in video. Per-vertex offsets after β are Laplacian-regularised and stay under about 3–5 mm.
Gauge: fix either the global pose or the camera extrinsics. Size lives inside β, so add a free scale (σ_log 0.05–0.1) only when there is no metric anchor, and label that output 'proportions only'.
Joint regression must use shape plus expression, as the reference layer does (shapedirs is 400 columns), and must be recomputed after every β update. Otherwise the jaw hinges about a stale pivot.
Take region weights from FLAME_masks.pkl: face 1, ears 0.3–0.5, scalp 0.1, neck 0.1–0.2, and 0 for eyeballs, boundary and mouth interior.

Record the licence as data: commercial_ok=false for FLAME 2017, 2020 and 2023 and 'unknown' for 2023 Open. Load models only from user-supplied paths, and have export refuse without an explicit research flag.

Round-trip from a sculpt: β̂ = argmin ‖S·β − (V − T̄)‖² + λ‖β‖². Store the residual as the likeness layer. Embed the quad delivery template in FLAME once, by barycentric mapping, and push every subject through that map.
takeaways: FLAME is a fitting cage and parameter-interchange format: 5,023 vertices, 9,976 triangles, 300 shape and 100 expression components, and 15 pose values over a root, neck, jaw and two eyes, skinned with plain linear blend skinning. It is not a likeness; ears, the nose tip and asymmetry need offsets or sculpting.

The licence decides the architecture. FLAME 2017, 2020 and 2023 are non-commercial research only. The reported CC BY 4.0 'FLAME 2023 Open' is unverified and is the top item to check before shipping anything derived from FLAME.

Topology carries over between versions but coefficients do not. Store {version, basis hash, K} with every coefficient vector and refuse mismatches; DECA, EMOCA, MICA and SMIRK expect FLAME 2020, while VHAP and GaussianAvatars expect 2023.

In Blender, keep metres at unit scale 1.0. Import OBJ with Forward −Z / Up Y and check for 5,023 vertices. Recompute joint positions after any identity change, freeze the fit as a shape key, and sculpt on a copy with Multires. Remeshing and Dyntopo destroy correspondence.
Convert the chumpy pkl to npz once, outside Blender. Blender's Python 3.11+ cannot import chumpy, and the npz is still licensed data that must not be committed.
gaps: No harvest file and no earlier draft existed for this step, so nothing in the note is URL-cited; all facts are 🧠 or ↔️.
FLAME 2023 Open: its licence text, what it contains (bases, training data, masks, UVs) and its release date.
Whether FLAME 2023 changed the UV layout or the eyeball vertex indices, and what exactly separates the 'with jaw' and 'no jaw' 2023 files.
The current FLAME Blender add-on: version, feature list, number of exposed components, and support for Blender 4.x/5.x.
Official numbers for the FLAME texture space (component count, resolution, training images) and its licence.
The exact size of the FLAME training data (number of registered frames, D3DFACS subject count) and the variance explained per shape component.
Measured average edge lengths and eyeball radius on the FLAME mean template; the current figures are estimates.

forehead-brow-temple-hairline.title: Forehead, brow ridge, temple and hairline
forehead-brow-temple-hairline.summary: Wrote the forehead, brow ridge, temple and hairline note (about 2,690 words of prose before Sources). This topic had no harvest and no earlier draft. The 40 cited URLs therefore come from sibling-topic harvests in research/_raw/harvests (skull-osteology, soft-tissue-thickness, craniometric-landmarks, muscles-upper-face, muscles-mastication-jaw, anthropometric-norms, facial-proportions-canons, facial-asymmetry, facs-expressions). The note and the sources JSON both say so. No URLs were invented. Contents: frontal bone anatomy (the superciliary arch and supraorbital trigone are treated as separat
algorithmic: Add anatomical controls on top of the bone/skin basis: forehead_inclination_deg (Frankfort frame), frontal_curvature, glabella_proj_mm, supraglabellar_break_mm, superciliary_proj_mm, trigone_flatness, eminence_amp_mm and spacing, temporal_crest_sharpness, ft_ratio (forehead width over cheekbone width), temple_fullness_mm, a brow-hair curve and a hairline spline with Norwood stage as a categorical prior.

Suggested priors (expert, to verify): inclination μ 12° men / 8° women, σ 5°; nasofrontal angle μ 125°, σ 7°; glabella_proj μ 5 mm, σ 2.5; supraglabellar break μ 1.5 men / 0.3 women, σ 1; ft_ratio 0.81 ± 0.03; temple_fullness μ 0 ± 3 mm, shifting negative with age over about 50 and low BMI.
Log-normal depth priors: glabella μ 5.3 mm, σ_log 0.15; mid-forehead 5 mm, 0.2; mid-brow 7.5 mm, 0.2; mid-temple 15 mm, 0.35. Males are thicker over the forehead.

Hinge constraints in the Frankfort frame: z(g′) ≥ z(n′) + 1 mm; g′ is the furthest-forward midline point between nasion and trichion; the midline profile above g′ stays convex, except a male dip of at most 3 mm in a band 10–25 mm above g′; the soft supraorbital rim sits ahead of the corneal apex; left/right symmetry sigma about 1.5 mm in the upper face.

Observation weights: profile forehead silhouette σ about 1 mm; frontal temple silhouette only where the face-parsing mask says skin; brow landmarks σ 3–5 mm for bone; hairline excluded from geometry and scale; MediaPipe forehead points σ ≥ 5 mm in-plane with depth ignored.
Solve head tilt jointly with forehead slope and add its uncertainty (about 2–3°) to the reported inclination.
Use hair and hat parsing masks with Tukey or Huber losses. Treat a forehead hidden by a fringe as unobserved and fall back on the prior.
Expression gate: if brow blendshape scores exceed about 0.2–0.3, drop that frame's brow and forehead residuals.
Tag the temporal crest, supraorbital rim, supraglabellar crease and glabella as feature lines on the template, and lower the cotan-Laplacian weights across them so warps keep these plane breaks.
takeaways: The true-profile forehead silhouette (slope, glabella to nasion, the male dip above the brow ridge) sits on about 5 mm of tissue, so it is the most trustworthy depth signal in the upper face. Match it within about 1 mm, but only after levelling the head to the Frankfort plane, because forehead slope changes one-for-one with head tilt.

The temple is a thick, variable stack (fascia, fat pads, temporalis 3.7–16.9 mm on MRI). Its fullness follows age, body fat and clenching more than bone, so sculpt it last from photo shading and capture with the jaw relaxed.

The brow ridge is a medial superciliary arch plus a flat lateral supraorbital trigone. The male pattern (projecting glabella, dip above the ridge, sloped forehead) and the female pattern (frontal eminences, vertical forehead, one convex curve) must not be mixed.

Eyebrows and the hairline are hair: they are groomed, recede and move with expression. Keep them in hair or texture layers, keep them out of scale and bone estimates, and remember that trichion and MediaPipe point 10 are not the same.
Forehead height varies more between ethnic groups than any other classic facial measure, and the equal-thirds canon fails in real samples. Use it as a weak prior, never as a constraint.
Temporalis thickness values disagree between ultrasound and MRI protocols; do not transfer them across imaging methods.
gaps: No dedicated web harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic; every sourced fact is borrowed from sibling-topic harvests.
There are no sourced numbers for forehead inclination, nasofrontal angle, forehead height (tr–n′ or tr–g′), frontal chord/subtense or minimum frontal breadth; all of these are expert recall.
There are no sourced tissue depths for supraglabella, frontal eminence, mid-brow or mid-temple (skin to bone), and no dense depth map for forehead or temple.
There are no quantitative norms for temple fullness by age or BMI, and no validated temple-hollowing scale was retrieved.
Eyebrow position norms (mid-pupil to brow, brow relative to rim by sex) and how brows change with age are unsourced and contested.
Hairline norms (shape distribution, frontotemporal recession depth, prevalence of hair loss by age and ethnicity) and the Hamilton/Norwood, Ludwig and BASP stage definitions are unsourced.
MediaPipe midline indices and blendshape names, and the Blender version for curves-based hair, are recalled from memory and change between releases.
Several cited sources have unconfirmed years or titles, for example the forehead ultrasound paper PMC11635371 and the OAE temporal fossa article.

forensic-reconstruction.title: Forensic facial reconstruction rules (skull to face)
forensic-reconstruction.summary:
I wrote the forensic-reconstruction note (about 2,800 words), its sources JSON and a data JSON. Neither input file existed: there was no harvest and no earlier draft. So the note has no URLs and every claim carries 🧠 (54 badges) or ↔️ (30). I cross-referenced sibling notes that do have sourced material, by file path only: skull-osteology.md, eyes-modeling-blender.md, ear.md and mouth-lips-teeth.md.

The note covers:
- The Gerasimov, American, Manchester and computerized template-warping methods, plus craniofacial superimposition as the closest forensic counterpart to the camera solve.
- Eye ru
algorithmic: Encode the rules as factors in a factor graph between bone landmarks, soft landmarks and hidden parts (eyes, teeth), weighted 1/σ². Photo reprojection residuals are separate factors, so with honest σ the observations dominate without manual switching.

Interval constraints in the superimposition style: (s − b)·n̂ within the log-normal tissue-depth prior (from skull-osteology.json), with tangential slack τ ≈ 2–4 mm for points that slide, such as gnathion, menton and gonion.

Suggested priors in mm, Frankfort-aligned frame: cornea_ahead_lat_rim N(16, 2), with ancestry shifts of +1.75 and −1.5, clamped to 11–22; hertel_lr_diff N(0, 1), warn above 2; globe_axial_len N(23.8, 1); corneal_diam N(11.8, 0.7) as a low-weight scale prior; en_lat_of_dacryon N(5, 1.5); ex_med_of_ectoconchion N(4, 1.5); ex_below_fz_suture N(10, 3).

alar_minus_aperture N(10/13/16, 3) by ancestry mixture; icw_over_mouth_width N(0.75, 0.05); stomion_above_U1_edge N(2.5/1.5/0.5, 1.5) by age band (<30, 30–50, >50); tragion_lat_of_porion N(11, 3) with vertical N(0, 5); tip projection from bone only as a σ ≥ 5 mm fallback when there is no profile view.
Expose sex, age, BMI and a soft ancestry mixture, defaulting to pooled values. Ask the user rather than infer ancestry from photos.
Avoid double-counting: when the skin already carries a PCA/3DMM prior, apply forensic rules only between hidden layers and skin.
Blender QA: Manchester-style tissue-depth pegs as Empties along bone normals, checked with a Raycast in Geometry Nodes and coloured by z-score; flag beyond 2σ rather than auto-fixing.
Evaluate per region (forehead, orbit, nose, lips, chin, cheeks, ears) plus endocanthion, exocanthion, pronasale and cheilion landmark errors, not a single RMS.
takeaways: Forensic rules predict skin from bone with errors of about 2–5 mm, and the worst errors are at the nose tip, lips, eyelids and ears. In photo-based work, photo evidence must always win; the rules are weak priors only for hidden structures and for directions no view constrains.

Place eyeballs by the Hertel-style rule (corneal apex about 16 mm in front of the lateral orbital rim, range 12–20, higher on average in African ancestry), never by the old supra/infra-orbital tangent rule, which sets eyes too deep.

The nasal dorsum follows the nasal bones within about 1 mm (rhinion cover is about 2–3.5 mm). The tip, alae and columella are poorly predicted by any rule (two-tangent, 3 × nasal spine, regressions), so take them from the photos.

Mouth width ≈ inter-canine width / 0.75, and resting mouth corners sit over the first premolars. At rest, upper incisal edges sit about 1–4 mm below stomion in young adults, falling toward 0 by the 60s. Use these to size and place a hidden teeth mesh.
Tragion sits about 8–14 mm lateral of porion, near Frankfort height. Ear length is typically 5–12 mm more than nose height, so 'ear length = nose length' is a myth.

Craniofacial superimposition (overlaying a skull on a photo by camera-pose solving with soft-tissue intervals) is the forensic method that transfers most directly to the project's multi-view fitting engine.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed, so no claim in this note is sourced. Everything is 🧠 or ↔️ pending verification.
The exact regression formulas and prediction errors of Rynn, Wilkinson & Peters 2010 (nose from skull) were not available.
The direction and size of the globe offset within the orbit (Stephan & Davidson 2008 versus Guyomarc'h et al. 2012) are unconfirmed.
The inter-canine width definition in the 75 % rule is unconfirmed.
The exact accuracy figures of the Manchester-method CT validations (2006, 2012, 2014) and of the automated methods are recalled only as ranges.
Tragion–porion offsets in three dimensions lack a source; the current values are derived from biporion versus bitragion breadths and canal anatomy.
Ancestry-specific alar-width offsets beyond European-descent samples are uncertain.
The current status and licence of OrtogOnBlender and of FreeForm (3D Systems) in 2026 are unknown.

generative-3d-heads.title: Generative / large reconstruction models for heads (2024-2026)
generative-3d-heads.summary:
I wrote the note on generative and large-reconstruction 3D head models from scratch, because there was no harvest file for this topic and no earlier draft. Most of it is my own expert knowledge, labelled 🧠 or ↔️. The 11 📄 facts come from 7 real URLs that I cross-cited from other harvest files in this library: KaoLRM, MICA, "Towards Realistic Generative 3D Face Models", the InsightFace model zoo, Sridhar 2025 on proportions in generative AI, GAF and Sapiens.

The note sorts the models into four families:
- feed-forward reconstruction models (LRM, TripoSR, InstantMesh, SF3D);
- native 3D latent
algorithmic: Backend contract: generate(image, seed) returns a GLB plus metadata (model, weights SHA, licence id, commercial_ok, territory_ok, cloud_upload, crop box). Weights are never bundled; each backend runs in its own venv or subprocess. The generator term is off by default in likeness mode and on in blockout mode.

Seed ensemble: use 4-8 seeds per photo and 2-3 photos. Align each output to the template and take closest-point correspondences to get a per-vertex mean and spread s_v. Set sigma_v^2 = sigma_region^2 + s_v^2, and drop vertices with s_v > 5 mm.

Depth-weighted residual: split r = x - mu_v into in-plane and along-view-axis parts with separate sigmas. Defaults: frontal skin 2-3 mm in-plane / 4-6 mm depth; nose and chin 2-3 / 6-10 mm; lateral face 4-6 / 8-12 mm; occiput silhouette only (>=15 mm); eyes, lids, mouth interior, nostrils, ears and hair off. Use a Geman-McClure kernel with c = 2 sigma.

Hierarchy: photo landmarks (sigma 0.02-0.03 IOD) and silhouettes rank above anatomical priors, which rank above the generator term. Cap the generator's information per region at about 25% of the landmark information.

Gates: disable a region when the generator's depth at glabella, pronasale, subnasale or pogonion is more than 3 sigma from the triangulated point. Double sigma_depth when the conditioning photo has f35 < 35 mm. Never mirror generator data, and halve its weight where photo-measured asymmetry exceeds 2 mm.

Discard the generator's scale, pose and implied camera. Scale comes from the metric solve, or else an IPD prior of 63 +/- 3.5 mm. Synthetic views (diffusion outputs, GAN renders) never feed landmark detection or camera solving; as silhouettes they get weight <= 0.25 and a synthetic tag.

Prefer the parametric route: a reconstruction model that regresses FLAME (KaoLRM-style) supplies an initial beta with sigma about 1. A free-surface generator is only a weak data term. A head-GAN completion is a back-of-head silhouette at sigma >= 10 mm.
Store provenance as Blender custom properties (model, version, seed, licence, commercial_ok, cloud_uploaded, consent_id), plus per-vertex ai_prior_weight and confidence for sculpt masks.
takeaways: Generic image-to-3D models give a plausible head but no likeness. Identity mostly rides on the projected texture. Depth (nose and chin projection, orbits, occiput), eyes, lips, ears and hair are invented, and outputs regress toward the mean and toward symmetry.

There is no published millimetre benchmark for these models on real faces. The bar is concrete: the scaled average FLAME face already scores 1.53 mm mean on NoW and MICA about 0.9 mm median, so a generated region adds information only where it beats about 1.5 mm.

The field's own fix for faces is to re-impose a 3DMM: KaoLRM regresses FLAME parameters from a pre-trained reconstruction model. Corresponded, near-metric parametric output is worth more to a fitting engine than a free-form surface.
EG3D and PanoHead show 512^2 detail that comes from 2D super-resolution of a 128^2 render, not from 3D density. 360-degree head GANs synthesise the back of the head from dataset statistics.

Identity-guided generators (Arc2Avatar, ID-to-3D) optimise ArcFace recognisability, which texture can satisfy. A high ArcFace score is not a 3D likeness, so the identity check must also run on untextured (matcap) renders.

Licences vary widely: MIT (TRELLIS, TripoSR, TripoSG), Apache-2.0 (InstantMesh, Step1X-3D), territory-restricted (Hunyuan3D excludes the EU, UK and South Korea), and non-commercial (EG3D, FFHQ-trained head GANs, InsightFace-based tools). Uploading a face to a hosted service means handling biometric data.
gaps: No topic harvest or earlier draft existed. Every architecture, resolution, version and licence detail is unverified expert knowledge, and the 7 cited URLs are cross-cited from other topic harvests.
There is no measured millimetre accuracy for any generic generator or head GAN on real faces. The Table 2 generator rows and the Table 5 sigmas are author estimates.
Licences for PanoHead, SphereHead, FaceLift, Arc2Avatar, Arc2Face and TRELLIS.2 are unconfirmed, and so are Hunyuan's current territory terms and vendor free-tier output rights.

Late-2025 to 2026 hosted model versions (Hunyuan3D 3.x, Rodin Gen-2, Tripo 3.x, Meshy 6) and their resolution claims are unverified. Hosted prices are given only as a range (about US$10-30/month entry tiers).
Venues and years for FaceLift, ID-to-3D and Arc2Avatar need checking, as does the effective date of EU AI Act transparency duties (stated as August 2026).

hair-blender.title: Hair in Blender for head reconstructions
hair-blender.summary:
I wrote the hair note from expert knowledge only. Neither input existed: no harvest at /home/user/minedesign/research/_raw/harvests/hair-blender.json and no earlier draft at /home/user/minedesign/research/blender/hair-blender.md. So the note cites no URLs, and every item carries a 🧠 or ↔️ badge (0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 96 🧠 / 29 ↔️), all queued for web verification.

The note covers:
- **Curves hair system (3.3+):** how the data is stored, UV-based root attachment, the rest-position requirement for deforming with shape keys and armatures, the sculpt brushes, and the Python API, with a fallback for older v
algorithmic: Layered model: skin/skull S, a hair envelope H (offset field over the scalp) and strands. Hair, brow and beard pixels are excluded from the skin silhouette, photometric and contour terms.

Containment: the signed distance from each scalp vertex to the hair-mask visual hull must be ≤ −t_min (2 mm with hair, 0 bald), as a hinge penalty. The envelope offset gets a log-normal prior by hair class (bald 1±1, short 10±5, medium 20±10, long 15±8, curly 60±30 mm).
Hairline: a HairUV polyline with the trichion plus 8–12 control points per side. Priors are trichion to glabella 60±10 mm and left–right mirror deviation σ 3 mm; observations have σ ≈ 2 px.

Flow field: a smoothest tangent field on the scalp (Knöppel et al. 2013, or harmonic interpolation in local frames). Constraints are hairline directions from a Gabor/steerable bank (16–36 orientations, 4–8 px wavelength), mesh cuts at the parting, whorls as index +1 singularities with a 20–45° spiral, and gravity.

Guide growth: RK2 with 2–3 mm steps. Elevation priors are 15±10° at the hairline and 37±10° at the crown. Guides are projected into H via its SDF, stopped at the photo tip length and resampled. Children use Poisson-disc sampling with a recorded seed.

Brow generator: zones head/body/tail at 0–15 / 15–70 / 70–100 % of brow length. Directions are +60…+90 / 0…+20 (lower rows 0…−15) / −10…−40° with σ 10°; lift 5–20°, length 4–12 mm. Brow landmark σ is 3–5 mm for the skull fit and 1–2 mm for placement.

Lash generator: built from the lid-margin edge with a 5–7 mm punctal skip, upper 90–160 lashes at 8–12 mm, lower 50–80 at 6–8 mm, curl 30–60°, clumps of 3–6, and at least 0.2 mm clearance from the cornea.

After a warp: snap_curves_to_surface(DEFORM), then Restore Curve Segment Length, then Shrinkwrap. Store hairline, parting, whorls, melanin, curl and seeds in a sidecar JSON. Check for Curves.add_curves at runtime and fall back to a polyline mesh plus Mesh to Curve; run ML strand models out of process because of their licences.
takeaways: Use the Curves object (3.3+) with the geometry-nodes hair assets (3.5+) for scalp hair, brows and lashes. Give the scalp its own non-overlapping 'HairUV' map and turn on Add Rest Position, or roots will not follow shape keys or template warps.

Fit skin and skull under the hair from priors and the hair-back photo set. Take only the hair envelope, hairline, parting, whorl, flow and tip lengths from the photos. A head size that fits the hair outline usually means a shrunken or enlarged cranium.
Brow landmarks from dlib and MediaPipe mark hair, not bone: give them a loose σ of 3–5 mm in the skull fit, and use them tightly only for placing brow hair.

Match hair colour with Melanin and Melanin Redness by rendering a swatch under the matched light rig, never with an eyedropper. Make grey hair a per-strand mix, and give blond hair many more light bounces.

Realism comes from clumping, length variation and an irregular 3–10 mm hairline transition zone more than from strand count. Shrinkwrap Hair Curves and Part by Mesh Islands stop strands going through the head and across the parting.
Re-snap roots, restore segment lengths and re-run Shrinkwrap after every template warp, and never remesh a surface that carries hair.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed, so nothing in the note is sourced (0 ✅ / 0 📄); every claim needs web verification.
The exact Curves Python API and its version history, plus any 5.0–5.3 changes to Curves, edit-mode tools and hair asset names.
Principled Hair BSDF defaults and whether EEVEE supports the Huang model in the 5.x versions.
Alembic and USD curve export attributes for Unreal grooms, and whether a hair-dynamics node asset ships with Blender.
Primary population data for brow hair count and density, brow position against the supraorbital rim, whorl location and handedness, and lash lift and curl angles by ancestry.
Measured curl diameters per curl class (De La Mettrie et al. 2007) to replace the practice values in Table F.
Current licences of hair segmentation models and strand-reconstruction code and weights, and of the commercial Hair Tool add-on.

hair-eyes-teeth-recon.title: Reconstructing hair, eyes and teeth from images
hair-eyes-teeth-recon.summary:
Wrote the note on reconstructing hair, eyes and teeth from photos (about 2,800 words), plus its sources JSON (no URLs; 43 references named) and a data JSON with 10 tables. Neither input existed: there was no harvest and no earlier draft. So no URL is cited, and every claim carries 🧠 or ↔️. Where the eye and teeth numbers match sibling notes that have sources, the note links to those notes with "(lib: …)" markers.

The recommended approach is model-based for all three:
- **Eyes:** a fixed-size eye with gaze solved per photo, fitted to the edges of the iris; strabismus is flagged.
- **Teeth:** a
algorithmic: Eye sub-model, per subject: eye centres c_L and c_R in the head frame. Priors: mirror symmetry σ 1 mm, IPD 63 ± 3.8 mm, corneal apex 16 ± 2.5 mm ahead of the lateral orbital rim. Globe and cornea are fixed; HVID (11.8, σ 0.6) is freed only with 3 or more sharp views.

Eye sub-model, per view: yaw and pitch for each eye. Gaze prior by capture tag: into the lens (camera direction + 5° kappa, σ 3°), fixed mark (shared across views, σ 1°), untagged (σ 15°). Vergence coupling σ 1°. Flag strabismus when the residual exceeds 3° in 2 or more views, then decouple that eye.

Iris-edge residual: point-to-projected-circle distance on samples from the left and right arcs, σ 0.5–1 px. MediaPipe iris centre σ = 0.05 × iris diameter in px. Drop samples within 1 px of a lid edge. Resolve the two-fold circle-pose ambiguity by agreement across views.
Lid–gaze coupling: expected upper-margin shift = g·Δpitch·12 mm·π/180, with g ~ N(0.8, 0.2²). Hard constraint: the lid margin stays 0–0.3 mm off the eye surface.

Teeth sub-model: upper teeth rigid to the skull, lower teeth on the FLAME jaw pose. Priors: intercanine width 35 ± 2 mm, intermolar width 53 ± 3, front arch depth 9 ± 1, per-tooth width σ 0.5 (lateral incisors 0.7), incisal edge 2.5 ± 1.5 mm below stomion at rest, overjet 2.5 ± 1, overbite 2.5 ± 1.5, proclination σ 5°, dental midline offset σ 1.5 mm.

Teeth residuals: incisal-edge polyline, gaps between teeth and gum margin (σ 1–2 px), plus teeth-mask IoU from a parser that has teeth classes (Sapiens, not CelebAMask-HQ). The inner lip surface stays at least 0.5 mm outside the enamel. Scan path: similarity transform, then trimmed ICP, never rescaling beyond unit conversion.

Hair interface: the skull is constrained only from outside under hair (scalp signed distance to the hair hull ≤ −2 mm when hair is visible, 0 when bald), with a log-normal offset prior by hair class. A strand plug-in runs in a separate process and exchanges polylines only.

Strand acceptance gates: roots within 1 mm of the scalp after snapping; zero head penetrations; per-view hair-mask IoU ≥ 0.85; median orientation error ≤ 20° where confidence > 0.5. On failure, fall back to Tier 0. Choose guides by farthest-point sampling on root UV plus 3–5 shape PCA coefficients.

Strand import adapter: read PLY, NPZ or USC .data; convert units and Y-up to Z-up; align to the scalp with similarity ICP; build Curves, snap roots and resample. Write a sidecar JSON with eye centres, HVID, per-view gaze, the strabismus flag, arch parameters, tooth widths, the scan transform, the hair tier and gate scores.
takeaways: Never fit hair, eyes or teeth as skin. Mask all three out of the skin, silhouette, photometric and depth terms, and give each its own sub-model and exported object.

Hair from photos is reliable only at its outer layer: outline, 2D strand direction, hairline, parting and whorl (crown spiral). Every method invents the interior strands, and strand accuracy is scored on synthetic grooms or CT-scanned wigs, never on real people.

Practical hair tiers: Tier 0 (always) is a procedural groom driven by the photos. Tier 1 is a single-image strand prior (DiffLocks or HairStep class) used as a starting volume. Tier 2 is phone-video strand optimisation (GaussianHaircut, Neural Haircut, MonoHair): hours on a CUDA GPU, decimated to 500–3000 guide curves and re-combed by hand.
Eyes: keep the eyeball size fixed by priors and solve gaze for each photo. Log whether the subject looked into the lens. Model convergence: 3.6° per eye at 0.5 m, 6° at 0.3 m.

Near a frontal view, the shape of the iris ellipse carries almost no gaze information (cos 10° = 0.985). Use the iris centre's offset from the head-fixed eyeball centre instead, and fit only the left and right arcs of the iris edge.
A 3° gaze error moves the iris edge about 0.6 mm, which reads as a change in lid height. Solve gaze before sculpting lid coverage.
Glasses scale the apparent eye by about 1.2 % per dioptre, and coloured contacts fake the iris edge. Strabismus (2–4 %) and anisocoria (about 20 %) are normal variation, not fitting errors.

Teeth: the best source is the consenting person's existing intraoral scan, registered with 4–6 point pairs. Otherwise build an arch of per-tooth templates sized from the measured central incisor. Keep the upper teeth rigid to the skull and the lower teeth on the jaw joint.
Iris textures are biometric data and dental scans are health data. Keep both local, opt-in and deletable, even with consent.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed, so there are zero URL-cited sources. Every fact is 🧠 or ↔️, and the eye and teeth figures rely on sibling notes for sourcing.
2025–26 strand-reconstruction methods are low-confidence recall (Im2Haircut, TANGLED, StrandHead, SimAvatar, Digital Salon); 2026 conference programmes were not reviewed.
Licences, runtimes and GPU memory needs of Neural Haircut, GaussianHaircut, MonoHair, Dr.Hair, DiffLocks, Perm and HAAR are unverified.
There is no benchmark for strand accuracy on real people; reported metrics are synthetic only.
The upper-lid gain against vertical gaze, and how it varies with age, needs a primary clinical source.
Tooth-width and arch-width tables by ancestry and sex are missing; Wheeler averages are recalled, not checked.
Not established whether a permissively licensed statistical teeth model exists; TeethDreamer (MICCAI 2024) is unverified.
How Blender 5.x imports Alembic/USD curves into Curves objects, and the exact strand file formats each research repo outputs, are unverified.
Gaze-network error figures and the MediaPipe Iris depth-error claim need checking against the original papers.

identity-embeddings.title: Face recognition embeddings as identity signals
identity-embeddings.summary:
I rewrote the identity-embeddings note, about 2,800 words not counting the sources list. It keeps every sourced fact, citation [1]-[10] and verification result from the earlier draft. Its old ⚠️ marks now use the 📄/✅ badges, and the notes about the search budget running out are gone.

- **MICA correction:** the "MICA uses an ArcFace identity loss" premise is wrong. MICA uses ArcFace as a mostly frozen identity encoder and trains with a masked 3D geometry loss. The true identity-loss lineage is Genova 2018, Deng 2019, GANFIT and DECA.
- **Expert knowledge added (🧠):**
  - the ArcFace loss form
algorithmic: Split into IdentityScorer (ONNX, no gradients: evaluation and stopping), IdentityPrior (MICA-type embedding-to-FLAME regressor) and IdentityLoss (optional, off by default). Never call the scorer a loss.

MICA prior: centre at the coordinate-wise median of per-photo beta, sigma_k = max(1.4826*MAD_k, sigma_floor), with sigma_floor 0.5 for the first 20-50 components and 1.0 beyond (FLAME coefficients in SD units). This is a heuristic to tune on held-out scans.

Optional IdentityLoss: hinge max(0, tau - cos)^2 computed only on clay renders with generic eyes and brows, over random augmentations (shift 2 px, scale 3%, roll 3 deg) and at least 2 recognisers. Set tau to the post-landmark score + 0.05, capped at the genuine ceiling; limit it to 10-20% of total energy; reject steps that raise landmark RMS by more than 0.5 px or leave the 3-sigma prior.
No ONNX gradients are available in Blender, so optimise 50 or fewer shape coefficients with SPSA or CMA-ES. Stop on the impostor z-score from a held-out recogniser, not the one being optimised.

Per-model config read from the ONNX graph: sha256, licence, embedding_dim, input_shape, mean/std (detect leading Sub/Mul nodes), 5-point template, metric cosine, threshold null until calibrated, flip_tta false.

Per-view diagnostics: detector keypoint drift above 3 px in the 112 crop flags the misplaced feature for landmark fitting. A cosine spread above 0.1 across views flags a pose or camera error rather than shape.
Scale is never inferred from the embedding; it comes from the camera solve or anthropometric priors.
takeaways: MICA uses ArcFace as a mostly frozen identity encoder (only the last 3 ResNet blocks are fine-tuned) and trains with a masked 3D geometry loss, not an ArcFace identity loss. Identity losses belong to Genova 2018, Deng 2019, GANFIT and DECA.
Use the embedding as a likeness scorecard, not as a metric check. It is blind to scale (similarity alignment), weak on depth, ears and cranium, and driven by texture, eyes and brows.
Separate texture from geometry with a 2x2 render control (sculpt or mean head, subject texture or clay). Geometry's contribution is the clay sculpt score minus the clay mean-head score.

There is no portable threshold: 0.5 [9], 0.363 (OpenCV SFace) and about 0.32-0.36 (deepface ArcFace) all differ. Calibrate per subject with a genuine ceiling from the subject's own photos and demographically matched impostors, and report ceiling ratio, impostor z-score and rank.
Apply the photo's own 5-point warp to its pixel-registered render. Render with the Standard view transform and never flip-average, because flipping hides asymmetry.

Do not bundle the buffalo_l weights: they are reportedly non-commercial and mirrors are unofficial. Pin SHA-256 hashes, keep embeddings in memory only, and require a consent checkbox. Embeddings can be inverted into recognisable faces.
gaps: No study found that measures how much ArcFace similarity on 3D renders comes from texture versus geometry.
Official InsightFace model licence text and SHA-256 hashes of the buffalo_l files are not confirmed.
ArcFace paper benchmark tables (LFW 99.83, IJB-C) and buffalo_l zoo accuracy columns were not checked.
Successor models (AdaFace, MagFace, TransFace, ViT recognisers): ONNX availability and licences not searched.
Demographic-bias evidence (NIST FRTE updates after NISTIR 8280) and how to calibrate impostor sets for under-represented groups.
Identity-similarity metrics used in DECA/EMOCA-style evaluations; DECA's exact identity-loss network and weight not verified.
Legal status of computing face embeddings for consented avatar creation (GDPR household exemption, BIPA, EU AI Act changes in 2025-26).
Whether a 3D (depth or normal-map) recogniser could serve as a geometry-only likeness scorer.

import-export-scans.title: Importing scans and reconstructions into Blender
import-export-scans.summary: Wrote the import/export-of-scans note from scratch: the topic harvest and the earlier draft were both missing, so the old-draft facts and verification results had nothing to carry over. The note covers OBJ, PLY, STL, FBX, glTF, USD and Alembic import in Blender 4.x–5.x, units, axis and handedness conventions (FLAME is Y-up, Blender is Z-up), colour attributes, scan cleaning, decimation and remeshing, and Wrap/NICP-style template fitting inside Blender (Shrinkwrap, Surface Deform, Laplacian Deform, Multires Reshape). The body runs to about 2,800 words, plus a source list; its 24 cited URLs are
algorithmic: ImportRecord sidecar per mesh: format, file hash, declared and inferred units, 3x3 axis matrix, reflection flag, similarity s/R/t, vertex count, vertex-order checksum.
Unit inference: choose u in {1e-6,1e-3,1e-2,1e-1,1} minimising |log(d*u/d_ref)| on intercanthal or exocanthion distance; accept within ±30%, else flag.
Orientation: build a head frame from eyes, nose tip and chin; run Umeyama with det(R)=+1 and with reflection allowed; flag 'mirrored source' if reflected RMS < 0.5 × proper RMS; never auto-flip.
Log-normal scale prior sigma by source: clinical/structured light 0.5–1%, phone LiDAR 2–3%, metrical regressor (MICA) ~3%, non-metric regressor 5–7% around the population mean, SfM free.
Rigid gate after 7-landmark alignment (NoW-style): RMS 2–5 mm is normal; above 10 mm, treat landmarks or axes as wrong.

NICP: stiffness schedule {100,50,20,10,5,2,1} normalised by mean edge length; landmark weight 1→0.05; 3–10 iterations per stage; reject pairs beyond max(3·MAD, 5 mm), with normal angle > 60°, or landing on scan boundaries.
Region weights: eyeballs, mouth and nostril interiors 0; hair-covered scalp 0.1; ears 0.3–0.5; face 1 (FLAME-style vertex masks).
Own NumPy OBJ/PLY readers guarantee vertex order; inside Blender use foreach_get (float32), then solve in float64; spatial queries via mathutils BVHTree/KDTree because SciPy is not bundled.
Output the fit as a 'likeness' shape key (from_mix=False); store colour as a linear Float attribute on the Point domain; round-trip export tolerance 2 µm.
Load user-supplied FLAME/BFM files rather than bundling them; MPFB code is GPL, its assets CC0/CC-BY.
takeaways: Treat every scan or 3DMM import as an unknown similarity transform plus a possible reflection. Infer units from one face distance: intercanthal width spans only about 31–41 mm across populations, while candidate units are 10x or more apart. Record s, R, t and a reflection flag in a sidecar file rather than trusting importer defaults.

Vertex order survives single-mesh OBJ, PLY, FBX, USD and Alembic imports, but not glTF, whose seam splits change the vertex count. Use OBJ or PLY, or the engine's own NumPy parsers, for anything that carries template correspondence.

Apply object scale and rotation immediately after import. Voxel size, merge distance, Shrinkwrap limit and bake distances are local-space values, so an unapplied scale of 0.001 multiplies all of them by 1000.
A mirrored face still looks like a face but flips every asymmetry (healthy asymmetry is about 0.8 mm RMS). Test proper vs reflected Umeyama fits and check against an unflipped photo.
Scanned hair is a shell over the scalp: down-weight it to about 0.1. Voxel remesh does not fill holes in an open scan; it turns them into a double-walled shell. Fill and fair the holes first.

Shrinkwrap is a per-vertex projection with no regulariser. Use a landmark warp (TPS or Laplacian Deform), then NICP with decreasing stiffness, then a short-range Shrinkwrap (Limit 2–5 mm), with Multires Reshape for detail.

Clinical 3D surface imaging agrees with direct measurement to about 0.2 mm, and most differences are under 2 mm. Automatic template registration reaches under 2 mm for only about 53% of landmarks, so don't claim better than the reference modality.
gaps: This topic's own harvest and earlier draft did not exist. All URLs are borrowed from sibling harvests, and no first-party Blender manual page about the importers themselves is in the library.
The FLAME frame and units, the BFM 2009/2017 units and the MediaPipe canonical units are unverified expert knowledge.
No source confirms whether the Blender 5.x OBJ importer preserves vertex order under every option, or which glTF Merge Vertices behaviour 5.x has.
USD/USDZ import handling of metersPerUnit and upAxis in 5.x is unverified, as is whether PLY import reads custom vertex properties.
Native Gaussian-splat (3DGS PLY) import or rendering status in Blender 5.x is unknown.
R3DS Wrap / Faceform naming, licence and pricing are time-sensitive and unverified.
There are no benchmarks for Surface Deform or Shrinkwrap performance on scan targets of 1M+ triangles, or for BVHTree query cost per call.
Default engine priors (NICP schedule, rejection thresholds, scale sigmas) are expert defaults and have not been tuned on data.

instagram-social-sculptors.title: Instagram and social media sculptors' tips
instagram-social-sculptors.summary:
I rewrote the note (about 2,800 words), the sources file and a new data file. The harvest reached only five Instagram profile pages, whose snippets were bios with no technique. Those are the note's only sourced facts: 4 📄 bullets, with @cooleblumen excluded as off-topic. Everything else is expert knowledge, badged 🧠 (51) or ↔️ (15), with 0 ✅.

The expert content covers:
- the advice portrait sculptors repeat (big-to-small blocking, comparing silhouettes from many angles, mirror and flip checks, blink comparison, longer lens from further away, caliper trilateration from fixed points, when to tu
algorithmic: Coarse-to-fine schedule mirroring 'big to small'. Stage A: pose, scale and focal from 6-10 landmarks plus silhouette. Stage B: RBF template warp with landmark prior sigma 8 mm. Stage C: laplacian_deform with prior sigma relaxed to 3-4 mm and more silhouette weight. Stage D: local refinement only where at least 2 views agree.
Scale priors: IPD ~ N(63, 4) mm as fallback; iris diameter ~ N(11.7, 0.5) mm per eye when the iris is at least 20 px; a user ruler or caliper overrides both.
Per-photo distance estimate d = f_px*IPD_mm/ipd_px; warn when d < 1.0 m, reject as a shape cue when d < 0.6 m, flag photos whose d exceeds 1.5x the set median.

Focal policy: keep the log-normal focal prior (sigma_log 0.35) and the f35 hypotheses 24-200 mm; for near-frontal views with d > 1 m, tie focal and distance through the IPD prior instead of trusting free focal.
Symmetry sigma schedule: about 1 mm in stages A/B, relaxing to 2 mm or looser in C/D; strong symmetry pull only in occluded regions.
Caliper constraints: residual (||X_i - X_j|| - m)/sigma with sigma 1-2 mm; trilateration from fixed triplets (both tragi plus nasion).
Eye placement prior: corneal apex N(16, 2) mm anterior to the lateral orbital rim; eyeball sphere 24 mm.
Silhouette energy: per-view mask IoU with hair segmented out; the highest weights go to the profile silhouette and midline landmarks.
Optional caricature control X' = mu + (1+k)(X - mu), k in [0, 0.15], default 0, preview only.
Diagnostics returned by the solver: per-view IoU and per-region mismatch, per-landmark reprojection error sorted worst first, per-photo d and f35, left/right asymmetry vector.
Claim registry: social-only tips may drive UI hints and become priors only with non-social corroboration.
takeaways: The only sourced material is five Instagram profile bios; no post captions, reels or TikTok, X or Threads content was harvested, so every technique claim is unverified expert knowledge.

Social sculptors' recurring checks each have an exact engine counterpart: silhouette comparison by profiles becomes per-view mask IoU through matched cameras; mirror and blink checks become flip and toggle operators; calipers from fixed points become distance residuals and trilateration.

Perspective depends only on camera distance: at 0.3 m the nose is magnified about 1.33x relative to the ears, against about 1.05x at 2 m. The tool should estimate distance per photo (d about f_px*IPD/ipd_px), warn below 1.0 m and reject selfies below 0.6 m as shape cues.
Use matched cameras rather than orthographic front and side planes. Blender's default 50 mm camera and viewport lens rarely match phone photos (about 24-28 mm equivalent).
Proportion canons (eyes at half, thirds, five eyes, ear = nose) are blocking scaffolds; measured adults often deviate (Farkas), so they must not be hard fitting targets.

Shape priors shrink toward the mean and cause the 'generic' look; an opt-in caricature slider X' = mu + (1+k)(X - mu), k in 0 to 0.15, mirrors the sculptors' 'push it slightly' advice (contested for realistic 3D).
Reference hygiene matters as much as sculpting: one age and weight window, no glasses, teeth lightly together, camera at eye height, 8-16 yaw views plus elevation views, and a scale reference.
gaps: No post-level content (captions, reel transcripts, threads) from any named portrait sculptor has been retrieved; TikTok, X and Threads have no sources at all.
None of the named artists (Faraut, Kazu Hiro, Grassetti, Longhi, Skutt, Diba, Munoz Gomez, Zarins, Eaton, Kaspar, Dobarro, YanSculpts) has a verified piece of advice attributed to them.
All anthropometric ranges (IPD, iris, Hertel, ear and nose lengths, head height) are expert knowledge and need checking against the library's anatomy notes and primary sources.

Blender specifics need testing on the current version: no native viewport flip (the scale.x = -1 camera or Image Editor flip workaround), the sculpt X-mirror default, and the brush Radius Unit option.
Status, licence and price of fSpy, KeenTools FaceBuilder and PureRef are time-sensitive and unverified.
There is no evidence on whether 3D caricature, or any specific social-media likeness check, measurably improves rated likeness.

jaw-chin-neck.title: Mandible, chin and neck
jaw-chin-neck.summary:
Neither input existed: there was no harvest file and no earlier draft for jaw-chin-neck. The note is therefore written entirely from expert knowledge and cites no URLs. Every claim is badged 🧠 (51) or ↔️ (21), and none is ✅ or 📄. Values that overlap with sibling notes are pointed to those notes (skull-osteology, muscles-mastication-jaw, muscles-lower-face, craniometric-landmarks, facial-asymmetry), where they are sourced. The bone priors match the existing muscles-mastication-jaw priors: gonial N(122,7) and bigonial M 97 / F 90 mm.

The note covers:
- mandible variation and the vertical-patter
algorithmic: Parameter set. Bone: gonial angle, ramus height, bony bigonial width, mandibular-plane angle, chin projection relative to the N'-perpendicular, chin height, chin width, squareness, midline deviation. Soft tissue: t_pog, t_me, submental fat, jowl, gland ptosis. Neck: hyoid height and AP position, circumference, SCM, larynx prominence. Per photo: head-neck pitch, yaw and roll, plus jaw rotation and protrusion.

Latent vertical pattern z_v ~ N(0,1) coupling gonial angle +5 deg/z, MP +5 deg/z, chin projection -3 mm/z, lower-face height +3.5 mm/z and CMA +4 deg/z, with residual noise. These are heuristic coefficients to tune.

Priors: gonial M N(120,6), F N(124,6), unknown N(122,7), bounded 105-145. Bigonial bone M N(97,6), F N(90,5) mm. Ramus M N(60,5), F N(54,4) mm. t_pog lognormal(11.5 mm, 0.20). t_me lognormal(7.5 mm, 0.25). Convexity N(12,5). Lower lip to E-line N(-2,2.5). CMA N(118,12) in canonical pose. Lower-face-throat N(100,8). Submental fat lognormal(5 mm, 0.5). Larynx Beta(4,2) M, Beta(1.5,6) F. Neck circumference M N(39.5,2.5), F N(33.5,2.5) cm. Pitch per photo N(0,10). Chin deviation Laplace(0,1.5 mm).

Fit the jawline, chin and neck front as occluding-contour residuals, recomputing correspondences every iteration. Use detector jaw points (dlib 0-16, MediaPipe face oval, point 152) only to initialise. Derive Pog', Me', C (curvature maximum) and gonion (tangent intersection) from the FH-aligned profile contour.
Masks: beard and stubble down-weight everything below the lip line; collar and hair masks remove the neck base and angle; fit shading only above the jaw terminator, never the cast shadow.
Compute CMA and submental fat only after un-posing to canonical pose. A flexed-neck frame must not update submental fat without a flexion corrective.
Identifiability: with only a frontal photo, return the prior with wide covariance and say so in the UI. One profile should pin chin projection to about 1-2 mm and the angles to about 2-4 deg.

Template warping: tag feature curves (mandibular border, posterior ramus, chin-plane edges, submental line, SCM borders), stiffen the bone-anchored chin and border, let the submental and neck regions deform more, and skin the neck as a separate articulated part.
takeaways: Read chin projection, gonial angle and cervicomental angle (CMA) only from camera-solved profile or 3/4 views. A frontal photo cannot identify them.
Head pitch changes CMA roughly degree for degree, and flexion creates a submental roll. Solve head-neck pose first and measure the neck only in canonical pose (FH level, neck neutral).
The vertical pattern is the main mandibular shape axis after size. High-angle faces go with an obtuse gonial angle, short ramus, long lower face, retrusive chin and obtuse CMA.

Sex differences are average tendencies with heavy overlap: a squarer, wider chin with two tubercles, a slightly smaller everted angle and a 90-deg thyroid keel in men. Treat sex as a covariate, not a switch.

The visible jawline is a plane break whose sharpness depends on fat, platysma and skin more than on masseter size. Its true edge is the terminator, not the cast shadow on the neck or a trimmed beard line.
Profile norms (E-line, Z-angle, zero meridian, CMA ideals) are clinical ideals from mostly white samples, not population means.
Pivot the jaw at the condyles, 10-15 mm in front of the tragus, never at gonion, and add forward translation after about 20 mm of opening.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic, so no URL sources were available and every claim is 🧠 or ↔️ pending verification.
Population norms for CMA, submental fat thickness and chin width by sex, age, BMI and ancestry, measured with a consistent protocol, are lacking.
No validated way to infer hyoid position from surface photos was identified.
Reliability of photo-based CMA and gonial-angle measurement against CBCT or 3D scans is unknown.
3D statistical neck and submental shape models: the face-only models and the MediaPipe mesh stop at the jaw, and FLAME's neck coverage is limited (needs checking).
Exact Farkas values for go-go, sn-gn and neck measurements were not available and are given as ranges.
Whether the gonial angle opens with age in dentate adults (Shaw et al. versus others) is unresolved.

landmark-detection.title: Facial landmark detectors
landmark-detection.summary:
Neither input existed for this topic: there was no harvest file at _raw/harvests/landmark-detection.json and no earlier draft. I wrote the note from expert knowledge, about 2,750 words, and every item carries a 🧠 or ↔️ badge (0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 73 🧠 / 19 ↔️). No URLs are cited, so the sources JSON has an empty source list and 19 references named in words.

**What the note covers:**
- **MediaPipe Face Landmarker:** its 478-point layout and iris index ranges, the 52 blendshapes, the 4×4 transform, how its coordinates are defined, its usable pose range, and its licence.
- **The other detectors:** dlib 6
algorithmic: LandmarkSet schema: scheme, detector_version, uv_px[N,2], cov_px[N,2,2], visible[N], optional z_rel, image_wh, iod_px, orientation, mirrored. Branch on scheme, not N.

Per-class sigma in % of image IOD: iris 1.0; anchors (canthi, cheilia, labrale, subnasale) 1.5; lid and lip contours 2 normal / 5 tangent; pronasale 2.5; sellion 2 horizontal / 4 vertical; brows 3-5; jaw/oval 2.5 normal / 10-15 tangent, or a silhouette term. Use anisotropic covariance R diag(sn^2, st^2) R^T.
For dense correlated MediaPipe output, keep 80-120 distinct points or inflate sigma by sqrt(N/N_eff) with N_eff 60-100.

Test-time augmentation: 6-10 passes (flip with L/R permutation, scale 0.9-1.1, rotation +/-10 deg, shift +/-3 %). Set sigma = max(class sigma, spread), and add a second detector's disagreement in quadrature.
Visibility weight: 0 when n.(-v) < cos80, ramping to 1 at cos60. Drop far-side oval points when |yaw| > 25 deg.
Huber delta = 2 sigma in px. Reject points beyond 4 sigma after the first solve. Flag a view when more than 15 % of its points are rejected.
Build the L/R permutation by mirroring the canonical mesh, and assign iris L/R geometrically from the eye corners.
Detector-semantics calibration: render the template from 20-50 known cameras and store barycentric correspondences per (scheme, detector version, template version).
Expression gate on blendshapes (uncalibrated starting values): jawOpen < 0.08, mouthSmile < 0.15, eyeBlink < 0.35, browInnerUp < 0.2, judged relative to the subject's most neutral photo.
Scale only from iris (11.7 +/- 0.5 mm), IPD (63 +/- 3.5 mm) or a measured value, never from MediaPipe's canonical model.
takeaways: MediaPipe Face Landmarker is the only widely used detector with permissive code and weights. Treat its z, transform translation and canonical-model scale as non-metric. Use only its rotation, as a PnP seed below about 60 degrees yaw.

Benchmark NME of 3-4.5 % outer IOD is roughly 3-4 mm per point. Inner anchors are about 2x better, and jaw contours plus large-yaw views are much worse. Detectors are biased toward the mean face, so landmarks give a starting fit, never the likeness.

Set the bundle adjuster's sigma_px from image IOD. In a 12 MP portrait, 1 % IOD is about 9 px, so anchors get sigma of about 13 px. The current 1.0 px default over-weights reprojection about 170x against the mm priors.

Jaw and face-oval points in 2D-convention schemes slide with yaw. Fit them as silhouette residuals, or with large tangent sigma, never as fixed vertices. Drop occluded points that MediaPipe still returns.
Almost every open heatmap detector (dlib 68, FAN, HRNet, SPIGA, PIPNet, InsightFace) has weights trained on research-only data. Keep them optional and user-installed.
With 4 or more views, systematic bias dominates random noise. Calibrate what each detector index means by rendering the template in Blender, and use silhouettes for profiles.
gaps: No harvest or prior draft existed, so nothing is source-verified. All numbers are from training knowledge.
No published accuracy-versus-yaw measurement for MediaPipe on controlled portrait photos; it needs to be measured with calibration renders.
MediaPipe indices for the alar region are uncertain (several candidates). Iris L/R index naming is inconsistent across sources.
Licence status of SPIGA, Sapiens and the MediaPipe model card weights is unconfirmed, as is the commercial status of weights trained on research-only datasets in general.
Whether Wood et al. 2022's dense model, or any faithful reimplementation, is publicly available.
2025-2026 detectors (foundation-model-based landmarkers, newer MediaPipe versions) are not covered.
The quantitative anatomical offset between detector points and anthropometric definitions (caruncle vs endocanthion, nose highlight vs pronasale) is estimated as 1-3 mm without a source.

licences-tos.title: Licences and platform terms
licences-tos.summary:
Wrote the licences and platform-terms note (about 2,800 words), plus a sources JSON and a data JSON. Neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so no URLs are cited. Every claim is expert knowledge (64 🧠) or contested (32 ↔️). The note checks three permission chains:
