- **Subject consent:** cross-referenced to `ethics/consent-likeness-law.md`.
- **Photograph copyright:** it belongs to the photographer, not the subject. Fitting geometry extracts facts and carries low risk; texture projection copies the photo. Covers *Rogers v. Koons*, *AWF v. Goldsmith*, DMCA §1202 on keeping copyrig
algorithmic: A LicenceTag on every component and image: {spdx_or_custom, commercial_ok: true|false|null, redistributable, attribution, share_alike, use_restrictions[], territory_excluded[], source, version, sha256, accepted_at}; null counts as false at export.

Taint propagation: result.commercial_ok = AND of commercial_ok over every component used in the run (detector, prior, template, regressor, segmenter, photos), with fit_only and texture paths tracked separately.

Photo rights gate: rights_basis in {self_shot, subject_selfie, photographer_licence, cc_licence, public_domain, unknown}; unknown allows a private-study fit with a warning and blocks texture bake, packing and export.
Model registry entries {name, url, sha256, bytes, licence_text_hash, commercial_ok, needs_network}: show the licence text and require a click before download; never bundle non-commercial weights.
Inputs are local files only: no URL importers, no social-platform importers, no account logins.
Metadata policy: preserve EXIF/IPTC Artist and Copyright into a sidecar and glTF extras (DMCA §1202), strip GPS and device serials by default, auto-generate ATTRIBUTION.txt for CC-BY assets.

Licensing: the bpy glue is SPDX:GPL-3.0-or-later with SPDX headers and a NOTICE; the engine package is MIT or Apache-2.0; never port code from NC or unknown-licence repositories, and ship no FLAME landmark-embedding files.
CI check: fail on any bundled file without an SPDX entry, and run the fitting tests on the CC0 template alone so the commercial path never depends on research assets.
takeaways: Three permission chains must each be clean: subject consent, photographer copyright (the subject does not own photos others took of them), and the licence of every model, dataset and template.

The asset or weight licence decides, not the code licence: MIT code wrapping FLAME, BFM, InsightFace or dlib-68 weights is still non-commercial, and ONNX conversion or fine-tuning does not change that.

The commercially safe default stack is MediaPipe (Apache-2.0) + ONNX Runtime (MIT) + an own numpy fitter + an MPFB2 CC0 base; FLAME, BFM, DECA, MICA and InsightFace stay opt-in, downloaded by the user, and taint the project as non-commercial.
A bpy add-on should be GPL-3.0-or-later, but GPL does not cover meshes, .blend files or renders; a bpy-free engine can be MIT or Apache-2.0 for reuse outside Blender.
The GPL alone does not forbid shipping non-commercial weights alongside GPL code (mere aggregation); the assets' no-redistribution clauses and the Extensions policy do.
Fitting geometry from photos extracts facts and carries low copyright risk; projecting or baking texture copies the photographer's work and needs a known rights basis.
Instagram and other platforms forbid automated collection and the Basic Display API is gone; the clean route is the subject's own Accounts Center export plus each photographer's permission.
A CC BY portrait is not cleared for a likeness: CC 4.0 expressly excludes publicity and privacy rights.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed: zero URLs are cited, and every claim is 🧠 or ↔️ pending verification.
Exact licence text not checked for: FLAME 2023 Open, MediaPipe model cards per model, ICT-FaceKit, FAN weights, SMIRK and HRN.
Blender Extensions policy on downloading model weights or binaries at runtime is unconfirmed.
Current X, TikTok and Pinterest terms (including the liquidated-damages figure) are time-sensitive and unverified.
Appeal outcomes in Kneschke v. LAION, Getty v. Stability AI and the Clearview UK tribunal proceedings are unconfirmed.
Whether outputs of non-commercial models (e.g. NC detector landmarks) legally taint fitted geometry is unresolved.
KeenTools FaceBuilder EULA terms on exported meshes, and stock-agency AI and 3D-derivative clauses, were not checked.
The note is not jurisdiction-complete (no detailed coverage of Korea, Brazil or Australia) and is not legal advice.

likeness-mistakes.title: Common likeness mistakes and diagnostics
likeness-mistakes.summary:
Neither the harvest (/home/user/minedesign/research/_raw/harvests/likeness-mistakes.json) nor an earlier draft existed, so I wrote the note from scratch. It is about 2,800 words. Everything in it is expert knowledge or pinhole arithmetic, so it cites no URLs. Where other library notes already hold sourced facts, it points to them by path (anatomy/facial-asymmetry.md, anatomy/ear.md, anatomy/mouth-lips-teeth.md, community/reddit-face-from-photos.md, community/art-anatomy-books.md, community/instagram-social-sculptors.md).

The note covers:
- **Why likeness errors happen,** in perception terms:
algorithmic: Likeness lint: compute each Table A metric on the fitted mesh. Store the model value, the photo-derived value with σ (from triangulate_points spread or reprojection) and a population z. Flag only when |model − photo| > 2σ_photo, or when |z| > 2.5 for features the photos cannot see. Never pull a feature the photos support toward the mean.

Perspective-error signature: if the camera distance is wrong and focal length compensates, a landmark's radial residual is about ρ_i·δ_i·(1/d − 1/d′). Regress BundleResult.per_view_residuals on ρ_i·δ_i. If the slope implies more than 5% magnification error, free the focal length or request a photo taken from further away.

Solve pose before features: give ear landmarks weight 0 when |yaw| < 30° and until pitch is constrained by at least 2 views or a profile. Then apply ear priors: tragion height vs orbitale σ 4 mm, axis 20 ± 7°, length 60 ± 4 mm, protrusion 17 ± 4 mm.

Eye priors: globe radius 12 ± 0.5 mm, cornea 16 ± 2.5 mm ahead of the lateral orbital rim, iris 11.7 ± 0.5 mm, MRD1 4.5 ± 1 mm. Add a hinge penalty on sclera visible above the iris unless at least 2 views show it.

Symmetry: keep Priors.sigma_sym = 2.0 mm and sigma_mid = 1.5 mm. Warn 'over-symmetric' if the whole-face RMSD against the mirror is below 0.3 mm on a face whose photos show asymmetry. Flag 'suspicious asymmetry' when a left-right difference correlates with one view's roll or yaw.

Shrinkage detector: with k whitened coefficients, a real face has ‖c‖² ≈ χ²_k. Warn 'pulled toward average' if ‖c‖² < k − 2√(2k), or use Mahalanobis D² over 3N dimensions for per-landmark priors. This needs calibrated σ; the current scalar sigma = 8.0 mm is not calibrated.
Caricature slider: a shape key S(α) = M + α(S − M) from the template mean, excluding scale and pose. Default α = 1.0, range 0.8-1.4, stored in metadata.

Diagnostic renders per solved camera, generated in numpy so they don't depend on Blender's version: overlay at α 0.5, difference, Canny edges, silhouette chamfer in % IOD, flipped/blurred/64 px/grayscale pairs, a 3 Hz blink GIF, a residual-arrow plot, and leave-one-view-out reprojection RMS.
Use identity-embedding similarity only as a relative score on textured renders with matched lighting. Untextured renders score low whatever their shape.
takeaways: Most likeness errors are predictable and directional: eyes too big, too open or too far forward; face too flat and cranium too short; nose projection too low; lips idealised (fuller, more even); ears misplaced; asymmetry erased. Together they produce 'a good-looking cousin'.

Much of the error comes from the reference, not the sculpting. Perspective depends only on camera distance, so selfies make the nose too big and the ears too small. Unsolved pitch moves the ears 5.7-7.0 mm relative to the eyes at 5° and 11-14 mm at 10°. 3° of roll or 5° of yaw creates more apparent asymmetry than a normal face has.
Projected photo textures make any geometry look right from the photo's own camera. Review shape with texture off, from cameras at least 20-30° away, and against at least 2 held-out photos.

Each studio check defeats one mechanism. Flip and inversion reset adaptation. Squint/blur at Gaussian σ ≈ 3-5% of face width and a 48-64 px thumbnail test overall configuration. The silhouette is independent of lighting and reveals depth. Overlay, difference and blink at 2-3 Hz expose offsets. Grayscale removes hue that hides form.
The upside-down check is double-edged: it helps judge spacing but hides feature-level errors (Thatcher illusion), so always pair it with an upright check.
A bald, browless grey sculpt will look less like the sitter even when its geometry is right, because brows and hair are strong identity cues. Don't distort the geometry to compensate.

A single photo is a poor stand-in for identity because one person varies a lot across photos. Judge likeness against many photos from one period, and finally with a viewer who knows the sitter, shown both orientations.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so the note has 0 ✅ and 0 📄. Every figure needs verification, and the Sources section cites no URLs.
No empirical data were found that rank which mistakes most often break 3D likeness, or how many millimetres of error per feature destroy recognition for viewers who know the person.
The depth levers in Table B (outer canthi to nose tip 35-50 mm, outer canthi to tragion 65-80 mm) are the author's estimates and should be checked against anthropometric depth data.
Most normative ranges come from European-descent populations. Ancestry-specific norms for canthal tilt, alar width, lip projection, Hertel values and cephalic index are thin.
The size of the eyes-too-high effect in Carbon & Wirth 2014 and the exact title are unverified, as is the exact sorting result in Jenkins et al. 2011.
Blender UI details (background-image Flip Horizontally, AgX Greyscale look, compositor nodes in 5.x) are time-sensitive and unverified.
Whether caricature or exaggeration helps or hurts in realistic 3D renders is unmeasured. Whether embedding scores track human likeness judgements of sculpts is unknown.

metahuman-cc-bridges.title: Bridges to MetaHuman, Character Creator, Daz
algorithmic: Store each bridge as a data profile {units_per_m, up, forward, handedness, template_vcount, template_topology_hash, door, cloud, redistribute_template:false, commercial_ok}. An unknown licence field blocks export.
Hash the face-index arrays of the template and assert the hash plus the vertex count before any write-back. Refuse on mismatch.
Store correspondence packs as landmark → (triangle id, barycentric), generated locally from the user's licensed template. Ship the generator only.

Wrap pipeline in five steps: (1) Umeyama similarity on at least 8 anchors, with a scale accept range of 0.8–1.25; (2) thin-plate-spline landmark warp, with anchor σ 1.0 mm and sliding-contour σ 1.5–2 mm; (3) NRICP with stiffness 100→50→20→10→5→2, rejecting matches beyond 8 mm or 60°; (4) normal-ray projection; (5) Laplacian relaxation. Protected zones (eyelids, lips, nostrils, ears) get ×5 stiffness. Add a soft symmetry prior with σ 1–2 mm.
Eye-socket constraint: eyeball radius 12 ± 0.5 mm, centre placed from the canthi and lid margins. Penalise lid–globe gaps above 0.5 mm.
Neutralise expression with an ARKit-named basis (σ ≈ 0.3 on the 0–1 range), then discard it and export identity only.

Accept a wrap when face RMS is below 0.5 mm, scalp and neck below 1.5 mm, no triangle has flipped and no triangle area falls below 0.2× rest. Log landmark, region and profile error before and after each vendor step to quantify drift.
Apply axis matrices in code for OBJ. For FBX, trust the metadata but validate the test import against anthropometric sanity ranges.
takeaways: MetaHuman, CC and Daz all build characters from one fixed template. A Blender likeness gets in either through a vendor tool that fits any mesh (Mesh to MetaHuman / Creator Conform, Headshot mesh mode) or as a morph on a matching mesh with identical vertex count and order (Morph Loader Pro, CC morph import, MetaHuman template or DNA).

The add-on should export a 'bridge-ready neutral': real scale in cm, projected-photo texture, lips closed, eyes open with sphere eyeballs (r ≈ 12 mm), neck kept, photo expression removed, hair removed.
Never use glTF for morph round trips: it splits vertices at UV seams. Export with Multires at level 0, and avoid Join, Separate, Sort, Remesh and merging Mirror on the template.
Unit and axis conversion: to Daz, Maya or DNA use ×100 and (x, z, −y); to UE use ×100 and (x, −y, z), letting FBX carry it. Check imports with IPD ≈ 6.3 cm to catch ×100 errors.

Mesh to MetaHuman loses likeness at the nasal tip, the lip shape, the eyelid opening and the jaw angle. Audit it by bringing the head back and measuring signed distance, and fix it through the template route, never by editing the DNA mesh alone, which leaves the joints misplaced.

Licences, not geometry, are the binding constraint. Ship no vendor meshes, index lists or priors. Generate correspondence packs locally from the user's own licensed template. Record consent that names any cloud processing.
gaps: Neither the harvest nor the earlier draft existed for this topic, so there are no first-party sources on MetaHuman, Reallusion or Daz. Every vendor fact is 🧠 or ↔️.
UE and MetaHuman features and licence terms after 5.6/5.7 are unknown, as is the current UE version in Nov 2026.
Template vertex counts (MetaHuman LOD0 head, CC3+, Genesis 8/9) are recalled, not checked.
Not known: CC5 and Headshot version, editions and prices; Daz Face Transfer support for Genesis 9; whether FBX export needs a particular CC edition.
Status and licence on Blender 5.x are unknown for the Poly Hammer MetaHuman DNA tool, Epic's DNA Calibration library, CC/iC Blender Tools, DazToBlender and Diffeomorphic.
No source measures the mm-level likeness kept by any vendor route (Mesh to MetaHuman, Headshot, Face Transfer).
It is unclear legally whether vertex index lists or correspondence packs for vendor topologies may be redistributed.
A private claude.ai artifact of the .md note was created by mistake (https://claude.ai/artifact/SeZLqLbMLsBAo2uwSLdWwS). It is left in place pending the user's decision.

monocular-depth-normals.title: Monocular depth and surface normals for faces
monocular-depth-normals.summary:
Rewrote the note on monocular depth and normals for faces using the new badge scheme. All 22 harvested sources and their findings are kept. The DSINE NYUv2 error of about 16.4° and the November 2025 date for DA3 are ✅. The contested DA V2 metric-accuracy results are ↔️. The obsolete notes about the search budget are gone. Expert knowledge added (🧠):
- **Depth Anything V2:** its relative checkpoints output inverse depth (disparity), not depth, so scale and shift must be fitted in disparity space. Model sizes, licences (Small is Apache-2.0; Base, Large and Giant are CC BY-NC 4.0) and the 518 px
algorithmic: Observation registry types: relative_disparity (DA V2, MiDaS), affine_depth (Marigold), metric_depth_focal (DA3 metric, needs f), normal_cam. Store with each: axis adapter, model, version, crop/resize, and licence ('unknown' until verified).

Depth residual in the model's native space. For disparity, fit 1/z_p(V) ≈ s·d̂_p + t in closed form each iteration, keep s·d̂ + t > 0, and use r_p = z_p(V) − 1/(s·d̂_p + t). Use σ about 6 mm with Huber δ = 1.5σ.

Normal residual: von Mises–Fisher term κ(1 − n̂·n(V)) with κ = π/(2m²), m = assumed mean angular error in radians. Defaults: m = 20° for scene-trained models (κ≈13), 15° for human-specific models (κ≈23). Wrap it in a robust loss.
Subsample the normal term at a stride of about 8 px (errors are spatially correlated) so that 10^5 pixels do not swamp 68–100 landmark terms.
Rotation-bias correction: weighted Kabsch on predicted vs base normals (SVD of Σ w n̂ n0ᵀ). Apply if ≤10°; a larger angle flags a convention or intrinsics error.

Mesh-space detail solve after Nehab et al. 2005:
- Unknown offsets δ along base normals.
- Per-edge linear constraint n̂_ij·((x_j+δ_j m_j)−(x_i+δ_i m_i)) = 0.
- Regularise with λ_L‖Lδ‖² + λ_0‖δ‖² and δ = 0 at landmarks.
- The system is symmetric positive definite: use the engine's cotan_laplacian and sparse.cg.
- Iterate 2–3 times.
Multi-view fusion: target normal = average of the per-view normals rotated into the world frame, weighted by κ·cos(view angle). Drop views beyond 70°.

Image-space alternative: ∂log z/∂u = −nx/(ũ·nx + ṽ·ny + f·nz), with ũ = u − cx and ṽ = v − cy. Integrate with bilateral normal integration, then high-pass against the rendered base depth (geodesic Gaussian σ about 6 mm).
Masks: skin only, eroded 3–5 px. Exclude highlights (HSV V > 0.95), grazing pixels beyond 70°, and the eye, lip-border, nostril and hair regions.
Alarm: if nose-tip-to-alar-crease depth changes by more than about 1 mm after the detail pass, reduce the clamp or reject the pass.
Convention unit test on a synthetic render in the OpenCV frame: forehead ≈ (0,0,−1); image-left cheek nx < 0; under-chin and subnasale ny > 0.
takeaways: No face-region accuracy number exists in this library for Depth Anything V2/3, Marigold, DSINE, Lotus, StableNormal, Sapiens or DAViD. Benchmark them ourselves on synthetic and scanned heads.
Single-image depth cannot set nose projection or head depth because of affine invariance and the bas-relief ambiguity. Use depth only as a weak low-frequency prior after fitting scale and shift.

Predicted normals are the useful detail signal. Apply them as a clamped (about ±2.5 mm), landmark-anchored displacement on a subdivided base (edges ≤1 mm). Keep the result as a reversible shape key or Multires layer.
Fit Depth Anything V2 in disparity space. Treating disparity as depth gives a bowl-shaped profile error of about 4.9 mm at 300 mm and 2.6 mm at 600 mm.
Integrate normals under perspective: selfie-distance ray obliquity is about 13° at a point 70 mm off-axis. Pass crop-adjusted intrinsics to DSINE and DA3 metric.
Crop the face to about 60% of the network input. At 518 px the face sees about 0.43 mm/px; uncropped half-body shots resolve only about 3.5 mm folds.
DA3 metric depth scales linearly with the focal passed in, so a 10% focal error gives a 10% error in both distance and relief. The resolution the focal refers to is unconfirmed.
Licences vary: Depth Anything V2 Base, Large and Giant are reportedly non-commercial. Run predictors out of process, cache float outputs, and never bundle non-commercial weights.
gaps: No face-region angular or depth error was found for any general or human-specific model, nor any head-to-head comparison against the face-normal papers [15][16].
CPU/ONNX latency was not measured for any model. Table 2 timings are order-of-magnitude estimates.
Licences are unverified for DA3, Marigold weights, Marigold V2, DSINE, Sapiens, DAViD, Depth Pro and MoGe.
DA3 metric details are unconfirmed: whether the focal refers to the original or the processing resolution, the output unit, and whether the metric head is reliable at portrait range (0.3–2 m).
Whether DA3 multi-view inference on 2–5 portraits beats landmark bundle adjustment is unknown.
Whether Sapiens or DAViD normals resolve eyelid creases and nasolabial folds is untested.
No sourced default exists for any fitting weight. All suggested sigmas, clamps and cutoffs are expert starting points to tune.
The face-normal error range on Photoface (about 10–20°) comes from memory and is unverified.
The DSINE data-efficiency claim and the claimed 500K-image Sapiens fine-tuning set remain weakly attributed.

mouth-lips-teeth.title: Lips, mouth and dental support
mouth-lips-teeth.summary:
I rewrote the lips, mouth and teeth note at /home/user/minedesign/research/anatomy/mouth-lips-teeth.md. It is about 2,470 words of prose (2,820 counting table cells and citation markers). It has all six required sections, and the evidence line reads 3 ✅ / 27 📄 / 50 🧠 / 20 ↔️.

What carried over and what changed:
- **Kept from the earlier draft:** all 23 sourced facts and citations, plus its checks: the doubtful attribution of the toddler finding to [1], the ambiguous wording of the StatPearls ratio, [17] and [18] being the same study, the unpinned 82.8% figure, and both dropped claims. The sea
algorithmic: Landmark schema: sn, ls_border (Farkas ls) and ls_prom (orthodontic labrale superius, kept as separate names), cph_L/R, sto_sup/sto_inf, li, sl, ch_L/R. Store the upper vermilion border (ch–cph–dip–cph–ch), the lower border and the stomion line as polylines.

Correspondence switching: the vermilion border and cheilion are surface-fixed (barycentric) targets. The outer lip contour in profile or steep three-quarter views is an occluding contour and needs sliding silhouette correspondences. Switch per point by a normal·view test, or above roughly 35–45° yaw.

Neutral gate: flag lips as parted when the inner-lip gap / ch–ch exceeds about 0.04. Flag an expression when cheilion height relative to stomion is more than about 2 mm off the cross-frame median, or when teeth are visible. Only frames that pass feed the identity shape.

Weak Gaussian priors, each w·((x−μ)/σ)²: ch–ch/IPD 0.85 (σ 0.06); ch–ch/al–al 1.55 (σ 0.15); sn–sto/sn–me 0.33 (σ 0.03); ls–sto = 8.0 − 0.05·(age−25) mm (σ 1.5); sto–li/ls–sto 1.3 (σ 0.3, clamped to 0.8–2.3); cph–cph 11.5 mm (σ 1.5); commissure depth 15 mm (σ 4); E-line distances −4/−2 mm (σ 3); resting incisor display 3 mm (σ 1.5). Inflate σ ×1.5 when ancestry or age is unknown.

Latent dental arch: parameters are intercanine width (about 33–37 mm), arch depth, incisor labial position, incisal-edge height (which sets display) and proclination. Lips = arch + a soft-tissue thickness field (about 11–15 mm at ls) with its own prior, so projection error is split between teeth and soft tissue. Export the teeth as a separate mesh.

QA warnings only, never constraints: ch–ch/IPD outside 0.70–1.00, sto–li/ls–sto outside 0.8–2.3, sn–sto/sn–me outside 0.27–0.40, resting display outside −2 to 6 mm, commissure depth outside 6–25 mm. No mouth-width = IPD constraint.
Solve head pitch before measuring smile-arc curvature. Report the arc class as a descriptor, not a target. Carry each prior's evidence badge into the solver as a confidence weight.

Detector mapping: iBUG-68 uses 48–59 for the outer lip and 60–67 for the inner lip. MediaPipe uses 61/291 for the corners, 0/17 for the outer midlines and 13/14 for the inner midlines. Neither marks the philtral columns, and both are biased by lipstick and shading.
takeaways: Fit identity lip shape only from neutral, lips-closed, bare-lip frames, because expression, lipstick and filler all move the vermilion border and Cupid's bow. Route smiles to separate shape keys.

The lower vermilion is taller than the upper (✅). The 1.6:1 figure is an aesthetic target from young white women, not a population mean, and measured means are likely about 1.1–1.4. Never pull a subject toward 1.6.

"Mouth corners under the pupils" is untested. Typical means give mouth width / interpupillary distance of about 0.8–0.9, so resting corners sit near the medial limbus. Place the corners from the photos, not from the eyes.
The 22–23 mm 'upper lip height' in [2] is sn–sto (vermilion included), not sn–ls as the earlier draft labelled it. Upper vermilion thins about 1.5 mm from the 20s to the 50s.

The Cupid's bow comes from the depth of the philtrum and its columns, not from lip volume. The bow peaks sit at the feet of the philtral columns, so peak spacing is about the philtrum width (about 11–12 mm).

The teeth support the lips: about 2–4 mm of upper incisor showing at rest is the norm, and too little reads as old and gives poor lip support. Build a dental arch proxy before sculpting lip projection.
The mouth wraps around the dental arch (corners roughly 10–20 mm behind the lip midline, low confidence). A flat mouth reads fine from the front and fails in three-quarter views.
Smile arcs are consonant in only about 43–83% of people and lay preference varies, so copy the subject's own arc after correcting head pitch.
gaps: Full text of PMC7984336 [2]: ancestry, sample size, sex split and exact landmark definitions (whether the 22–23 mm value is sn–sto).
Sex or subgroup labels for the Kenyan lateral lip heights (23.5 vs 22.3 mm) [4].
Which study reports the 82.8% consonant smile-arc figure.
No study directly tests mouth width against interpupillary distance or the medial-limbus line in large multi-ethnic 3D cohorts.
Measured population lower:upper vermilion ratios by ancestry and sex: the note's 1.1–1.4 is expert knowledge, not yet sourced.
Exact Vig & Brundo incisor display values by age and sex, and resting display in non-Western or 3D-scan cohorts.
3D lip morphometrics from 2024–2026 (vermilion volume, tubercle projection, commissure depth); the 10–20 mm commissure depth is low-confidence.
Unread lip sources [9] (Indonesian lip anthropometry), [10] and [23] (lip and philtrum injection anatomy) probably contain usable numbers.
Accuracy of 2D lip-landmark detectors under lipstick, beards and three-quarter poses.
Practitioner views (Polycount, BlenderArtists, Reddit) on mouth-corner placement and lip proportion in likeness sculpting.
Crowdsourced lip-ratio preference (Heidekrueger et al. 2017, ~1:1) is unverified.

multi-view-fitting.title: Multi-image and video 3DMM fitting
multi-view-fitting.summary:
I rewrote the multi-view / video 3DMM fitting note and the matching source and data files.

**Kept from the draft:** every sourced fact and citation [1]-[13]. This covers the Metrical Tracker, VHAP, flame-head-tracker, video-head-tracker, the two 2026 multi-camera papers and the GAF use of VHAP.

**Changed:**
- Old ⚠️ badges are now 📄 or ✅.
- The search-budget notes are gone.
- **Scale correction:** the draft implied a calibrated multi-camera rig fixes millimetres. It does so only if the baseline length or an object of known size is in metric units. Uncalibrated multi-view, including structure
algorithmic: Parameter layout. Shared: beta, albedo, intrinsics per camera and zoom setting. Per view: R, t, psi, jaw and eyes, 27 spherical-harmonic lighting values, a 3-value exposure/white-balance gain. Video adds velocity priors (about 0.5-2 deg/frame and 1-5 mm/frame at 30 fps).

Staged solve: rigid PnP with focal on the mean shape, then joint landmark LM (alternate beta and psi when starting cold), then a silhouette/contour term from face-parsing masks, then optional photometric or dense-UV refinement, then Laplacian/RBF offsets kept to about 3-5 mm or less.
Replace the independent 8 mm per-landmark Priors.sigma with a 3DMM layer, X = mu + B*beta, with an N(0,1) Mahalanobis prior on beta. Flag |beta| > 3.
Expression prior: sigma 0.3 on neutral-tagged views, 1.0 on expressive views. Jaw rotation sigma 2-3 degrees on neutral views.

Landmark noise: about 1-1.5% of inter-ocular distance (IOD) for crisp points, 3-5% for jaw and brow contours. Use sliding or dynamic contour correspondences above 15 degrees yaw and drop them past 60 degrees. Set the Huber threshold to about 2x the median residual after the first pass.

Focal prior: sigma_log 0.05-0.10 with trusted EXIF, 0.35-0.5 otherwise, shared per camera. Lock focal when estimated d/depth exceeds about 12. Fix the principal point unless cropping offsets are known.
Keep the symmetry prior at 1.5-3 mm (current 2.0) and the midline prior at 1-2 mm (current 1.5).
Scale-mode tag (calibrated / object / measured / prior) written to export metadata. Report leave-one-view-out error and the per-vertex mm spread of beta across view subsets as confidence.
Video keyframes: neutral frames (blendshape scores near zero) that are sharp (variance of the Laplacian), spread over yaw -70 to +70 and pitch ±20 degrees. Use 8-15 keyframes.
takeaways: Multi-view and video FLAME fitting share one identity vector beta across all views. Pose, expression, jaw/eye pose, lighting and exposure are fitted per view. Intrinsics are shared per physical camera and zoom setting.

Images alone never give absolute scale. A single perspective image cannot, and uncalibrated multi-view (including SfM) also leaves global scale free. Put an A4 sheet or ID card in shot, measure the subject, or label the result 'proportions only' with about 4-5% scale error from the population prior.

The benefit of extra views comes from new viewing directions, not from photo count. Profile and three-quarter views turn nose projection, chin projection and forehead slope into image-plane measurements, so 7-9 well-spread neutral photos beat 20 near-frontal ones.

Shoot the identity set from 1.5-2 m with an 85-135 mm-equivalent lens. At selfie distance (about 0.3 m) the nose plane is magnified about 33% relative to the ear plane. Beyond about 1.2 m focal length is barely observable from the face, so lock it to EXIF.

All open-source reference trackers (Metrical Tracker, VHAP, flame-head-tracker) are offline GPU tools. VHAP's own authors call photometric alignment sensitive and say aligning the neck with the head is hard, so mask hair, beard, glasses and neck.
No source quantifies the multi-view accuracy gain. Validate fits yourself with leave-one-view-out reprojection error and the spread of beta across view subsets.
gaps: No quantified accuracy gain (mm) of N views over one view, for either landmark-only or photometric fitting.
Licences of VHAP, the Metrical Tracker repo, flame-head-tracker and FLAME 2023 are unverified.
VHAP's official multi-view support is from expert knowledge only.
The resolution and iteration settings behind flame-head-tracker's 0.9 / 1.9 s/frame are unknown, and there is no same-GPU comparison with VHAP's batched speed.
The anthropometric scale-cue values (iris, interpupillary distance, head-breadth SD) and all suggested sigmas are expert heuristics without a source in this library.
MVF-Net and other learned multi-view regressors have no harvested numbers.

muscles-lower-face.title: Muscles of the lower face, lips and chin
muscles-lower-face.summary:
I rewrote the lower-face muscle note. It keeps all 32 sources and citations from the earlier draft, merges the new harvest (31 new numbered sources, 63 in total) and drops the obsolete notes about the search budget running out. It covers orbicularis oris, depressor anguli oris (DAO), depressor labii inferioris (DLI), mentalis, platysma and the modiolus, plus the mentolabial sulcus, marionette fold, jowl and mandibular ligament, chin cleft vs dimpling, and chin ptosis.

New sourced numbers:
- The DAO inserts about 10 mm lateral and 10 mm below the mouth corner.
- Mentalis: 6.7 ± 1.4 mm deep, 4.
algorithmic: Add landmarks supramentale (B'), gnathion_soft and derived modiolus_L/R alongside the existing stomion, labrale_inferius, pogonion, menton and cheilion_L/R. Take B' as the profile-silhouette point farthest from the Li–Pog' chord.

Fit detector chin and jaw contour points as silhouette constraints (nearest occluding-contour vertex per view, 3DDFA-style landmark marching), never as fixed vertex correspondences. Verify the MediaPipe indices (61/291, 13/14, 17, 152) and dlib-68 indices (49/55, 58, 9).

Gaussian priors in mm: mentolabial_depth 4±2, truncated to [0,10]; lower_lip_to_SnPog 2±1.5; lower_lip_to_Eline −2±2 (±3 if ancestry unknown); mentolabial_angle 125°±12°; lip_chin_ratio 0.50±0.06; interlabial_gap_rest 2±2 (≥0).
Soft-tissue depth priors over the fitted skull: Li 13.5±2.5, B' 11±2, Pog' 11±2, Gn' 8.5±2, Me' 7±2.5 mm, with sex and BMI covariates.

modiolus_offset from cheilion: lateral 12±4 mm, vertical −3±5 mm. DLI and DAO region widths 20±4 and 14±3 mm, scaled by mouth width / 52 mm. Mentalis thickness 4.0±1.4 mm for layered models. Weight single-source and knowledge-only priors low.

Neutral-frame gate: score chin high-frequency energy vs cheek, sulcus depth vs the multi-frame median, lower-lip height, per-side commissure height against the stomion line, and marionette crease contrast. Fit identity to a robust multi-frame median and down-weight frames more than 2σ away.

Expression basis from FACS AU15/16/17/18/20/21/22/23/24/28, with signed direction priors: mentalis +y+z, DLI −y−z plus eversion, DAO commissure −y. Use a small-σ L2 prior on AU weights in neutral frames, and keep the lower-face identity basis roughly orthogonal to these directions.
Keep chin_cleft_depth (bone layer, static) separate from the mentalis_dimple blendshape (dynamic). Expose dao_platysma_coupling in [0,1].
Template-warp relative stiffness: lips 0.3, chin pad 1.0, jowl 0.5, mandibular-ligament anchor 2.0, with a crease allowance along the marionette curve. These are heuristic starting values to tune.

Fit left and right independently with a soft symmetry prior (σ about 1–2 mm on commissure height). Do not symmetrize a large left/right AU16 difference. Couple modiolus descent, fold depth and soft-tissue thickness to an age parameter.
takeaways: The lip–chin profile (sulcus depth, lip projection, chin projection) comes mostly from teeth, mandible and soft-tissue thickness. Muscle tone changes it. The fitter must keep skeletal identity separate from mentalis and DAO activation.

Many 'neutral' photos are not neutral. Mentalis strain (flattened sulcus, textured chin) and DAO tone (lower mouth corners, sharper marionette crease) are common, and Botox studies show resting tone visibly changes chin and corner shape. Gate frames before fitting identity.

Profile views are mandatory for this region. Sulcus depth and chin projection are almost invisible from the front, and shadow width is not depth. Point-to-line measures (sulcus depth, E-line, mentolabial angle) survive head-pitch errors; angles measured against the horizontal do not.

A cleft that is visible at rest belongs in the bone layer and persists in every shape key. Dimpling that appears only when the chin tenses belongs in the AU17 shape key. The two should never share a parameter.

Orbicularis oris is interlacing quadrants and layers, not a sphincter. Rig pout (superficial fibres) and press (deep fibres) as separate shapes. Treat the modiolus about 1 cm lateral to each corner as a topology pole where the DAO, zygomaticus and platysma edge flows meet.

The marionette fold has several causes and two parts: an upper part from the DAO's skin insertion and a lower part tied to the mandible by the ligament (whose nature is contested). Its depth depends on age, so take it from the photo, not a template.
Real lower-face asymmetry, including one-sided lower-lip weakness from nerve injury, should be fitted, not symmetrized.
gaps: No sourced population norms (by sex or ancestry) for mentolabial sulcus depth, mentolabial angle or modiolus offset. Table 3 priors are expert knowledge only.

Sample size and measurement site for the DLI/DAO widths [11] are unknown. Mentalis numbers [40], the DAO insertion offset [35] and the innervation percentages [12] come from search snippets, not full text.
There is no measured perioral or platysma muscle thickness from MRI or ultrasound. The 6.4 mm figure at the DLI point is skin plus fat, not muscle.
No population prevalence for cleft chin. The 7.2% figure is only among cheek-dimple carriers.
The grade definitions of the marionette photonumeric scale [10] and the DAO coordinates in [27] were not extracted. Sources [29], [30] and [60]–[63] are unread.

Whether the modiolus has a true ligament [17] or a 'false ligament' [51], and whether these are the same study, is unresolved. Same for the mandibular ligament: osteocutaneous anchor [22] vs sub-platysmal only [47].

MediaPipe and dlib landmark indices and the ARKit blendshape names are from memory and need checking against current documentation and code. The Blender shape-key/Multires advice may depend on the Blender version.
No open Blender FACS rig mapping these muscles to shape keys was searched for.

Operational: the scratchpad directory is shared by parallel agents. My generic temp filenames (body.md, rep.py, sources_section.md) collided with another agent's files. No change to its file was detected (the edit script found no matches and rewrote the file as it was), but use unique per-topic prefixes from now on.

muscles-mastication-jaw.title: Masseter, temporalis and the jaw line
muscles-mastication-jaw.summary:
I rewrote the note in full: about 2,600 words of body text, 5 tables and 50 numbered sources, plus a sources JSON and a data JSON with 10 tables. Every URL cited in the three files was checked against the harvest file and the committed draft; none fall outside them.

- **Sources merged.** All 23 sources from the earlier draft keep their numbers. The harvest added 27 new ones, and 5 duplicates were merged: [6], [15], [17], [18] and [20], with alternate URLs kept for [18] and [29].
- **Badges.** The draft's ⚠️ marks were converted to the four-badge scheme, and the obsolete search-budget notes we
algorithmic: Layered offset model along the bone-surface normal: x' = x + n·[t_m(1+κc)·w_m + s_f·w_f + p·w_p + d_t·w_t], with the skeleton (bony bigonial width, θ_go, ramus height, SN-MP) fitted as separate parameters.
Masseter prior (relaxed, per side): F N(10, 1.8²), M N(12, 2.0²), unknown sex N(11, 2.3²) mm, bounds 6-20. The Korean source values N(9.8, 1.3²) and N(11.3, 1.2²) were widened by design.
Per-image clench state c ∈ [0,1] with prior Beta(1,4) for rest captures, fixed at 1 for a deliberate clench shot. Gain κ ~ N(0.28, 0.05²) clipped to 0.15-0.40; temporalis κ_t ≈ 0-0.1.
Coupling: shift the t_m mean by about −0.14 mm per degree of SN-MP above 32° (derived). Weak covariances with gonial angle (negative) and ramus height (positive), |ρ| ≈ 0.2-0.3, tunable.

Skeleton and soft-tissue priors (🧠, verify): θ_go ~ N(122°, 7²) with bounds 105-145°; bony go-go M N(97, 6²) and F N(90, 5²) mm; fat s_f ~ N(6, 2.5²) mm scaled by BMI; temple d_t ~ N(13, 3²) mm with an age decline of about 0.6%/yr (M) and 1%/yr (F) after 30.
Symmetry: t_m,L − t_m,R ~ Laplace(0, 0.8 mm). Allow large one-sided temple deficits only when the user flags surgery.
Use occluding-contour residuals at the jaw with correspondences recomputed every iteration ('landmark marching'). Never treat 68-point or MediaPipe jaw points as gonion.

If a clench pair exists, fit both photos jointly with shared bone and fat; the displacement gives t_m ≈ Δ/κ directly. Report the posterior covariance of the bone/muscle split instead of a point estimate.
Model perspective explicitly: jaw-plane scale = d/(d + ~0.095 m) relative to the nose-tip plane, so close-range photos must go through the calibrated camera solve.
takeaways: Jaw-line width in a frontal photo is bone + 2×(masseter + fat) + parotid. A frontal view alone cannot tell these apart; profile views pin the bone (gonial angle, ramus) and the far-side 3/4 silhouette pins the masseter belly.

Relaxed adult masseter is about 10-15 mm per side (men thicker; Korean F 9.8, M 11.3 mm) and grows about 27-30% on clenching. Never mix clenched and relaxed photos in one width solve, and ask for a deliberate clench pair: the difference isolates the muscle.

Low-angle (short) faces have thicker masseters, about +1.4 mm, and long faces thinner, about −1.4 mm. A long, steep-plane face with a big flaring jaw is atypical, so check for a clench, parotid swelling or fat before accepting it.

Botulinum toxin reduces masseter bulk by about 25-30%, peaking around 3 months and lasting about 6-12 months. Effects on bone are contested, so photos from different injection windows should not be mixed.

Temple fullness is temporalis plus fat compartments (not muscle alone). The temporalis is larger in men and declines with age, faster in women. Temporalis thickness values are not transferable between ultrasound, MRI and CT.
Selfie perspective shrinks the jaw plane by about 20% at 40 cm relative to the nose tip. Judge jaw width only from camera-solved views.

In Blender, keep the scene in metric units and drive per-layer shape keys or Normal-direction Displace modifiers (masseter, temporalis, parotid, jowl, buccal hollow) from custom properties in millimetres. Multires has no native sculpt layers.
gaps: Whether the Bunkyo masseter volumes [24] and the Taiwanese temporalis volumes [21] are per side or bilateral; none of the sources was re-read in full text.
No sourced soft-tissue depth over gonion, ramus or temple by sex, age or BMI. The Table 5 values are expert knowledge only.

No sourced adult norms for bony bigonial width, gonial angle or go-go/zy-zy by sex in this topic's inputs. The skull-osteology note's harvest has gonial-angle data, but those sources are not cited here.
No correlation coefficients between masseter size and gonial angle, ramus height or bite force for a quantitative covariance prior.
Population coverage is skewed to East Asian and small single-centre samples. There is no multi-ethnic norm measured with one protocol.
No 3D-scan or photogrammetry study separates masseter bulk from skeletal width at the jaw line, which is the core identifiability question.
No practitioner or sculpting-art sources (Polycount, BlenderArtists, ArtStation) on masseter or temporalis form were found.
Temporal hollowing incidence after pterional craniotomy (87-100% in a summary) and the attribution of [23] are unconfirmed.
The year of [49] is unclear: the harvest says 2024, but the PMC ID suggests about 2020.

muscles-mid-face.title: Muscles of the mid face
muscles-mid-face.summary: I wrote the note from scratch because no earlier draft existed. It is about 2,670 words before Sources and follows the required structure: key facts by muscle (zygomaticus major and minor, levator labii superioris, levator labii superioris alaeque nasi, levator anguli oris, risorius, nasalis, buccinator), plus the modiolus, the nasolabial fold and the smile. It has four reference tables: attachments, layers and FACS/ARKit mappings; sourced variation and EMG figures; smile movement and population frequencies; and muscle dimensions as weak priors. The Blender section has nine steps covering capt
algorithmic: Add skull-anchored zmj_origin_L/R (about 5-20 mm anterior and 0-10 mm inferior to zygion, sigma about 6 mm), lao_origin_L/R and infraorbital_foramen_L/R. Add derived modiolus_L/R (12 ± 4 mm lateral and -3 ± 5 mm vertical from cheilion, consistent with the lower-face note).
Fit the nasolabial fold as a curve by image-space chamfer distance against per-view traced polylines, not as point correspondences. Weight by contrast and light angle.

Nasolabial fold priors: upper end 2-6 mm lateral and 0-5 mm above the alar crease point; lower end 11 ± 4 mm lateral and 0 ± 6 mm vertical from cheilion; length 30-50 mm. Rest depth is half-normal with scale 0.5-1 mm under age 30 and 2-4 mm over 55.

Expression basis: per-muscle linear actuators of the Waters 1987 type (origin, insertion, angular zone, radial falloff), with zygomaticus major angular zone about 35 degrees and peak mouth-corner movement 10-15 mm. Give each AU a direction prior with angular sigma 15-25 degrees (unit vectors in the data JSON, face3d head frame).

Neutral gate: score frames on mouth-corner angle to the stomion line, mouth width against its multi-frame minimum, upper-lip height, fold contrast and cheek height, plus MediaPipe-style blendshape scores when available. Fit identity to a robust multi-frame median.

Put a half-normal prior with sigma about 0.05 on AU weights in neutral frames. Orthogonalize the midface identity basis against the AU9-14 displacement subspace so identity cannot absorb a slight smile.
Variant switches zmj_bifid (p about 0.3), zmn_present (p 0.5-0.9) and risorius_present only scale expression bases and never alter neutral geometry.
Warp stiffness: upper lip 0.3, cheek fat 0.5, zygomatic body 1.5-2.0. Along the nasolabial fold loop, anchor position to the traced curve and cut bending weight to 0.2-0.3 so a crease can form.
Fit left and right sides independently, with a symmetry prior of sigma about 1.5 mm on neutral fold endpoints. Never symmetrize smile vectors, because one-sided levator anguli oris weakness is real.
takeaways: Zygomaticus major is the smile muscle (AU12). It runs from the zygomatic bone near the zygomaticotemporal suture to the modiolus and pulls the mouth corner up, out and back around the dental arch. Risorius is not the smile muscle: it produces a lateral, fearful stretch (AU20).

The nasolabial fold is a fixed fat-boundary hinge made by the elevators' insertions into the skin. It is present from infancy. Sculpt it as a convex cheek overhang above a flat, tethered lip, not as a V-groove. Which muscle dominates the fold (the levator labii group plus zygomaticus minor, or zygomaticus major plus the elevators) is contested.

A FACS-consistent split of the fold for driving expressions: the upper third goes with levator labii superioris alaeque nasi and levator labii superioris (AU9/10), the middle with zygomaticus minor (AU11), and the lower part with zygomaticus major and levator anguli oris (AU12/13).

Anatomy varies a lot: zygomaticus major is bifid in about 34% of specimens (sourced secondhand), zygomaticus minor is often absent (44% pattern in one series) and risorius is inconsistent. MRI and CT cannot resolve these muscles in vivo, so they belong in expression priors, never in identity geometry.

The levator labii superioris alaeque nasi origin (frontal process of the maxilla vs medial orbital wall), the buccinator insertion and the nature of the modiolus are all contested. A 2026 study adds a buccinator attachment at the pterygoid hamulus.

Use a smiling photo only to locate fixed lines (nasolabial fold, dimples), never to set cheek volume. A smile key that moves only the mouth corners gives a 'Joker' look: the upper lip, cheek mass, fold endpoint and nostril must move too.
gaps: No sourced quantitative nasolabial fold geometry (position, length, angle, depth by age, sex or ancestry); all fold priors are heuristic.
No sourced muscle thickness, length or width norms for the midface elevators (ultrasound or cadaver).
The absence rates for zygomaticus minor and risorius, and how they differ by ancestry, were not found.
The primary sample size of the 1998 bifid zygomaticus major study is unconfirmed, and so is its link to cheek dimples.

Full texts of the 2025 zygomaticus variability review, the nasolabial fold micro-CT study (whose year is also unconfirmed) and the 2026 zygomaticus major EMG study were not opened. It is unclear whether that study's 'contraction %' means strain or a percentage of maximum voluntary contraction.
Commissure excursion and smile-direction norms, and the Rubin and Tjan smile-type percentages, come from training knowledge only.
Titles for PMC3498722 and PMC7773723 were not captured. Code availability and licences for the biomechanical and EMG papers (arXiv 2111.06517 and 2503.09556) were not checked.
No open Blender FACS rig that maps these muscles to shape keys was identified.

muscles-upper-face.title: Muscles of the upper face
muscles-upper-face.summary:
Wrote a new note on the upper-face muscles; there was no earlier draft, so the harvest was the only input. It covers frontalis, corrugator supercilii, procerus, depressor supercilii, orbicularis oculi (orbital and palpebral parts) and levator palpebrae superioris, with sourced attachments, actions and nerve supply.

The note has five parts:
- **Disputes:** frontalis and corrugator insertions, the level of the procerus insertion, the origin of the palpebral orbicularis, and whether depressor supercilii is a separate muscle.
- **Numbers:** 3 tables (sourced values; dimensions and excursions; fib
algorithmic: Add landmarks brow_peak_L/R, upper_lid_apex_L/R, lower_lid_nadir_L/R, crease_apex_L/R and a bone-layer supraorbitale_L/R. Treat brow points as hair: sigma 3-5 mm against bone.

Build the expression basis from per-muscle masks with displacement along fibre lines. Frontalis moves +y with amplitude decaying to a per-subject galea_junction_height. Add a parameter frontalis_upper_mobility in [0,1] with a prior skewed low, because only the lower forehead moved in 53% of one cohort. Corrugator moves medial-inferior, about (-0.93,-0.34,+0.1) on the left side; procerus and depressor supercilii move -y; orbital orbicularis contracts toward the medial canthus. Project this subspace out of the identity fit.
For the forehead in expression warps, use a sliding-on-bone constraint: tangential motion is free and normal motion has sigma about 0.3 mm, mimicking the subgaleal glide plane.

Keep lid margins on a sphere of globe radius plus 0.5-1 mm, and rotate lids about the eyeball centre. Couple upper-lid elevation to eye pitch at about 0.9±0.15. Add a hinge penalty on sclera above the iris unless at least 2 views show it.

Priors in mm: MRD1 4.5±1; MRD2 5±1; crease height 8±2 (European women), 7±2 (men), 4±2.5 (East Asian, with a no-crease Bernoulli term), 6.5±3 if unknown; left-right brow difference 0±1.5; depressor supercilii insertion 13.5±2; corrugator lateral end 35±7 from the midline; neutral-frame action-unit weights sigma 0.1. Clamps: brow raise at most 15 mm, frown brow-head travel at most 8 mm.
Neutral gate: drop brow and forehead residuals when brow height is more than 2.5 mm above the subject's multi-frame median, or when brow blendshapes exceed 0.2-0.3.
Relative warp stiffness: lid margins 3.0, upper tarsus 2.0, medial canthus 2.5, lateral canthus 1.5, brow 0.7, forehead 0.5 (sliding), glabella 0.4 with a crease allowance.
Store a per-vertex wrinkle orientation field and generate wrinkle normal maps driven by action units, perpendicular to it. Keep static and dynamic line parameters separate.
takeaways: Frontalis is the only brow elevator. It stops near the temporal fusion line, so the brow tail has no elevator but is pulled down by orbital orbicularis. This explains lateral hooding and why forehead lines stop short of the temple.

Dynamic lines run perpendicular to the muscle pull: horizontal forehead lines (frontalis), vertical and oblique glabellar lines (corrugator, depressor supercilii), a horizontal radix line (procerus), and crow's feet radiating from the lateral canthus (orbital orbicularis).

A 'neutral' photo is easily spoiled by frontalis raising the brows to compensate for ptotic or hooded lids, by upgaze, by squinting in bright light, and by lid height that follows gaze. Use the close-eyes-then-open-slowly routine at eye-level camera height.
Glabellar frowns were asymmetric in about 62% of one 3D sample, and 1-3 mm brow asymmetry is common, so never mirror the brows or the dynamic keys.
Cosmetic treatment changes what the photo shows: toxin, energy devices (about a 2 mm lift) and fillers. A flat forehead with a peaked lateral brow means toxin, not anatomy. Ask the subject.

Upper-lid crease height is set by where the levator aponeurosis inserts into the skin and differs strongly by ancestry. It should be an observed parameter with a wide, ancestry-dependent prior, not a fixed template feature.

Attachment details are disputed in the sources (frontalis and corrugator insertions, the procerus insertion level, depressor supercilii as a separate muscle), but not in ways that change surface form much.
gaps: No primary in-vivo measurements (thickness, length, fibre angle) for frontalis, corrugator, procerus or orbicularis were found in the harvest.
The four-shape frontalis classification and the figure of 41% of corrugators piercing both layers have no confirmed source URL.
Full text for the 2025 glabellar 3D study is missing: its sample size (about 29 is inferred) and its definition of 'lateral pattern'.
The Hur and Lee 2022 depressor supercilii study is unlocated, and Cook 2001 is available only as a hosted abstract.
The 3D frontalis displacement study gives no year, and the 'earlier study' it contrasts with is unidentified.
No sourced numbers exist for lid crease height, tarsal height, levator excursion or brow excursion; all are expert knowledge.
Ancestry-specific differences in muscle patterns are covered only by the 103-patient African-descent glabellar study.
No sourced coefficient for how the upper lid follows vertical gaze.
No community material from Polycount or BlenderArtists, and Reddit was blocked.
The title of the forehead ultrasound layer study (PMC11635371) was not captured.

neural-head-avatars.title: NeRF and Gaussian-splatting head avatars
neural-head-avatars.summary: Neither the harvest (/home/user/minedesign/research/_raw/harvests/neural-head-avatars.json) nor an earlier draft existed, so the note is written entirely from expert knowledge (56 🧠, 14 ↔️, no URLs cited). It covers lineage from NeRFace/NHA/IMavatar through PointAvatar, INSTA, NeRSemble, GaussianAvatars and MonoGaussianAvatar to 2024-2025 successors (FlashAvatar, SplattingAvatar, Gaussian Head Avatar, 3D Gaussian Blendshapes, NPGA, RGCA/URAvatar, SurFhead, CAP4D, Avat3r, LAM, GAGAvatar, GAF). Central message: neural avatars are appearance models; for Blender sculpting their value is the refine
algorithmic: Interoperate rather than reimplement: import tracker outputs (beta, per-frame psi/pose, K, [R|t]) as initialisation and avatar outputs as observations; convert FLAME metres to engine mm (x1000) and undo NeRF scene normalisation.
PLY importer for 3DGS SH3: 62 props; alpha = sigmoid(opacity), s = exp(scale), normalise quaternion (w,x,y,z), rgb = 0.5 + 0.28209479*f_dc.

Gaussian-centre data term: normal = rotation column of smallest scale; keep if alpha >= 0.5 (0.3-0.7), s_min/s_max <= 0.3, s_max <= 5 mm, skin region, |n_i.n_mesh| >= cos45; point-to-plane residual with sigma_i = sqrt(sigma0^2 + s_min^2), sigma0 = 0.5 mm multi-view / 1.0-1.5 mm monocular; weight alpha; Geman-McClure c = 2-3 mm.
Specular gate: down-weight the top 10-20% of Gaussians by ||f_rest||/||f_dc|| (highlights, eyes).
Prefer rendered median depth (2DGS/TSDF) with sigma = 1 mm*(1+|tan theta|); drop pixels with grazing angle > 70 deg.
Coverage map per FLAME triangle (bound-Gaussian count, mean opacity); in sparse/oversized regions fall back to beta prior and symmetry (sigma_sym 1.5-3 mm).
Priors: beta ~ N(0,1); neutral psi ~ N(0,0.3^2); post-3DMM offsets Laplacian-regularised sigma 2-3 mm capped at 5 mm; IPD scale prior (61-64 mm, SD 3-4) only without a scale object.
Neutral keyframe selection: score ||psi|| + w|jaw| + eyelid closure - sharpness, keep best 5-15 across yaw, fit beta jointly.
Camera conversion: c2w_blender = c2w_cv * diag(1,-1,-1,1); lens = f_px*36/W with Sensor Fit Horizontal; shift from principal point via to_blender_camera.
Mesh extraction defaults for a 0.30-0.35 m head box: marching cubes 512^3 (~0.6-0.7 mm), TSDF voxel 0.5-1 mm with 3-5 voxel truncation over 60-150 views, Poisson depth 9-10.
QA outputs: leave-one-view-out reprojection, per-region Hausdorff fit-vs-surface (alert > ~3 mm on skin), scale-mode tag, commercial_ok provenance per asset.
takeaways: Neural head avatars optimise re-rendering, not surface accuracy; papers report PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, never mm geometry, so render quality is not evidence of likeness.

For Blender sculpting, harvest three by-products: the refined FLAME fit plus cameras (clean topology, scale), camera-registered neutral reference renders from virtual near-orthographic cameras, and a confidence-weighted point/depth signal.

Mesh-bound Gaussian designs (GaussianAvatars, FlashAvatar, SplattingAvatar) map directly onto FLAME and Blender rigs; free-deformation designs (PointAvatar, MonoGaussianAvatar) do not give a FLAME-aligned canonical mesh.

Only surfel (2DGS/SurFhead) and SDF (IMavatar, MonoNPHM) routes produce surfaces close to sculpt quality; project them onto a subdivided base only in a skin mask (never hair, eyes, mouth interior, ear backs).
Export the neutral base from the most neutral tracked frame(s), not psi=0, because FLAME's zero expression is not the subject's relaxed face.
Few-shot diffusion/feed-forward avatars (CAP4D, Avat3r, LAM, GAGAvatar, GAF) hallucinate unseen regions; treat them as plausible guesses, not measurements of the person.
Licences are the main blocker: Inria 3DGS and instant-ngp are non-commercial, gsplat is Apache-2.0, FLAME is research-licensed with an unverified 'Open' variant, NeRSemble is research-only.
gaps: No web harvest or prior draft existed for this topic: zero sourced or verified facts; every method detail, venue and number is expert knowledge pending verification.
No millimetre geometry benchmark for animatable head avatars is known; geometry ratings in the method catalogue are author judgement.
Primitive counts, training times and render speeds are order-of-magnitude recollections, not checked against papers.
2025-2026 successors beyond those named (and their code availability/licences) are unknown; 'best method' is time-sensitive.
Native Gaussian-splat support in Blender (4.x/5.x, 2026) and current state of third-party splat add-ons (e.g. KIRI Engine 3DGS Render) unverified.
GaussianAvatars, VHAP, FlashAvatar, SplattingAvatar, SurFhead code licences unverified; FLAME 2023 Open terms unverified.
Exact GaussianAvatars output file layout (binding indices, FLAME param files) and whether its tracker adds static per-vertex offsets not confirmed.
Whether relightable avatars (RGCA, URAvatar) yield measurably better normals for sculpting is open.

nose.title: Nose anatomy and morphology
nose.summary: Neither designated input existed: there was no nose harvest and no earlier nose.md. I wrote the note from scratch. The 39 cited URLs are reused only from sibling harvests in research/_raw/harvests and from anatomy/skull-osteology.md; the note marks the latter "via" and says where every URL came from. The note covers: (1) the three-tier anatomy (nasal bones and keystone, ULC T-vault, alar crura, cartilage-free alar rim, scroll, septum, ANS); (2) surface landmarks, with the conflicting definitions of n′, prn, sn, al, ac and sbal; (3) tip anatomy (tip-defining points, supratip break, c′ double br
algorithmic: Nose parameter block with sex-specific μ/σ: radix depth 12/11 ± 3 mm; n–sn 54.5/50.5 ± 3.3/3.1; n–prn 50/45.5 ± 3.5; sn–prn 20/18.5 ± 2; al–al 34.9/31.4 ± 2.1/2.0, or 36/33 ± 4 when the population is unknown; al–al − ac–ac 4 ± 1.5; nasolabial angle 100/105 ± 9°; nasofrontal angle 125/130 ± 7°; signed hump 1/0 ± 1.5 mm; supratip break 0.5/1 ± 0.7; columellar show 3 ± 1.2; tip deviation Laplace σ 1.2 mm; nostril asymmetry ± 0.8 mm.
Apply the nasofacial angle or the Goode ratio as a prior, never both, since Goode, Crumley and nasofacial are the same triangle. Give aesthetic ideals a weight of at most 0.1 of the population prior.

Observation model: prn σ 2.5% of IOD with a 1–2 mm bias allowed toward the estimated specular highlight; sn σ 1.5% of IOD. Map detector alar points to ac or sbal, and take al from an edge term on the frontal alar contour.

Profile silhouette chamfer term along n′→prn→c′→sn with tangent sliding. ¾ silhouettes constrain dorsal width and alar-groove depth. Build profile ratios from midline points only, because off-profile yaw shifts ac by x·sin ψ.

Depth–distance coupling: with frontal-only data, projection and camera distance trade off. Fix distance from multi-view or a metric cue such as the iris, and let the projection prior dominate when there is no profile.
Hard hinge constraints: skin ≥ 1.5 mm over the nasal bones; columella below the alar rim with 0–7 mm show; prn in front of sn and ac; ac 8–16 mm behind sn; no self-intersection of the nostril rims.

Template warp handles with stable vertex IDs for n′, skin rhinion, supratip, the tip-defining points (L/R), prn, c′, sn, al, ac and sbal (L/R) and the nostril apex (L/R). Use ARAP or biharmonic deformation with high rigidity on the vestibule loops.
Down-weight a photo's nose observations when AU12, AU9 or AU38 is detected. Evaluate with per-feature mm and degree errors rather than a single RMS.
takeaways: Only the bony upper third (nasion to rhinion, about 3 mm of cover) follows the skull. Tip, alae and columella are weakly predictable from the aperture: 26 of 76 nose–aperture relations were significant and RV < 0.4. So the photos, especially profile and basal views, must supply them.

Width reads in the frontal view. Projection, rotation, the hump or supratip break and columellar show read almost only in profile, ¾ and basal views. A basal ('worm's-eye') shot is the most-missed reference.

The nose is the most perspective-sensitive feature. The tip is the nearest facial point, about 30 mm in front of the alar base and 100 mm in front of the tragion, so close photos inflate it. Pitch moves the tip about 0.5 mm per degree relative to n′ and the alar base.
Goode (0.55–0.60), Crumley (3:4:5) and the nasofacial angle (33–37°) describe one triangle. Encode only one as a prior, and use aesthetic ideals only as warnings.
al ≠ ac ≠ sbal: detector 'alar' points sit at the alar base, so take al from the frontal alar contour; al–al exceeds ac–ac by about 2–6 mm of flare.

Keep real asymmetry (tip and columella deviation of 0–3 mm, nostril differences) as explicit parameters, never snapped to x = 0, and gate out smiling photos, since a smile drops the tip and widens the alae.
gaps: No nose-specific web harvest exists. Every numeric angle and ratio norm (nasolabial, nasofrontal, nasofacial, nasomental, columella–lobule, Goode, Byrd, Simons, Baum) is expert knowledge or contested, with no URL.

No sourced population-specific nasal norms beyond al–al proxies (alare–midline n=297, southern Spain ratios, Malay width with an unclear definition). No sourced East Asian or African-descent nasal angle or projection data.
Tip, supratip and columella soft-tissue thickness, nostril shape and axis norms, and columella length are unsourced.
No nose-specific error figures for 3DMM or regression methods, e.g. projection error on NoW or REALY nose regions.
MediaPipe alar and nose indices are unverified, and the anatomical meaning of individual dlib indices is unsourced; only the 27–35 block is sourced.
The size of the selfie effect (Ward 2018), against the geometric prediction, is unverified.
Several sources have no year or confirmed title (search-snippet provenance), e.g. PMC 5017614, the USP thesis and the Taylor & Francis chapter.

open-source-pipelines.title: Open-source end-to-end photo-to-3D-face pipelines
open-source-pipelines.summary:
Wrote the open-source photo-to-3D-face pipelines note (about 2,800 body words). This topic had no harvest file and no earlier draft, so the note reuses 30 real URLs from sibling harvests and marks each with the harvest it came from (multi-view-fitting, single-image-regression, identity-embeddings, facs-expressions, craniometric-landmarks, blender-face-addons, blender-version-status-2026). Everything else is author knowledge marked 🧠.

The note covers 14 pipelines and groups them three ways:
- per-image regressors: DECA, EMOCA, MICA, SMIRK, 3DDFA_V2, Deep3DFaceRecon_pytorch, HRN, FaceVerse;
- o
algorithmic: Adapter contract per backend: {backend, version, licence_code, licence_assets, topology_id, units, axes, camera_model in {weak_persp, affine, perspective}, K, R, t, convention, landmarks{scheme, xy, sigma}, beta, psi, jaw, mesh_path, measured|generated}. Refuse any mesh whose topology_id is unknown.
Implement a numpy FLAME evaluator, v = LBS(T + B_S·beta + B_E·psi + B_P(theta)), from a one-time pkl-to-npz conversion, so every FLAME backend reduces to parameters with no chumpy and no mesh export.
Identity prior from MICA: per-component median over photos, sigma_k = max(0.3, spread across photos) for k <= 100, sigma = 1 above. DECA floor 0.6. Huber vertex scale 1.4 mm (MICA) or 1.8 mm (DECA).
Log-scale prior sigma: 0.05 for MICA, 0.10 for non-metric backends, 0.01 with a user measurement. Log-focal sigma: 0.03 with EXIF, 0.15–0.2 without.
Landmark sigma: 1–1.5 % IOD for inner points; 2–4 % IOD for contour and brow points, inflated by 1/cos(yaw), with sliding contour correspondences.
Neutral-gated photos: psi ~ N(0, 0.3²) per component, jaw sigma 2–3°. Rotation prior from a 3DDFA_V2 or SMIRK initialiser: sigma 5°. Never initialise from 3DDFA_V2 beyond about 90° yaw.

Camera conversion to Blender: OpenCV diag(1,−1,−1); PyTorch3D diag(−1,1,−1); lens_mm = f_px·sensor_mm/W_px; shift_x = (W/2 − cx)/max(W,H); shift_y = (cy − H/2)/max(W,H); weak-perspective Z0 = 2f/(s·W_crop).

Consensus weighting: down-weight views where backends disagree on beta or pose by more than about 2 sigma. Photometric terms are opt-in, used only under even lighting. Propagate the union of licence flags to every derived shape key.
takeaways: Every runnable open photo-to-3D face pipeline is a research codebase. Assume Linux plus NVIDIA CUDA, pinned PyTorch, model files you register to download (FLAME, BFM) and non-commercial terms on at least one of code, weights or rasteriser.
Per-image regressors (DECA, MICA, SMIRK, 3DDFA_V2, Deep3D) take milliseconds, but they use weak-perspective or affine cameras. Use them as initialisers and never let them set depth or scale.

Offline FLAME trackers (flame-head-tracker at about 0.9–1.9 s/frame on an RTX 4090; VHAP; metrical-tracker) assume video or a calibrated rig. Unordered stills taken with different cameras need the project's own bundle adjustment.
What Blender needs is a mesh on fixed topology (FLAME 5,023 vertices, Deep3D 35,709, 3DDFA_V2 about 38k) plus cameras and landmarks. Import with vertex order kept and assert the vertex count.
Units vary wildly: FLAME in m, the MICA demo possibly in mm, Deep3D about dm, 3DDFA_V2 in image pixels, MediaPipe in cm. Settle them with one anthropometric measurement.

Install traps: chumpy breaks on NumPy 1.24 or later, so convert the FLAME pkl to npz; PyTorch3D and nvdiffrast builds; Blackwell GPUs against old CUDA pins; no Apple Silicon support; Google Drive checkpoint quotas.
The shippable default should be MediaPipe (Apache-2.0) plus our own numpy fitter plus an MPFB2 (GPL) template. Research backends are opt-in, run outside Blender, and carry licence flags.
gaps: This topic had no harvest file and no earlier draft. All URLs are reused from sibling harvests, and per-pipeline install details, output formats and licences are mostly 🧠.
Code licences are unverified for SMIRK, VHAP, flame-head-tracker, Pixel3DMM, HRN and FaceVerse, and FLAME 2023 Open's terms are unresolved.
There are no measured VRAM figures for any pipeline; the GPU needs in Table 1 are estimates.
It is unknown which repos currently work with Python 3.11+, NumPy 2 and CUDA 12.8 / Blackwell GPUs.
The units of MICA's demo output (mm or m) and 3DDFA_V2's exact vertex count are from memory and need checking against code.
No NoW or REALY numbers were found for SMIRK, Pixel3DMM or HRN, and there are no independent comparisons of the trackers on still-photo identity accuracy.
It is unknown whether flame-head-tracker or VHAP support multi-view stills with different intrinsics.

photogrammetry-heads.title: Photogrammetry of human heads
photogrammetry-heads.summary: I wrote the photogrammetry-heads note (about 2,620 words of prose), its sources JSON (empty sources list, 18 references by name) and a data JSON with 10 tables. Neither listed input existed (no harvest at _raw/harvests/photogrammetry-heads.json, no earlier draft), so every claim is expert knowledge (🧠) or contested (↔️). I cited no URLs from other topics' harvests. Cross-references go to sibling notes by path, plus _raw/harvests/anthropometric-norms.json, which holds sourced stereophotogrammetry accuracy figures. I computed the capture-geometry tables by arithmetic: image resolution (mm/px) by
algorithmic: Add a camera importer (proposed face3d/io/sfm_import.py) for COLMAP text, Metashape XML, RealityScan XMP and AliceVision .sfm into Camera. Accept only square-pixel models with k1/k2 distortion; otherwise require undistorted images. Convert pixel conventions: OpenCV-convention sources need +0.5 px against Camera.centered. Validate every import by reprojecting the tool's sparse points; the mean must match the tool's reported error and be under 1 px.

Never let landmark residuals move imported cameras. Detector noise is about 1–1.5% of inter-ocular distance (10–14 px at 0.067 mm/px), versus about 0.5 px for the camera solve. Use estimate_focal=False or f_prior_log_sigma of 0.005–0.01 and freeze poses; if refining, use rotation sigma 0.05° and centre sigma 0.5 mm. Then triangulate_points and umeyama to the template.
Add a ScaleRef (two 3D points, length in mm, sigma). Combine references by inverse variance, warn when they disagree by more than 1%, and export a scale-mode tag.

Scan-to-template fitting: fit_template_to_landmarks, then point-to-plane non-rigid ICP regularised with laplacian_deform or ReducedDeformer. Lower the stiffness over 5–8 stages. Reject correspondences beyond 3 sigma (10 mm cap coarse, 3–5 mm fine), with normals more than 45° apart, or on scan boundaries. Use a Huber loss at about 1.5 sigma. Residual sigma: 0.3–0.5 mm for rigs, 0.5–1 mm for the single-camera central face, 2–3 mm for ears, hairline and under the chin.
Give zero weight to eyes, inner mouth, nostrils, brows, lashes, hair and beard, using face-parsing labels projected onto scan vertices by majority vote over the views where each vertex is visible.
Under hair, use a one-sided constraint: penalise the template only when it lies outside the scanned surface, with a weak 5–15 mm inward prior (1–3 mm under a cap).
For scans, raise Priors.sigma_sym to 3–5 mm (the default 2 mm suits landmark-only fits) so the scan's real asymmetry survives.

Coverage QA: for each vertex, require at least 3 views with incidence under 60–70° and a largest triangulation angle of at least 10–15°. Otherwise tag the vertex as prior-driven and show a heat-map in Blender.

Movement QA: check residuals per view and per region against a rigid triangulation, and drop a view only for the eye or mouth region where it is an outlier. Reject blink frames (eye aspect ratio below about 0.2) and rank frames by variance-of-Laplacian sharpness.
Capture planner: from target mm/px and sensor, compute distance, stations per ring and expected depth sigma before shooting.
takeaways: Geometry is not the limit: triangulation precision at head-portrait resolution is about 0.05–0.25 mm. Real live-sitter errors of 0.5–2 mm come from movement of the face itself, skin shine and low texture, and hair or eyes, far more than from the choice of solver.

1 mm of face movement is 7–20 px at 0.05–0.15 mm/px, while dense matching tolerates about 1–2 px. Keep each ring of photos to 20–30 s or less and the whole capture to 1–3 min or less, with fixed gaze and a fixed lip and teeth position.
Whole-head sway is harmless if the background is masked or plain, because the camera solve absorbs it. Against a textured room it splits the solve. Apply masks before alignment.

Single-camera recipe: 3–4 rings at 10–20° steps (60–120 photos); 0.8–1.5 m at 50–105 mm full-frame equivalent; f/8–f/11; 1/200 s or faster or a strobe; ISO 400 or lower; manual exposure and white balance. On phones, lock the 2–3× lens and stop it auto-switching lenses.
Scale must be rigid with the head or measured on the sitter: a 300 mm scale bar gives 0.17% (0.25 mm), caliper head breadth about 1%, and a population prior 4–6%.
Corneas, hair, beards, brows, lashes, ear backs and the lip seal reconstruct badly. Hair sits 5–30 mm outside the skin, so rebuild eyes and hair by hand and sculpt the scalp inside the hair blob.

In Blender, keep 1 unit = 1 m at true size. Orient to the Frankfurt plane, decimate to 1–2 M triangles, voxel remesh at 0.5–1 mm for sculpting, wrap a 5–20k-quad base, and bake detail from the raw scan.

Which solver is best is contested and capture quality dominates. RealityScan is fast and detailed (CUDA), Metashape is robust and runs on macOS, COLMAP is open and scriptable, and Meshroom is a free GUI that needs the sensor width in its database.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so the note has zero sourced (📄) or verified (✅) claims.
Published accuracy of single-camera and smartphone photogrammetry on live faces versus 3dMD or structured light needs real studies with sample sizes.
No head-specific benchmark compares COLMAP, Meshroom, RealityScan and Metashape.

Current software status is unconfirmed: RealityScan 2.x licence and pricing, Metashape editions and prices, Meshroom release and CUDA requirement, whether COLMAP has integrated GLOMAP, and Apple Object Capture platform limits.
Each tool's camera-export conventions (Metashape transforms, RealityScan XMP fields, AliceVision principal point) need checking against official docs.
Physiology figures (blink rate, seated head sway, breathing-driven neck motion in mm) are approximate and unsourced.
Studio rig camera counts and synchronisation tolerances are unsourced.
How well learned matchers (LightGlue, MASt3R, VGGT) or Gaussian-splat mesh extraction (2DGS) work on head scans is unknown and changes fast.
Hair-thickness bias over the scalp (5–30 mm) and how much a swim cap compresses hair (1–3 mm) are estimates.

polycount-likeness.title: Polycount: likeness sculpting knowledge
polycount-likeness.summary:
The Polycount likeness note is written, but every claim in it is unverified expert knowledge. Neither input existed: there was no harvest (polycount-likeness.json) and no earlier draft, and no Polycount URL appears anywhere in the library. So the note cites no URLs and the evidence status is 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 62 🧠 / 23 ↔️.

The note covers four areas:
- **How Polycount critiques:** the reference goes beside the render at a matched angle and lens; critics ask for a clay render and wireframes first; paintovers are the most actionable critique but show only one view; and fixes go big shapes first, deta
algorithmic: Stage gates: masses until silhouette chamfer < 2% of n–gn and landmark RMS < 4% IOD; features until detector RMS < 3% IOD (user pins < 1.5%) in all views including one held-out photo; surface passes must not move landmarks > 0.5 mm.
Symmetry schedule: Priors.sigma_sym 1.0 mm (masses), 2.0 mm (features, engine default), 4.0 mm (surface), with sigma_mid fixed at 1.5 mm.
One-sided hinge on hair and beard silhouettes (margin 0–3 mm, no inward pull), plus a cranial prior: g–op 175–205 mm, σ ≈ 7 mm, scalp tissue ≈ 4–8 mm.

Paintover ingestion: dense 2D flow from render to paintover, then solve per-vertex Δx with projection Jacobians, σ_w ≈ 2 px, a cotan Laplacian regulariser and reprojection terms from the other views; reject the edit if another view's RMS rises > 0.5% IOD.

Critique lint from Table A: flag only when the model disagrees with the photos by > 2σ_photo, or by population |z| > 2.5 where no photo sees the feature; never pull a photo-supported feature toward the mean.
Caricature handles: the user tags 3–5 distinctive regions; double their landmark weights and exclude them from prior shrinkage.
Region sliders for the sitter's approval, built on ReducedDeformer with masks (eyes, nose, mouth, jaw, ears, cranium), limited to ±3 mm and exported as named shape keys.
Edge-loop preservation: measure quad angle distortion after RBFWarp, and switch from laplacian_deform to ARAP when cranium or jaw scale changes by more than 10%.
Export likeness check: per-vertex deviation from sculpt to game mesh against Table D (0.2–0.3 mm at lid margins, lip border and alar rim); block 'approved' status if exceeded.
Soft landmarks: hairline σ 3–5 mm, brows σ ≈ 2 mm, never used for camera solving; generate the critique sheet numpy-side for each solved camera.
takeaways: Polycount critique is camera-first: no likeness verdict is meaningful until the render camera matches the photo's distance and FOV; selfies under 0.8 m are for texture and expression only.
The usual crit order (silhouette and head mass, then feature placement, feature shape, surface, shading) maps directly to staged fitting with numeric gates before detail is allowed.
A paintover or liquify critique shows only one view; any 3D change it drives must be checked in every other solved camera and rejected if it worsens them.

Recurring verdicts: cranium and neck too small, eyes too big or proud with paper lids, lips not wrapping the dental arch, ears low or upright, over-symmetric 'cousin' faces, and likeness lost in retopology, baking, shading or hair.
Hair and beard outlines should bound the skull and jaw from outside rather than be fitted; the cranium under hair comes from a prior.
Judge likeness with brows and hairline proxies on and shape with them off; matched key lighting and grayscale reviews beat matcaps for likeness verdicts.
Keep sitter-approval edits reversible (region shape keys) and run a tolerance check on export so likeness survives retopology and baking.
gaps: No Polycount thread or wiki page was harvested; the note has no sourced (📄/✅) facts and no URLs.
Whether any Polycount thread gives quantitative likeness tolerances, in mm or reprojection pixels, is unknown.
There is no frequency count of critique categories in Polycount portrait WIP threads; the ranking given is a synthesis.
Exact names and content of the Polycount wiki's face-topology and edge-loop pages are unverified.
The cheilion-to-labrale-superius profile depth (1.5–2 cm) is uncertain.
The game-head polygon budgets and MetaHuman LOD0 counts are rough and time-sensitive.
The Table D retopology tolerances and the stage-gate thresholds are engineering suggestions to be tuned on synthetic data and real held-out photos.
Current forum activity, AI policies and vendor naming (R3DS/Faceform Wrap) are time-sensitive.

population-variation.title: Craniofacial variation across human populations
population-variation.summary:
Wrote the population-variation note with no inputs to build on: the harvest file and the earlier draft for this topic do not exist. So every claim is expert knowledge or contested (0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 84 🧠 / 27 ↔️), and no URLs are cited. The note points to sibling notes that carry sourced population values (anthropometric-norms, forensic-reconstruction, mouth-lips-teeth, face-perception-likeness).

What the note covers:
- **Within-group vs between-group variance.** Genetic markers put about 85–95% of variance within populations (Lewontin, Rosenberg). Craniometrics put about 11–14% between regions (Re
algorithmic: Balanced pooled prior: μ = (1/K)Σμ_k and Σ = (1/K)Σ[Σ_k + (μ_k−μ)(μ_k−μ)ᵀ]. Never weight groups by training frequency.

Widen per-trait σ by k = σ_pooled/σ_within: al–al and nasal index 2.0–2.5; radix 1.8–2.2; visible en–en 1.8; vermilion and lip protrusion 1.6–1.8; cephalic index 1.6–2.0; nasolabial angle and tip 1.3–1.5; zy–zy and ch–ch 1.2–1.3; n–gn, ex–en, interpupillary distance and ear 1.0–1.15.
When building the shape PCA, keep group-mean offsets as explicit basis vectors with wide priors (σ ≈ half the largest offset) and reweight scans by inverse group frequency.
Optional Gaussian mixture over shape clusters, with uniform weights and responsibilities from geometry only. Never surface or store a cluster as an ethnicity (GDPR Art. 9).
Discrete latents with per-state shape keys: fold {none, palpebral, tarsal, inversus}; crease {absent, low, high}.
true_en = visible_en + δ·medial, with δ ~ HalfNormal(2 mm) when a fold is present and N(0, 0.7 mm) otherwise. Keep narrow priors on interpupillary distance and bony intercanthal width.
Cap the prior at 10–20% of the objective where multi-view data exist. If the radix, tip, lip or occiput estimate is more than 70% prior-determined, request a profile or top view.
Weight landmarks by local contrast and detector confidence. Do not regularise skin tone toward an albedo PCA mean.

Audit: per-group signed bias under 0.25 within-group SD and worst/best group error ratio under 1.2. Benchmarks such as NoW and REALY are not demographically balanced, so their mean errors hide group gaps.
