Default the reference to 'pooled (balanced)'. Label z-scores 'outside reference', and use |z| > 3 to prompt a re-check, never pulling toward the mean.
takeaways: Most facial variation is within populations, but nose width, nasal index, radix height, midface projection, lip fullness and protrusion, folds and creases, and cephalic index have group means 2–4 within-group SDs apart.

These high-variance traits are mostly depth and projection features. Frontal photos constrain them least, so a 3DMM prior trained mostly on European-ancestry scans pulls reconstructions toward European proportions there.
Require profile, basal nose and top-of-head views, and caliper measurements where the subject consents. Never use ethnic templates or ancestry sliders as shortcuts.
The epicanthal fold inflates the visible en–en and shortens the visible fissure. Model it as a discrete skin web over a true canthus that stays in place.
'Facial flatness' means a low radix plus forward malars, not cheeks pushed back.
Use a balanced pooled prior with equal group weights and a variance widening factor k of 1.0–2.5 depending on the trait. Store no inferred ethnicity, and audit signed bias per group.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed, so there are zero sourced or verified facts. Every number is recalled.

There are no sourced multi-population 3D soft-tissue norms. South Asian, Middle Eastern and North African, Indigenous American, Pacific, Aboriginal Australian, Central Asian and admixed groups are missing.
Radix (sellion) projection and lid-crease height norms in millimetres are not pinned down.
The African-ancestry lid-crease height was not recalled.
The training composition and licences of 2024–2026 3DMMs and landmark detectors are unknown (time-sensitive).
Quantitative evidence of reconstruction bias per group, as signed errors on nose, lips and radix, is not sourced.

portrait-lighting-compare.title: Matching photo lighting and verifying likeness renders
portrait-lighting-compare.summary:
Rewrote /home/user/minedesign/research/blender/portrait-lighting-compare.md (about 2,700 real words, 2,340 before Sources). It keeps every sourced fact from the earlier draft, its 13 citations and its verification results: the orientation-first lighting method stays ✅ via [6][7], and nothing was refuted. The obsolete search-budget notes are gone. I added expert knowledge, marked 🧠, in these areas:
- **Lighting physics:** order-2 spherical harmonics capture diffuse shading, so the sharp lights in an HDRI can only be recovered from cast shadows, catchlights and highlights.
- **Reading the photo'
algorithmic: Camera prior: log-focal σ ≈ 0.05–0.1 when EXIF focal length and sensor are known and the image is uncropped; the engine default 0.35 with 24–200 mm (35 mm-equivalent) hypotheses when the focal length is guessed. Principal point fixed at the image centre unless crop data exists (σ ≈ 1.5 % of width if freed).
Metric scale prior from the visible iris diameter, 11.7 ± 0.5 mm (to verify), to break the focal/depth ambiguity alongside anthropometric priors.

Blender export contract: lens = f_px·sensor_w/W_px with Sensor Fit = Horizontal, and shift = offset_px / (sensor-fit dimension). The engine currently divides by max(W,H); fix it or switch fit, then add a round-trip render test asserting sub-pixel landmark agreement.

Lighting stage 1: SH9 per RGB channel (27 parameters) by linear least squares, E(n)=Σ Â_l L_lm Y_lm(n) with Â=(π, 2π/3, π/4). Huber δ≈0.05 linear. Exclude eyes, brows, lips, nostrils, hair, the top 2–5 % brightest pixels and n·v<0.3. Ridge on band 2. Weak light-from-above prior: elevation N(30°,25°), azimuth N(0°,60°).

Lighting stage 2: key direction from the band-1 vector (L11, L1-1, L10) → (x, y, z), ambient from L00. Refine by maximising IoU between rendered and segmented nose/brow cast shadows; set sun Angle or area-light Size from the penumbra. Calibrate intensities against a rendered grey sphere, not closed-form watts.

Verification gates G1–G4: landmark NME with point-to-curve distance for contours (start ≤2–3 % IOD, landmark σ 1.5–3 % IOD); contour mean ≤1 % of face height on unoccluded jaw and cheek; photometric MAE, SSIM and LPIPS/ꟻLIP per region only after the geometry gates pass; ArcFace cosine divided by the photo-vs-photo baseline. Never auto-accept on photometric or identity scores.

Require at least 2 views at least 30° apart in yaw before reporting depth-dependent likeness. Store a reproducibility record (Blender version, engine and sampling, colour management, photo colour space, camera and light parameters, seed) with every comparison.
Generate the compositor graph from Python (Alpha Over, Mix Factor, Difference → BW × alpha × mask → Map Range → Color Ramp, Split) behind a Blender-version guard for the 5.0 node-group API change.
takeaways: Solve the camera before sculpting, from landmarks rather than vanishing-point tools, and export lens, sensor width, sensor fit, shift and resolution together. Judge alignment only in camera view, never with the free-viewport lens, which reads about 2x because of a built-in zoom factor.

Lighting: match direction first and balance second. This is the one ✅ fact, from two independent tutorials. Read the key from the nose-shadow pattern, catchlights and penumbra, and record the key:fill ratio in stops, not labels, because the two label conventions disagree by up to about 0.6 stop.

Diffuse skin shading constrains only about 9 SH lighting coefficients per channel. The exact HDRI is not recoverable from a portrait; sharp-light information comes only from cast shadows, catchlights and highlights.

Blender composites in linear light and its blends ignore alpha. Mask Difference maps with render alpha × face mask, use the Standard view transform (not AgX) while comparing, and never compare against After Effects or Photoshop numbers.

Gate verification in order: geometry first (landmark error, contour distance), then photometric scores (SSIM, LPIPS/ꟻLIP, ΔE00), then identity similarity normalised by a photo-vs-photo baseline. Lighting error looks like shape error, so never auto-accept on photometric or identity scores.

Check at least front, ¾ and profile views. A single view can be matched by a wrong shape paired with a wrong focal length, and selfie-distance photos exaggerate the nose by roughly 30% (🧠, to verify).
gaps: No input source gives a numeric value for lighting-match accuracy, landmark or photometric thresholds, or colour-difference magnitudes. All numbers in the note are 🧠 or derived.
Blender 5.x manual and API pages (camera shift units, background-image settings, compositor node names and Python identifiers) were not retrieved; the 5.0 Cameras URL [13] is listed but unread.

Lens-shift units and the viewport zoom factor come from memory of Blender's source. The possible engine bug for portrait-orientation photos needs a real round-trip render test; no Blender binary is available in this environment.
No sources on how accurate learned portrait light estimators (SfSNet, Sun 2019, LeGendre 2020, DiffusionLight 2024) are once converted to a Blender rig.
The anthropometric nose-tip-to-ear depth (Δ ≈ 0.12 m) used in the perspective table is assumed, not sourced; it should come from the anthropometry notes.
Gate thresholds (NME, contour distance, IoU) are engineering defaults and need calibrating on consented portraits with known cameras.
Most sourced claims are single forum or vendor pages (📄); only the orientation-first lighting method has two independent sources.

reddit-face-from-photos.title: Reddit: face-from-photos problems and answers
reddit-face-from-photos.summary:
I rewrote the note at /home/user/minedesign/research/community/reddit-face-from-photos.md (about 2,600 words of prose, tables excluded) and wrote /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/reddit-face-from-photos.json and /home/user/minedesign/research/data/reddit-face-from-photos.json.

There was no harvest file for this topic, and the earlier draft had no sourced facts. So the sources list is empty and every claim is 🧠 (58) or ↔️ (9). The note synthesises long-running discussion on r/blender, r/3Dmodeling, r/photogrammetry, r/ZBrush and r/computergraphics. It covers:
- **Routes and verdicts:** f
algorithmic: Check inputs before fitting. Parse EXIF fields (FocalLengthIn35mmFilm, LensModel, DateTimeOriginal, Orientation); flag missing EXIF, crops and front-camera lenses; warn when photo dates span more than 18 months.
Test whether each photo is mirrored: solve the image and its horizontal flip, and mark it mirrored if the flip lowers the multi-view residual by more than 20%.

Use a log-normal focal prior on the 35 mm-equivalent focal length. With EXIF, sigma_log 0.05. Phone without EXIF, mean 26 mm and sigma_log 0.25. Unknown camera, mean 50 mm and sigma_log 0.6. With a single view, fix the focal length; free it only when the views span 60 degrees of yaw or more.
Distance sanity check: Z = f_px * 63 mm / IPD_px. If Z is under 0.8 m, warn about strong perspective but keep the photo.

Landmark noise in units of interocular distance: automatic internal points 0.02-0.03; contour points 0.05-0.08, using the silhouette-normal component only; ears 0.06-0.10, disabled when |yaw| is under 30 degrees; user-moved pins 0.01. Use a Huber loss with delta = 2 sigma, and down-weight views with RMS above 3 sigma.
Mask out hair and beard regions from the contour terms, and rebuild the hairline and jaw from the skull and shape prior.
Use one identity vector shared across views and a per-view expression vector with prior N(0,1). Views tagged neutral have expression fixed at 0.
Use a symmetry prior, not a constraint: sigma 1-2 mm per mirrored pair, which multi-view evidence can override.

Pick the fitting mode from view coverage: if the largest |yaw| is under 20 degrees, label depth as prior-driven and ask for a profile photo. Export a per-vertex confidence attribute to use as a sculpt mask.
Treat AI-generated meshes as weak priors only: align them with umeyama and add a shape term with sigma 3-5 mm, never as landmark ground truth.
Built-in QA: reprojection error on a held-out view, overlay and Difference renders through to_blender_camera, mirror and thumbnail views, and an optional identity-embedding cosine score.
takeaways: On these subreddits, no automatic face-from-photos route (FaceBuilder, Headshot, Face Transfer, FaceGen, photogrammetry, AI generators) is said to give a finished likeness. Each gives a base mesh, and depth, proportions, eyes and hair still need a manual sculpt pass.

The most common failures come from inputs, not tools: arm's-length selfie perspective, orthographic front/side planes that cannot line up, mirrored front-camera images, beauty filters and re-uploads, and photos taken years apart.

Perspective depends on camera distance, not focal length. The nose/ear-plane magnification ratio is about 1.2 at 0.5 m, 1.1 at 1 m and under 1.04 at 3 m or more, so close photos need a solved perspective camera, never orthographic tracing.

Photogrammetry of a live sitter with one camera works only if the sitter holds still for 1-3 minutes. Hair, beards, eyes, teeth, ear undercuts and shiny skin fail, and raw scans need a clean base mesh wrapped onto them before sculpting.
AI image-to-3D is judged useful for blockouts and small prints but weak on likeness: averaged, symmetric, baked lighting, triangle-soup topology. Gaussian splats and NeRFs are not sculptable meshes.
Likeness-craft advice: big proportions first, check every solved camera (depth errors show only in 3/4 and profile views), use mirror and thumbnail checks, and turn symmetry off for the final pass.
gaps: No Reddit thread or harvest file exists for this topic. Every community claim is author synthesis and needs thread-level confirmation. Domain-filtered reddit.com search returned HTTP 400 before, so use unfiltered queries.
No counted evidence on how often each failure mode appears, or on what photo sets users actually have (a single photo vs controlled multi-view).
No quantitative likeness benchmark (mm error or recognition rate) was found for consumer tools: FaceBuilder, Headshot, Face Transfer or AI generators.

Current prices and licences are unverified: KeenTools FaceBuilder (subscription and trial terms), Reallusion Headshot, FaceGen, Metashape editions, 3DF Zephyr Free's 50-photo cap, and the TRELLIS and Stable Fast 3D weight licences.
The capture settings in Table 3 (photo counts, shutter, aperture, distances) and the mesh counts in Table 4 are recalled, not sourced.
The proposed engine defaults (focal sigmas, landmark sigmas, mirror threshold, date-span warning) are design choices that still need tuning on synthetic and real data.
The current state of AI image-to-3D likeness (2025-26 multi-image identity-preserving models) changes fast and was not assessed.

reference-camera-setup.title: Reference images and camera matching in Blender
reference-camera-setup.summary:
I rewrote the reference-camera-setup note (about 2,850 words in the body, all 25 harvested sources kept). Every sourced fact from the earlier draft is still there, re-badged: its ⚠️ single-source marks are now 📄, and its "excluded" 1.4e-7 benchmark claim is kept as unconfirmed, not refuted. Two facts reach ✅ because two input sources agree: what fSpy computes [10][11], and that it needs scene lines [10][18]. New expert material, all marked 🧠:
- Lens-shift units follow the sensor-fit dimension. This points to a probable bug in face3d/geometry/camera.py `to_blender_camera`: it divides shift by m
algorithmic: Per-photo camera parameters [rvec, t, log f] with the principal point fixed at the image centre, optional k1/k2, and one shared head shape. Use scaled-orthographic only for initialisation.

Log-focal prior sigma by provenance: 0.03-0.05 for EXIF f35 on an uncropped original; 0.05 for EXIF f_mm with a spec-sheet sensor; 0.35 when the crop is unknown; multi-hypothesis 24-200 mm f35 with no EXIF. Tie f across photos from the same device and zoom with sigma 0.02.

Metric-scale priors: iris diameter 11.7 mm (sigma 0.5 mm) per eye; IPD 63 mm (population SD 3.5-4 mm; about 1 mm if measured), corrected for vergence when z < 1 m. Hard distance bounds 0.25-10 m, with a warning below 1 m.

Expose an explicit dolly-zoom coordinate (f/z_ref held constant) and the posterior SD of log f, flagging values above 0.15. Single-view relative error of z is roughly 11% at 0.5 m, 15-20% at 2 m and over 30% at 5 m, so lock focal beyond about 1.2 m unless side views constrain depth.

Fit jaw, cheek and chin outline landmarks as occluding-contour (silhouette) constraints, not fixed vertex correspondences. Weight interior landmarks higher, and set the Huber threshold to 1-2% of the inter-ocular pixel distance.

Fix to_blender_camera: with HORIZONTAL fit divide shift by W, not max(W,H) (or use AUTO and the larger dimension for both lens and shift). Add an H > W unit test and a round-trip test via world_to_camera_view (u = x*W, v = (1-y)*H) with tolerance below 0.01 px.
Pad all photos into a common square canvas, offsetting cx and cy, so every reference camera shares one scene render resolution.
QA outputs: per-landmark residuals, silhouette IoU, cross-view reprojection error, z and f with uncertainty, and perspective strength P = 100 mm/z (above 0.1 strong, below 0.03 near-affine).
takeaways: Perspective in a face photo is set by camera distance, not focal length. At ~0.3 m the nose tip images ~33% larger relative to the ears; at 3 m the excess is ~3%. Choose the distance first, then zoom and crop.

Never trace near-field photos in orthographic views. Rebuild each photo's camera (f_px, principal point, pose) and compare through that camera, using camera background images for camera views and image empties only for ortho or axis-aligned use.

fSpy and other vanishing-point tools need architecture in the frame. For portraits, solve the camera from facial landmarks with focal length free under an EXIF prior, and treat any fSpy result as a prior only.
A single-view overlay cannot reveal depth errors. Only cross-view reprojection (project photo A onto the mesh, view it through camera B) and a dolly-zoom (f and z together) test expose them.

A 2 degree yaw in a 'front' photo shifts the nose tip 2.4-3.5 mm against the cheeks or ears, which is above the 2-4 mm asymmetry perception thresholds. Solve the pose; never judge asymmetry from an unsolved photo.

Blender camera setup: resolution set to the photo's pixel size, pixel aspect 1, HORIZONTAL fit, lens = f_px*S_w/W, shift divided by W, clip_start about 0.01 m, background offset/scale/rotation left at identity, camera transforms locked.

Phone photos are usually distortion-corrected already. Some phones also unwarp faces in wide shots, which breaks the pinhole model, so avoid the ultra-wide lens, portrait mode and beauty filters, and keep the face centred.
gaps: Every 📄 fact rests on harvested search snippets. No source page was opened, including the Blender manual, fspy.py and the fSpy issues.

Lens-shift units and the suspected to_blender_camera bug come from my memory of Blender's source. I did not test them in Blender (it is not installed here), and the engine's tests only cover a square image.
The landmark depths behind pronasale (40/70/100 mm) are approximate expert values, not sourced anthropometry. They should be replaced from Farkas-type data once the library sources them.

Exact figures for the clinical distance effect (Ward 2018 ~30%), the Noyes & Jenkins distances and clinical lens standards were not checked. The ~12% geometric estimate against the ~30% reported figure is unresolved.

Current Blender 5.x behaviour is unverified for: EXIF Orientation handling, HEIC support, the UV Project modifier honouring camera shift, Line Art under Grease Pencil v3, image-empty option names, and the Images-as-Planes core status (4.2).
The licences of fSpy, fSpy-Blender and perspective-match, and whether the importer works on Blender 4.5/5.x, are unconfirmed.
The solver prior sigmas in Table 6 are unsourced engineering choices and need validating on real portrait photo sets.
The accuracy of the learned single-image calibrators (GeoCalib, Perspective Fields) on close-up faces is unknown.

reference-photography-protocol.title: How to shoot reference photos for 3D faces
reference-photography-protocol.summary: Neither input existed: there was no harvest and no earlier draft for this topic. So the note is written from expert knowledge plus camera arithmetic, cross-referenced to sibling notes: blender/reference-camera-setup, reconstruction/photogrammetry-heads, multi-view-fitting, community/reddit-face-from-photos, anatomy/craniometric-landmarks and blender/skin-shading. It sets out a full capture protocol: why 85–135 mm lenses are used at 1.5–2.5 m, camera height and head orientation, a core shot list of 7–9 views with an extended list of 15–20, preparing the sitter, light, smartphone and video tips,
algorithmic: Capture manifest, one JSON per session. Per photo: view_tag, nominal yaw and elevation, lens_id, tape-measured distance, expression, hair state, glasses, lighting tag. Per session: caliper measurements with σ, scale objects and the consent record. The add-on shows it as a live shot checklist.

Pose priors from view tags: yaw σ 10° freehand or 5° with floor marks; pitch σ 5° on the main ring and 8–10° on the high and low rings; roll σ 3°. A view whose solved pose differs from its nominal pose by more than 3σ is flagged as mislabelled or mirrored.
Distance prior: tape-measured z with σ ≈ 5 cm. It breaks the focal–distance degeneracy when EXIF is missing or the crop is unknown.
Intrinsics grouping key: (Make, Model, LensModel, FocalLength, W, H, still/video). log f is shared within a group with σ ≈ 0.02 and never across groups, and video always gets its own group.

Quality gates: EAR < 0.2 rejects the frame as a blink; the sharpness-relative bottom 20% by variance of the Laplacian is down-weighted; face width warns below 250 px and rejects below 120 px; more than 2% clipped skin pixels disables photometric terms; mouth aperture over 3% of IOD excludes the view from identity; hair over the ears drops the ear and temple landmarks.

Coverage score over yaw and elevation bins. Nose and chin projection count as 'measured' only with a front view plus a view with |yaw| ≥ 60°, and the jaw underside only with a low view. Otherwise those regions are shown as prior-driven in a heat-map.
Anti-duplication weighting: each view gets weight 1/(views in its 15° bin).
Caliper distances become landmark-pair residuals (σ 1–2 mm). The ID-1 card becomes a ScaleRef (σ ≈ 0.5 mm over 85.6 mm).
Lighting tags route the data: albedo and photometric terms use only even or cross-polarised views, while directional views feed landmarks and silhouettes with a per-image gain.
Video frame picker: at most 3 frames per bin, dropping frames where relative angular speed exceeds 10–15°/s (rolling-shutter skew).
takeaways: Distance, not focal length, sets perspective. Nose-over-ear magnification is about 100 mm divided by distance: 10% at 1 m, 6.7% at 1.5 m, 4% at 2.5 m. Shoot at 1.5–2.5 m with an 85–135 mm-equivalent lens (or a phone's 2–5× lens) and crop afterwards.

Core identity set: front, ±45°, ±90°, plus about 25–30° below and above, 7–9 stills. Extend to 15–20 with half-turns, rear views, a top view, ear close-ups and hair-down shots. Raise or lower the camera; never tilt the head.
Camera at the sitter's eye–nose level. A 30 cm height mismatch at 1.5 m gives 11° of pitch and about 20 mm of nose-vs-ear shift, the usual cause of 'ears too high or low'.

At matched framing, depth of field barely depends on focal length. Focus on the eyes at f/8 full frame (f/5.6 APS-C, f/4 Micro Four Thirds) to keep the nose tip and the ears sharp. At f/2.8 only about 6 cm is sharp.

Sitter: neutral face with a consistent teeth position, gaze fixed on a mark (not following the camera), hair off the ears and hairline, glasses off early, a beard logged. Take caliper measurements and put an ID-1 card in at least 2 views for scale.
Use even, diffuse light for fitting and texture. Cross-polarise only for albedo and photogrammetry. Add a directional-light set so the sculptor can read the planes.
Phones: never the front or ultra-wide camera. Lock one physical lens, because phones silently swap to the main camera; check EXIF LensModel. Disable portrait, beauty and mirror modes.

Video supplements stills and does not replace them: it has its own intrinsics and suffers rolling shutter and compression. Orbit slowly (≥25–35 s per ring) at 1/250 s or faster and pick sharp, open-eye frames. Photogrammetry is a separate pass of 40–150 photos.
gaps: There was no web harvest or prior draft for this topic, so there are no sourced URLs; every claim is expert knowledge or arithmetic.
No quantitative study is known to me of how much each added view gains in mm, or whether a 30° or 45° oblique is better for 3DMM or landmark fitting.
Phone telephoto focal lengths, crop-mode behaviour and lens-switching rules are time-sensitive and model-dependent.
Whether phone computational pipelines (multi-frame fusion, face-aware processing) measurably alter facial geometry is unknown.
The amount of cross-polarisation light loss and the exact definitions of the clinical oblique and basal views are recalled, not checked.
The ICAO and ISO distance and pose tolerances are recalled from memory.
The engine priors and QC thresholds (pose sigmas, gates) are engineering guesses and need calibration on real capture sets.

scan-cleanup-wrapping.title: Cleaning scans and wrapping base topology
scan-cleanup-wrapping.summary:
I wrote the note from scratch: this topic had no harvest and no earlier draft. Every linked source (14) comes from a sibling harvest, following the precedent set by the import-export-scans note. The rest is expert knowledge marked 🧠. Badge counts: 4 ✅, 9 📄, 53 🧠, 11 ↔️. Length is about 2,800 words counting the sources.

The note covers five areas:
- **Community cleanup pipeline:** keep a locked raw scan as the bake source, a cleaned fitting target and the base as three separate objects; denoise by frequency (radius ≤1 mm, contours masked); leave large holes open and masked; let the scan overha
algorithmic: Pipeline API: prepare_target(scan, masks) returns weights and a 2–3 mm boundary band; wrap(template, target, pairs, schedule) returns a per-vertex displacement stored as a shape key; qa() returns per-region statistics and a heat-map. Vertex order is never changed; check a topology hash.

Energy: Huber point-to-plane data term (σ_data 0.3–0.5 mm for rigs, 0.5–1 mm for one camera, 2–3 mm in the periphery) plus landmark term (points σ 1 mm, sliding contours 1.5–2 mm, ears and detector landmarks 2–3 mm) plus α·regulariser plus constraints.

Schedule: Umeyama, then TPS (λ set so the landmark residual is about σ_lm), then 4 NICP stages. Regulariser radius 15–20 → 8–10 → 4–5 mm → per vertex; α 100 → 20–50 → 5–10 → 1–2; β 1 → 0.5 → 0.2 → 0.05; correspondence caps 10 → 8 → 5 → 3 mm; normal gate 60° → 45°.
Reject pairs beyond max(3·MAD, stage cap), beyond the normal gate, or inside the boundary band. Add a reverse scan→template term at weight 0.3–0.5 to pull in concavities.

Region weights: face 1.0; lid margins 0.5; eyes, mouth and nostril interiors 0; ears 0.3–0.5 (backs 0); scalp 0.1 and beard 0.2–0.5, both one-sided (template penalised only when outside), with an inward prior of 5–15 mm, or 1–3 mm when the hair is capped.

Constraints: lid margin on the eyeball sphere plus 0–0.5 mm (σ 0.3 mm); no upper/lower lip interpenetration (hinge, margin 0–0.2 mm); edge-length log-ratio σ about 0.3; symmetry σ ≥ 3–5 mm, used only in unseen regions.
Final pass: snap along normals with a 1–2 mm ray limit, then 3–10 tangential Laplacian iterations (λ 0.3–0.5) with re-projection.
Detail split: displacement is the signed distance from the Catmull-Clark L2 surface to the raw scan, clamped to ±3 mm. A face median |d| above 0.3 mm flags a wrap failure.

Texture: per-texel normal ray to the raw scan, push-pull hole fill, 16 px dilation at 4K. Photo fallback weights views by cos^k θ (k = 2–4), cuts off at 70–75°, depth-tests, and solves per-camera gains. Work in linear float.

Acceptance defaults: face median under 0.3 mm, RMS under 0.5 mm, p95 under 1.5 mm; area ratio 0.2–5 with no flips; minimum angle above 10–15°. Never claim more accuracy than the scan modality (about 0.2–1 mm).
takeaways: Keep three objects: a locked raw scan (the only bake source), a cleaned and weighted fitting target, and the template. Never bake from a cleaned copy.

Likeness lives in forms of about 2 mm wavelength and up (complete by Multires L2 to L3, edges of about 0.4 to 0.9 mm). Denoise only at radius ≤1 mm, with lids, lips, alae and the nasolabial fold masked, and never symmetrise the shape (natural asymmetry is about 0.8 mm RMS).
Do not fill large holes you will fit to: mask them. Let the scan overhang the base. Replace the eyeballs with spheres of about 12 mm radius and cut the stomion before wrapping.

A real wrap means point pairs, then a thin-plate-spline warp, then non-rigid ICP whose stiffness and landmark weight decrease stage by stage. Shrinkwrap is only a final snap. Surface Deform passes on later deformation and does not fit; Data Transfer cannot move shape keys.

Recover detail with Multires Reshape from a shrinkwrapped copy, level by level, or by baking. Bake colour with the Emit trick and save with Save as Render off. Normal maps are OpenGL; flip green for Unreal.
4K maps (about 0.10 mm per texel on a head) already match photogrammetry resolution. Texturing the wrapped base directly from the photos inside the photogrammetry tool skips one resampling.
Mesh to MetaHuman is a vendor conform plus autorig that drifts from the likeness. Measure the drift against your own fit.
gaps: This topic had no harvest and no earlier draft. Every URL is borrowed from sibling harvests, and no community source specific to wrapping (forum thread, video, vendor doc) was harvested.
No Faceform/R3DS documentation was read. Node names, Wrapping parameters, licence and price are recalled.
No Blender manual pages for Shrinkwrap, Surface Deform, Data Transfer, Multires or Bake were read this pass. Version-specific behaviour in 5.x is unverified.
No Epic MetaHuman documentation was read. Mesh to MetaHuman behaviour from 5.6 onward rests on the sibling note and community recollection.
No measured comparison exists of Shrinkwrap-only, Wrap and NICP accuracy on the same face scans. The acceptance thresholds and the wrap schedule are design choices.
The Metashape 'Keep uv', RealityCapture texture-reprojection and de-lighting tool names and statuses are unverified.
Fact [8] (0.21 mm) came from a search snippet. The attribution of the asymmetry fact [11] was inferred from excerpts. The title of source [3] was not recorded in the harvest.

sculpting-likeness-workflow.title: Blender portrait likeness sculpting workflow
algorithmic: Coarse-to-fine DOF schedule mirroring the sculpt stages. A: similarity plus anisotropic scale (7–9 DOF). B: FFD lattice 3³–4³ or 10–30 Laplacian/PCA modes, length scale ≥ 30–40 mm. C: per-vertex offsets with 10–20 mm smoothness. D: 2–5 mm, only with dense scan or depth data.

Fixed-topology contract: never remesh inside the add-on. Emit fit_primary, fit_secondary and asym as separate shape keys. Under an existing Multires, update base coordinates with foreach_set so artist detail rides along. Push dense targets through multires_reshape from a temporary subdivided object.
Symmetry prior: σ_sym ≈ 1 mm in stages A/B, relaxed to 2–3 mm in C. Occluded regions keep a strong pull. Never symmetrize the output.
Landmark σ ≈ 0.03×IOD for interior points and 0.06–0.08×IOD for contours, with a Huber loss. IPD scale prior 63 ± 3.5 mm (1σ), overridable by a caliper measurement.
Silhouette chamfer term (rendered silhouette vs segmented photo contour) with σ ≈ 1–2 px, weighted up in profile views where depth is observable.

Stage stopping rule: landmark reprojection < 2–3% IOD, silhouette within 1–2 mm and primary ratios within ~2% in all views, or RMS improvement < 1% per iteration. Write per-region residuals and JᵀJ depth confidence as colour attributes.
Anti-averaging: down-weight the template/PCA prior where data are strong, and offer an exaggeration slider (default 0, range 0–20% of the deviation from the mean; contested).

Defaults to set: unit scale 1.0; View lens 85 mm; clip start 0.001 m; brush radius unit Scene; background alpha 0.5 with depth FRONT; lock_camera False; camera transforms locked; use_mirror_x True until the asymmetry stage; route-B voxel size 0.002–0.004 m; Multires L2 for likeness, L4–L5 for detail.
Version safety: probe for the brush asset API and sculpt_brush_type at runtime. Never hard-code brush names.
takeaways: Likeness is decided in the primary and secondary forms. Familiar faces stay recognisable at tens of pixels across, so fix the largest error at the lowest Multires level that can express it, and leave pores and wrinkles for last.

For a photo-fitted pipeline, use fixed topology. Put the template fit in shape keys, then use Multires for detail. Voxel remesh and Dyntopo are for freeform blockout only: they destroy UVs, shape keys and the landmark map.
Work at real scale (1 unit = 1 m). Voxel size, Dyntopo detail, Scene-unit brush radius and clipping are all in scene units. Tutorial values on a 2 m sphere are about 10× off.
Keep symmetry on through blockout and primaries. Fix head pose first, snapshot the symmetric state, then add the measured 0.5–4 mm asymmetries. Mirrored selfies flip asymmetry.

Judge likeness only through solved perspective cameras. Show the photo as a Background Image matched in resolution and principal point, never cropped, with Lock Camera to View off. Depth errors show only in profile and 3/4 views.
Studio checks (blink, flip, thumbnail, greyscale, held-out photo, relighting to the photo) map one-to-one onto automatable operators and residual metrics.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic, so there are zero sourced or verified claims. Every item rests on expert knowledge.
Blender 5.x sculpt changes are unknown: sculpt layers, Dyntopo status, plane-brush unification, practical Multires face limits after the 4.2–4.4 refactor.
Multires Reshape's exact topology requirement, and whether base-coordinate edits made from Python propagate cleanly under Multires, need first-party confirmation.
No measured perceptual tolerance exists for 3D likeness error in mm. Table 6 targets are engineering heuristics.
Caricature effect size and best exaggeration level for 3D portrait sculpts are unsettled.
No transcripts of professional likeness workflows were retrieved. Brush lists and per-stage radius ranges are practitioner heuristics.
Feature-width values (lid margin, vermilion ridge, wrinkles, pores) are approximate and unsourced.

sexual-dimorphism.title: Sexual dimorphism of the face and skull
sexual-dimorphism.summary: I wrote a new note on sex differences in the face and skull. There was no harvest file or earlier draft for this topic, so all 37 cited URLs come from the sibling harvests (anthropometric norms, skull osteology, soft-tissue thickness, chewing muscles, ear, eyes, facial-proportion canons). The sources JSON says so in a note field, following the precedent in forehead-brow-temple-hairline.json. The note sizes each difference with Cohen's d (how many standard deviations apart the male and female averages are). Strongly different: face height (d 1.43–1.80, computed from Kosovo and Indian data), nos
algorithmic: Shape model: X = k·R(μ̄ + (s/2)·Δ_sex + Σ c_i φ_i) + t. Δ_sex is the size-free male-minus-female mean difference, and the φ_i are PCs of the within-sex covariance, so the PCs do not encode sex a second time.

Sex prior on s, with s = −1 at the female mean and +1 at the male mean: declared sex gives N(±1, 0.65²); unspecified gives a 50/50 mixture of the two, or N(0, 1.2²); a custom setting or hormone therapy gives a user-chosen s₀ with σ ≈ 1.0. Multiply σ by 1.3 for unknown population or sparse landmarks.
Size prior: log k ~ N(log k̄ ± 0.035, 0.04²) by sex, from a male–female log-size gap of about 0.06–0.08. When metric scale comes from the camera, fix k and let s carry shape only.

Landmark sigmas (Priors.sigma in face3d/solve/bundle.py): conditioning on sex mainly shifts the means. SDs shrink only by 1/√(1 + d²/4), about 20% at d = 1.5. Suggested sex-conditioned sigmas: bony midline 2.5–4 mm, nose 3–4 mm, soft lateral points 5–8 mm. Keep the 8 mm default when sex is unspecified.

Soft-tissue coupling: t(x) = t̄(x)·exp(γ(x)·s/2 + β_bmi·(BMI − 22)). Use γ ≈ +0.10 to +0.18 at the lips, philtrum and chin; +0.05 at the forehead; −0.05 to −0.10 over the cheeks and jaw angle. Cap |γ| at 0.2, and make the BMI term larger than the sex term.

Features that should move s, weighted by d: strong are lower-face height, nose width and height, brow projection, cheekbone width, chin height and width, and masseter bulge. Exclude fWHR, beard-area silhouettes, eyebrow hair, eye-corner spacing and eye size.
Constraints stay sex-agnostic hinges only (e.g. soft glabella at least 1 mm ahead of soft nasion). No hard sex-specific bounds.
Age gate: scale Δ_sex by logistic((age − a_PHV)/1.5 y), where a_PHV (age at peak growth spurt) is about 11.5 for girls and 13.5 for boys.
Diagnostics: report the fitted s and its σ. Warn, without failing, when |s − s₀| > 2σ_s, and report per-region residuals against both sex-conditional means.

Δ_sex sources: 3DFN sex-specific summary landmarks and growth curves (European-ancestry only), or regressing a 3DMM's coefficients on sex labels (BFM 2009 attribute vectors). Licences need verification.
takeaways: Men's faces average about 5–9% larger on most linear dimensions. Face height, nose width, cheekbone width, jaw width and chin height have Cohen's d ≈ 1.3–1.8, i.e. the two distributions overlap by about 40–50%. Eye-region measures (eye-corner spacing d ≈ 0.3, eye openings, lip heights) barely differ, and eyeball size does not differ at all.

Single traits overlap heavily, but whole-face shape separates the sexes about 90–96% of the time. Sex is therefore best modelled as one continuous latent axis whose two sex means sit about 3 within-sex SDs apart, not as separate templates or hard bounds.

Much of the dimorphism is just overall size. A size-free shape difference remains at the brow and glabella (male medial brow mass, sloping forehead, dip above the brow), the nose (larger, higher bridge), the chin (taller and squarer) and the jaw. A female face is not a scaled-down male face.

The tapered female lower face comes mainly from masseter volume (about 35 vs 25 mL in older Japanese adults) and chin shape, not from the bony jaw-to-cheekbone width ratio (≈0.71 vs 0.70). 'High cheekbones' in women come from fat and a narrower lower face, not a higher zygoma.

Soft-tissue depth differs by sex in a region-specific way: men are thicker at the midline and around the mouth (mid-philtrum 16.41 vs 13.95 mm; chin 12.3 vs 11.0 mm), women are often thicker over the cheeks and jaw angle, and body weight (BMI) has a bigger effect than sex.
The jaw-angle difference between the sexes is small (about 2–6°). The repeated '90° male / 110° female' claim is wrong. fWHR is contested and should not be used as a sex cue.

Photo artefacts mimic sex differences: top lighting deepens the brow shadow, beards extend the jaw, makeup moves edges, a close camera enlarges the nose and head pitch changes the lower face. Rule these out before treating an extreme measurement as a likeness feature, and never pull real likeness features toward the sex mean.
gaps: No dedicated harvest or earlier draft existed. Every URL comes from sibling-topic harvests, and those facts are from search snippets, not full texts.
No sourced numbers for brow-ridge or glabella projection (soft glabella-to-nasion depth) by sex, although it is among the most dimorphic features.
No dense, population-specific 3D maps of male–female shape difference with within-sex SDs, so Δ_sex cannot yet be built from cited data.
Nasolabial and nasofrontal angle norms by sex are expert ranges that mix aesthetic and population data.
The 'whole-face separability ≈90–96%' and 'Mahalanobis D ≈ 3' figures are expert knowledge, but they set the key prior sigma.
No quantified effect sizes for soft-tissue facial change under adult hormone therapy.
Whether the amount of dimorphism differs between populations beyond sampling error is unknown, so the 1.3× inflation for unknown population is a guess.
The masseter volume figures (35 vs 25 mL) come from a search summary of an older Japanese cohort and are not verified against the full text.
Bigonial-to-bizygomatic ratios by sex in photo silhouettes (as opposed to calipers on bone) are unmeasured.

shapekeys-blendshapes.title: Shape keys and blendshape standards
shapekeys-blendshapes.summary:
Neither input existed: there was no shapekeys-blendshapes harvest and no earlier draft. I wrote the note (about 2,750 words) mostly from expert knowledge. I also cited 12 real URLs taken from two sibling harvests in this library: facs-expressions (Apple ARKit and Google MediaPipe docs) and blender-face-addons (Faceit, Face Shape Key Rig, CaptureForge, mediapipe-facecap). This follows the precedent set by the metahuman-cc-bridges note, and the note says where each URL came from. Nothing reached ✅, because each fact has only one source, or two pages from the same publisher.

The note covers:
- *
algorithmic: Basis structure: names[K] in canonical ARKit camelCase, D as K×V×3 float32, region masks, L/R pairs, antagonist pairs, combos as (indices, D_c), in-betweens as (k, w, D_i), plus name adapters for _L/_R, PascalCase and _neutral.

Forward model X(ψ) = X0 + Σ ψk·Dk + Σc (Π ψ)·Dc, with Jacobian Dk + Σ over combos containing k of (product of the other weights)·Dc. Precompute D at the landmark barycentric coordinates only, which gives a dense 51×51 Gauss–Newton system per view; drop tongueOut.

Priors: ψ bounded to [0,1]. Neutral views get a half-normal prior with σ 0.07 (0.05–0.10) plus L1 with λ 0.01–0.05; expressive views get σ 0.5. A calibrated MediaPipe score is an observation of ψ with σ 0.15–0.25 (0.3 uncalibrated), used to initialise or as a prior only. Antagonist product penalty weighted 1–10× the data term. Fit the jaw as a TMJ rotation with neutral prior N(1.5°, 1°²).
Conditioning: if cond(DᵀD) at the landmarks exceeds about 1e4, add a ridge term or solve in an orthogonalised basis and map back to the semantic weights.

Delta transfer: first-pass scale s = IOD_subject/IOD_template (expect 0.86–1.14) with local-frame rotation. Then deformation transfer: one sparse Poisson factorisation and 52 back-substitutions, with Jacobi-preconditioned CG as the numpy-only fallback.

MediaPipe remap: w' = clamp((w−lo)/(hi−lo),0,1)^γ, with lo at the 90th–95th percentile on neutral frames, hi at the 95th–99th over a range-of-motion clip, and γ of 1 (0.7–1.5). Smooth video with a One Euro filter (min_cutoff ≈ 1 Hz, β 0.005–0.05).

QA per key at weight 1: lid closure gap 0–0.5 mm with no crossing, lip seal at jawOpen+mouthClose, penetration count, L/R mirror RMS ≤ 0.5 mm, spill outside the mask ≤ 1–2 %, and magnitudes within the plausibility bounds table.

Blender bridge: float32 foreach_set, explicit relative_key, drivers with ID pointers and simple expressions only (`min(mc,jo)`, `max(0,1-abs(2*w-1))`, `a*b`), L/R split masks summing to 1 over a 10–20 mm midline band, respect lock_shape, and bake masks, relatives and drivers before export.
takeaways: Blender shape keys store absolute positions, not offsets. A Python write to Basis must add the same offset to every dependent key, or the expressions anti-apply the identity edit.

Use exact ARKit camelCase names for the expression set. MediaPipe's 52 scores use the same names (minus tongueOut, plus _neutral), so one rig can be driven by both phone and webcam capture and audited with the same scores. Normalise _L/_R raw strings and PascalCase CSV headers at the boundary.
Linear deltas follow chords, not arcs: about 1 mm of lid-into-cornea error and 1–4 mm of jaw error at weight 0.5. Add in-betweens (triangle and ramp drivers) or use a jaw bone.

Correctives are deterministic products of their parents' weights. Keep them in the fitting forward model so the identity does not absorb combination geometry, and write drivers as simple expressions only, so they work without Python auto-run.

After an identity fit, transfer the template's expression deltas (scale and rotate as a first pass, deformation transfer for production), then re-fit lid closure and lip seal. A plain copy is wrong for large identity changes.

Keep the likeness non-destructive: Basis is the template mean, ID_fit is the engine output (slider_max 1.5 gives a caricature dial), and artist is the sculpt layer. Bake to plain keys before export, because exporters may ignore masks, relative chains and drivers.
gaps: The topic had no harvest and no earlier draft. All Blender API behaviour (propagation semantics, operator names, lock_shape version, kb.points, 5.x changes) is unverified expert knowledge.
The full ARKit 52 list, the Apple raw strings and the left/right convention are not confirmed by any harvested source; the facs-expressions harvest explicitly failed to confirm them.
MediaPipe category ordering, the meaning of _neutral, the blendshape-head input (≈146 landmarks), and per-channel range compression are unsourced.
No quantitative source for per-blendshape surface displacement in mm: the plausibility bounds are heuristic, and D3DFACS or other 4D statistics are needed.
Exporter behaviour (FBX, glTF and USD handling of vertex_group, relative_key, in-betweens and modifiers) and engine weight conventions (Unity 0–100) are unverified.
Counts for the other standards (Meta Movement SDK 63/70, ICT FaceKit ≈53, VRM presets, Live Link CSV 61 columns) are recalled, not sourced, and are time-sensitive.
No evidence on whether product or min drivers better match real combination shapes, or on how well MediaPipe scores from still, non-frontal photos track AU intensity.

single-image-regression.title: Single-image 3D face reconstruction methods
single-image-regression.summary:
I rewrote the note (about 2,580 words before the Sources list) and wrote both JSON files: sources/single-image-regression.json and data/single-image-regression.json, which has 9 tables.

**Kept from the draft:**
- Every harvested fact and all 14 harvested URLs.
- All of the draft's ✅ results:
  - the NoW protocol, confirmed by [2] and [4];
  - DECA's validation scores, 1.18/1.46/1.25 mm (median/mean/std), confirmed by [1], [2] and [3];
  - the finding that DECA's detail layer barely changes NoW error (1.18 to 1.19 mm median), confirmed by [1] and [3].
- The correction that the 1.53 mm figure b
algorithmic: Backend interface returns: topology, coefficients, landmarks with their convention (iBUG-68 2D, 3D-consistent or MediaPipe-478), camera type (weak-perspective, affine or perspective), a metric flag and the licence.

Weak-to-perspective camera initialisation: Z0 = 2f/(s*W_b), where s is the crop-space scale, W_b the crop side in original-image pixels and f the focal length in pixels from EXIF. Lateral offset = pixel offset of the projected origin * Z0/f. For 3DDFA_V2, split the 3x4 matrix with an SVD.

Identity prior: beta ~ N(median of per-photo regressor codes, diag(sigma^2)), with sigma = spread across photos floored at 0.3 (MICA) or 0.6 (DECA) in FLAME unit-sigma units. Components the regressor does not predict get sigma = 1. These are design defaults.

Robust per-vertex residual (Huber or Student-t): scale about 1.4 mm for MICA initialisation and about 1.8 mm for DECA. These come from inverting the NoW statistics under a half-normal assumption; a mean/median ratio of about 1.23 indicates heavy tails.
Log-scale prior: sigma about 0.045 for MICA, at least 0.10 for non-metric backends, about 0.01 with a user measurement anchor (iris diameter about 11.7 ± 0.5 mm or a ruler).

Share identity and scale across views; fit expression, jaw and pose per view; set expression to 0 at hand-off. Do not initialise from 3DDFA_V2 on frames with |yaw| ≳ 90°, and down-weight frames where backends disagree.
Use sliding jawline contour correspondences or a silhouette term, so that 2D-detector jaw points do not bias jaw width as yaw changes.

Evaluation harness: NoW-style 7-landmark alignment, then scan-to-surface median, mean and std, run in both similarity and metric modes, plus REALY-style per-region errors. Log split, metric and mesh variant.
takeaways: On NoW, the best widely used identity regressor (MICA, about 0.90/1.11 mm median/mean) beats a correctly scaled average FLAME face (1.53 mm mean) by only about 0.4 mm. Regressors are priors, not likeness solutions.
DECA has two sets of NoW numbers: 1.09/1.38/1.18 mm is the test split (attribution from my own knowledge) and 1.18/1.46/1.25 mm is validation. Always cite the split with the number.
NoW solves scale during alignment and ignores detail, expression and likeness; REALY ranks methods by region and orders them differently.

DECA, EMOCA, SMIRK and 3DDFA_V2 assume an orthographic-style (weak-perspective) camera, so close-range selfies get baked into the shape (about 1.18–1.30x at 0.3–0.5 m). Shoot from 1.5 m or more, or solve a perspective camera.
Split the work by backend: MICA for neutral identity and a size guess; SMIRK, EMOCA or TEASER only to measure and reject expression; 3DDFA_V2 or MediaPipe for pose and landmarks.
Most research weights and the FLAME and BFM assets are under non-commercial terms. Build a default path from MIT and Apache parts only, and make research backends opt-in.
gaps: No input sources covered EMOCA, Deep3DFaceRecon, HRN or Pixel3DMM; their facts are all from my own knowledge (🧠).
No licence is confirmed from a source for any method or model asset.
No measured GPU or CPU timings for DECA, MICA, SMIRK, HRN or Pixel3DMM; the only sourced timing is 3DDFA_V2's.
REALY numbers are recalled ranges only, not exact per-region values.
Unknown NoW scores for SMIRK, TEASER, HRN and Pixel3DMM. Unclear which split and protocol the MICA [2] row A and the average-mesh baseline in [4] used.
No source quantifies MICA's absolute scale error, which the scale-prior sigma depends on.

skin-shading.title: Realistic skin shading in Blender
skin-shading.summary: I rewrote the skin-shading note. It covers the Blender ≥4.0 Principled BSDF subsurface inputs (Weight, Radius × Scale, Subsurface IOR, Anisotropy, Method), the Cycles-only features, how EEVEE Next approximates them, displacement microdetail, texture resources, and a table of fake-looking symptoms with their fixes. Every sourced fact from the earlier draft is kept with its citation, and the notes about the search budget are gone. One fact moved up to ✅: the developer PR and separate forum reports agree that Random Walk (Skin) fixes entry roughness at 1. Facts from my own knowledge are badged 🧠
algorithmic: Hard output contract for the fitting engine: metric units (metres); IPD prior 63 mm with σ ≈ 3.5 mm and a head-breadth check of 140–160 mm, rejecting heads more than about 10% off; watertight skin with no self-intersections; separate closed eye, teeth and tongue shells; a recommended render subdivision level so edge length is at most ¼ of the red mean free path.

Author region masks (T-zone, cheeks, lips, eyelids, ears, neck) once on the template's fixed topology and UVs, so they transfer to every fitted head. Expose per-region roughness offsets: nose −0.12, forehead −0.08, chin −0.05, cheeks/neck/ears +0.05, lips −0.12, each with σ of 0.04–0.06.

Store the subsurface radius as physical mfp in mm plus RGB ratios (1 : 0.37 : 0.19). Write Radius = mfp_mm and Scale = 0.001 / unit_settings.scale_length. Use a log-normal prior on scale with σ_ln ≈ 0.35 around red mfp 3.7 mm, range 1.5–4.8 mm.

Versioned material writer: check bpy.app.version, look up Principled sockets by identifier with fallbacks, enumerate the subsurface_method enum items at runtime, store version and engine in presets, and mark Cycles-only inputs inert for EEVEE.
Distortion-aware microdetail: compute per-face area stretch against the template. Above about 25%, warn, or rescale or retile the displacement so pores keep their physical size.

Photometric or shape-from-shading losses must treat skin shading as low-pass filtered over a few mm. Use low frequencies or the green/blue channels, mask specular pixels, and prefer cross-polarized input; otherwise a Lambertian loss distorts the geometry.
With an on-axis flash, specular highlight centres give normal constraints (normal faces the camera, σ about 5–10°).
Build a synthetic validation set: Cycles Random Walk (Skin) renders with randomized radius (log-normal), roughness (±σ) and lighting, to test how robust the landmark detectors are.
takeaways: Since Blender 4.0, skin should be Subsurface Weight 1, with Base Color as the albedo and Radius × Scale as a physical mean free path in mm on a metric head. Lowering Weight to fix waxiness misdiagnoses a scale problem.
4.x defaults (Scale 0.05 m, Radius (1, 0.2, 0.1)) give a 50 mm red radius, roughly 10–15× too large for skin. Start from Jensen skin1, Radius (3.67, 1.37, 0.68) with Scale 0.001 (🧠, to verify).
Random Walk (Skin), Subsurface IOR, Subsurface Anisotropy (manual: skin 0.8) and Specular Anisotropy are Cycles-only. EEVEE Next only approximates SSS in screen space.

Random walk scatters through the true volume. The fitted head must be watertight, free of overlaps and self-intersections, and subdivided at render to edges of about 1 mm or less, or the SSS shows facets.
Skin specular: IOR around 1.4 (F0 ≈ 0.028), white Specular Tint, Metallic 0, a regional roughness map (T-zone lower, cheeks higher). An optional low-weight Coat adds the sharp oily second lobe.

Microdetail: wrinkles go in displacement, pores in bump or normal maps at 0.2–0.5 mm peak-to-peak, varied by region. One 8K tile over the whole head (texel pitch about 0.06 mm) barely resolves pores; a face UDIM helps.
For likeness, albedo comes from the subject's own cross-polarized, chart-calibrated, de-lit photos. Lighting baked into Base Color reads as painted.
gaps: Primary-source verification of the Jensen 2001 mean-free-path values and of the anisotropy 0.8 measurement study (sample size not traced).
Exact Blender 5.x Principled subsurface method names, enum identifiers, defaults, and the thin-wall option, including when it was introduced.
EEVEE Next SSS internals and displacement support in 5.x; whether Cycles adaptive subdivision has left Experimental.
Measured regional specular roughness for skin (Weyrich et al. values) and the right way to map Beckmann m to Blender GGX perceptual roughness.
Pore density and size by facial region, and wrinkle depth by age, from profilometry studies.
Current licences and prices for skin texture resources (TexturingXYZ, 3D Scan Store, Digital Emily, MetaHuman, MPFB2).
Cause of the flat-shaded SSS artifacts in the Blender Artists thread (my explanation, render subdivision, is unconfirmed).
Measured skin albedo by Fitzpatrick type in linear RGB for albedo sanity checks.

skin-wrinkles-microdetail.title: Skin thickness, wrinkles, pores and microdetail
skin-wrinkles-microdetail.summary:
This topic had no harvest file and no earlier draft, so I wrote the note from expert knowledge only. That gives 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 74 🧠 / 32 ↔️, and no URLs are cited.

The note sits beside the existing library notes:
- **Skin thickness:** its values agree with the ultrasound measurements already sourced in anatomy/smas-ligaments.md. It points to that note by path rather than citing its URLs, because those URLs were not in this step's inputs.
- **Detail and shading:** it stays consistent with blender/skin-shading.md (Table D on microdetail size, and the orange-peel warning) and with blender/sculpting
algorithmic: Band split: fit landmarks, template warp and 3DMM only to content with wavelength of about 5 mm or more, after low-passing the targets at 2-3 mm. Put the residual into a UV displacement layer in physical units, never into shape coefficients.

Template layers authored once on the fixed topology: region masks, a tension-line direction field (sigma 10-20 deg), a skin-thickness map (log-normal sigma_log 0.2, male x1.1-1.25, over 60 x0.8-0.95) and a pore-spacing map (sigma_log 0.3).

Wrinkle primitive: z(s) = -A(1 - c s^2/sigma^2) exp(-s^2/2sigma^2), with c = 0.3-0.6 for static lines and 1.0 under compression, separate sigma per side, and a 15-25% smoothstep taper at the ends. Spacing is lambda ~ k*t, with k about 2 on the eyelid and 5-8 on the forehead; any depth prior should be weak (sigma_log 0.7).

Pore stamping in UV space: Poisson-disk sampling with minimum distance 0.75 x spacing, measured in mm through the per-face mm-per-UV Jacobian; log-normal radius (median 0.05-0.12 mm by region, sigma_log 0.35); funnel profile -A(1-r/R)^p with p 1.5-2.5, A = 0.4-1.0 R, capped at 0.15 mm; ellipses aligned to the tension lines; excluded from lids, vermilion and brows.

Resolution gate: compute mm/px for each view from the solved intrinsics and depth, enable line and pore extraction only below the thresholds (line position 0.25, fine lines 0.08, pores 0.033 mm/px), and label anything generated below the gate as synthetic.

Line detection: a Hessian valley filter at 0.3-2 mm scales on chroma-normalized luminance, keeping a line only if it agrees within 1 mm on the surface across 2 or more views. A line in at least N-1 of N neutral shots is static; otherwise it goes to an expression map.
Under expression, blur microdetail across the stretch direction and sharpen it under compression (Nagano 2015), and blend wrinkle maps by expression action-unit weight.
takeaways: Skin (epidermis plus dermis) is only 0.4-2.5 mm thick. Forensic soft-tissue depth tables (10-25 mm) include fat and muscle and must never be used as skin thickness.

Skin thickness sets how sharply underlying forms read: thin-skin zones (eyelid, nasal dorsum, ear) stay crisp, thick zones (sebaceous nasal tip, upper lip, chin) soften. Nasal skin thickness is a major likeness variable.
Wrinkles are folds, not cuts. Model them as rounded troughs with soft shoulders. Spacing scales with local skin thickness: many fine lines on the lids, few deep ones on the forehead.

Static lines (present in every neutral photo) belong in the neutral shape. Dynamic lines belong in expression shape keys or wrinkle maps, and baking them into neutral makes the sitter look older and tense.
Pores need roughly 0.03-0.05 mm/px photos. A 24 MP, 85 mm portrait at 1 m only resolves fine lines, so pores usually have to be generated from regional statistics, not copied.

Generated pores must keep their physical size through UV stretch, follow the tension-line direction, skip the eyelids and vermilion, and never be mirrored. Pore depth of 0.3 mm or more reads as orange peel.
Tertiary detail encodes age, not identity. Only marks (moles, scars, distinctive lines) need placing to about 1 mm.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic, so every quantitative value is unverified expert knowledge.
There are no normative 3D data on pore density and diameter by region, age, sex and ancestry; visible counts depend on the detection threshold.
There is no mm-scale atlas of wrinkle depth by type, age and sex; the depth ranges are broad heuristics.
Facial microrelief parameters by region (cell size, furrow depth, anisotropy) are mostly extrapolated from forearm and cheek replica studies.
The relative thickness ranking (nasal tip vs upper lip vs glabella vs chin) and how the dermis changes with age depend on the measuring method and are contested.
Whether in-vivo wrinkle spacing follows thin-film buckling scaling has not been confirmed for facial skin.
Ancestry effects on wrinkle onset and pore size are reported inconsistently, so no multipliers were given.
The current Blender 5.x status of adaptive subdivision and of Bake from Multires needs checking.
State-of-the-art single-image detail methods (DECA-style and newer) are time-sensitive and were not surveyed.

skull-osteology.title: Skull osteology that shapes the face surface
skull-osteology.summary:
I rewrote the skull-osteology note (about 2,570 words of body text, plus 51 numbered sources and 13 by-name references). I wrote two companion files: /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/skull-osteology.json and /home/user/minedesign/research/data/skull-osteology.json. The data file holds 10 tables: sourced midline depths, expert regional ranges, skin-layer thickness, sex direction by region, sourced and expert bony dimensions, infraorbital foramen distance, suggested engine priors, ordering constraints and dataset designs.

The note merges three things:
- all 23 sourced citations from the e
algorithmic: Two-layer model: skin = skull(beta_bone) + t(x; sex, age, BMI) * normal. Bone knobs: brow projection, orbit size, malar projection, bizygomatic width, maxillary projection, gonial angle, ramus height, bigonial width, chin projection/height/width, lower-face height.

Log-normal thickness priors per landmark. Means from Table 1 / data table engine_priors_suggested. sigma_log: ~0.15-0.20 at glabella, nasion, rhinion and gnathion; ~0.20-0.25 at pogonion and the orbital rims; ~0.30-0.40 at malar, buccal and gonion.

Covariates: sex as a per-region sign (sex_direction_by_region table); BMI as a positive slope, smallest on the nasal dorsum and forehead and largest in the cheek and submental area; Class III increases lower-face depth.

ViewObs.weights: nasion, glabella, pogonion and canthi 1.0; menton 0.6; tragion 0.5; zygion and gonion 0.1-0.2. Preferably use contour/silhouette residuals instead of zygion and gonion point residuals.
Anisotropic Priors.sigma (N,3) in mm (x lateral, y vertical, z depth): glabella and nasion (3,4,2); pogonion (3,4,3); menton (3,4,4); zygion and gonion (6,8,8).
Symmetry: sigma_sym 1.5-2 mm for the upper face and 3-4 mm for gonion and the lateral chin. This needs a per-pair sigma_sym array in face3d/solve/bundle.py. Never use hard symmetry.

Hinge (one-sided) ordering constraints in the Frankfort frame: z_glabella > z_nasion; z_cornea - z_lateral_orbital_rim in [12,20] mm; z_supraorbital_rim > z_lateral_orbital_rim; zygion within ±10 mm of Frankfort height; orbit width/height 1.1-1.2; gonial angle 110-135°.

Feature-preserving template warp: tag bone-driven crease curves (temporal line, lateral orbital rim, zygomatic arch, zygomaticoalveolar key ridge, mandibular border, mental tubercles) and reduce cotan-Laplacian smoothing weights across them.

Couplings: a larger gonial angle means less chin projection and a greater lower-face height. A bone edit should move the chin skin by a gain of 0.75-0.92. Use the nose/aperture relation only as a soft consistency term.
Store provenance (population, modality, living or cadaver, supine or upright, status) with every prior so pooled and single-population data are not mixed silently.
takeaways: Bone shows through skin only where the cover is thin. The midline glabella (~5-5.5 mm), nasion (~6-7 mm) and rhinion (~3 mm) and the chin (pogonion ~11-12 mm) must match the profile photo almost exactly. Cheek and masseter cover (15-25 mm) is governed by fat, muscle and BMI.

In profile at eye level the front-to-back order is brow/supraorbital rim, then corneal apex, then infraorbital rim, then lateral orbital rim. The lateral rim is the least projected, and the cornea sits about 12-20 mm in front of it (🧠, Hertel range).
The visible 'cheekbone' is the zygomatic body plus malar fat, just below the lateral orbit. The zygomatic arch sets bizygomatic width and runs roughly along the Frankfort horizontal.

The sex difference in soft-tissue depth flips by region. Men are thicker at the midline nasal and perioral points; women are thicker at lateral orbit, inferior malar and gonion. Encode sex as a per-region sign, not a global scale.
Zygion and gonion are poorly observable from skin. Weight them low or replace them with silhouette or contour residuals, and never symmetrise jaw asymmetry, which is skeletal.
Mandibular rotation couples the jaw and chin: a high gonial angle goes with a receding, narrow chin and longer lower face. The adult gonial angle is about 120°; the 90°/110° values are contested.
The piriform aperture only partly predicts the nose (weak correlations). Use it as a soft check, never as a constraint.
Depth tables are population averages that differ by modality and posture and carry large individual error. Store provenance with every prior.
gaps: No standard deviations were extracted for any soft-tissue depth landmark; all sigmas are heuristic.
Lateral and cheek depth values (supraorbital, infraorbital, lateral orbit, zygion, malar, buccal, gonion, menton) are expert ranges only, not sourced.
Temporal region: there is no soft-tissue depth in mm and no breakdown of temporalis versus fat versus bone; the Stephan & Devine 2009 and Zhao et al. 2015 papers were cited only secondhand.
The orbit dimensions (35 × 40 mm) and the Hertel range rest on one source and on knowledge respectively. The piriform aperture area (12.6-16 cm²) is suspect, probably a unit or definition error.
The Azerbaijani CT and high-frequency ultrasound skin studies came through as garbled snippets; their sample sizes and table rows still need checking against the full text.
There is no quantitative magnitude for age-related skeletal remodelling (orbit, piriform aperture, maxilla, mandible) or for edentulous lower-face collapse.
Supine CT and cadaver data have no correction to upright photos.
Observability errors for bony landmarks estimated from photographs, as opposed to CT-derived skin surfaces, are unknown; the source [11] is a non-peer-reviewed 2026 preprint.
No sculpting-practitioner or Blender-community sources on bone-driven planes were found; the artistic plane conventions (Asaro head, Hinderer lines) are expert knowledge only.
Bizygomatic and bigonial norms and cephalometric angles (SN-MP, FMA, ANS-Me/N-Me) are from memory of Farkas, Steiner, Tweed and McNamara norms and are not checked against a source.

smas-ligaments.title: SMAS and facial retaining ligaments
smas-ligaments.summary: Wrote the SMAS and retaining-ligament note from scratch. This topic had no harvest and no earlier draft, so the only URLs cited are 23 on-topic ones from sibling harvests in the library (lower-face, mid-face, upper-face and mastication muscles, skull osteology, soft-tissue thickness), and the Sources section says where they came from. The note covers: the five-layer model; regional SMAS types (Ghassemi) and the dispute over whether the SMAS is a discrete layer; true vs false ligaments (Furnas, Stuzin); orbicularis retaining ligament, tear trough, zygomatic, masseteric and mandibular ligaments,
algorithmic: Annotate the template with named ligament paths (tear trough, ORL, zygomatic, masseteric, mandibular, temporal) and fold curves (NLF, marionette). Define ligament origins on the bone layer so skeletal parameters carry them.
Make thickness variance depend on tethering: sigma_t(x) = sigma_lig + (sigma_space - sigma_lig)*m(x), with sigma_lig of about 1.0 mm and sigma_space of about 3.5 mm (heuristic).

Mobility field m: a harmonic solve with the existing cotan Laplacian, Dirichlet 0 on ligament strips, the lateral face and the bony midline, and 1 at the centroids of the prezygomatic, jowl, nasolabial and malar compartments.
Extend laplacian_deform with per-vertex row weights (W^0.5 L): ligament strips x3-5, spaces x0.5-0.7, lips x0.3; strips 3-6 mm wide.

Age basis: laxity in [0,1] with d = laxity*D*m(x)*g(x), D of about 5 mm (uncalibrated), g inferomedial in the midface and inferior at the jowl. Add deep_cheek_volume (+/-3 mm along the normal) and orbital_fat_prolapse; prior N(f(age), 0.2).

Placement priors in head-frame mm: tear trough medial end 3-6 mm below endocanthion (sigma 2), lateral end at pupil x, 14-18 mm below pupil centre (sigma 3); mandibular ligament at jaw arc fraction 0.25 +/- 0.07 from menton; masseteric line at arc fraction 0.6-0.75.

Fold image features: luminance valley detection (Hessian/ridge filter) chamfer-matched to projected fold curves, low weight, off in top-lit views. Treat folds on profile and 3/4 occluding contours as geometry.
Gate identity frames by AU6/AU12 intensity. Use a soft left/right symmetry prior (sigma about 1.5 mm) on groove positions. Down-weight supine CT priors where m > 0.5.
takeaways: Grooves (tear trough, lid-cheek junction, midcheek, prejowl) form where a ligament-tethered line meets a mobile fat mass. Sculpt the volumes on either side of the tether rather than carving the line.
The nasolabial fold is mainly a fat-boundary fold made by lip-elevator insertions, not an osteocutaneous ligament line, and which muscle dominates is contested.
The jowl forms in front of the masseteric ligaments and behind the mandibular ligament. Whether the mandibular ligament is osteocutaneous or only sub-platysmal is contested (Furnas vs Minelli 2022).
The lateral face over the parotid is effectively fixed. Expression and ageing act in front of a roughly vertical ligamentous line.
Ageing is ligament laxity plus fat deflation plus bone remodelling plus muscle tone. Model age as its own small basis so jowls and troughs do not use up identity modes.
Capture: upright, Frankfort horizontal, no top light, plus one smile frame to reveal the fixed lines. Never use smile frames for identity fitting.
CT and cadaver thickness priors are supine and under-represent upright sag over the glide spaces.
gaps: This topic's own harvest and earlier draft were absent. All cited URLs come from sibling harvests, and most periorbital and midface ligament anatomy is expert knowledge that has not been checked.
No measured SMAS thickness by region (MRI or ultrasound) is in the library.
No population dataset of 3D ligament positions relative to facial landmarks is known; the placement priors are heuristics.
Values from the 1174-adult layer-specific CT study were not extracted.
Groove depth in mm per photonumeric grade (tear trough, NLF, marionette) is not calibrated; 1 mm per grade is a placeholder.
Nobody has checked whether the 2025 'ligament of the modiolus' and the modiolus 'false ligament' studies describe the same structure.
The publication year of the NLF micro-CT paper (PMC7402499) is unclear: the harvest says 2024, while the PMC ID suggests about 2020.
The 2024 deep-fascia review (PMC11104498) was surfaced but not read.

soft-tissue-thickness.title: Facial soft-tissue thickness (forensic tissue depth tables)
soft-tissue-thickness.summary: Wrote the soft-tissue-thickness note (body ~2,800 words, sources excluded) from the 27-source harvest plus flagged expert knowledge. No earlier draft existed, so nothing was merged. Tables in the note: a 24-landmark adult consensus table (mean, range of study means, typical SD, which sex is thicker, BMI sensitivity), the Rhine & Moore 1984 male and female 21-landmark values, a dataset inventory, and the effects of method and covariates. The Rhine & Moore values are recalled from reproductions and flagged ±0.5 mm until checked. Sourced point values are in Key facts and the data JSON: Iranian MR
algorithmic: Two-layer model: skin(x) = bone(x) + t(x)·n̂_bone(x), with n̂ smoothed over 5-10 mm; constrain midline landmarks to the midsagittal plane.

Per-landmark log-normal prior: log t ~ N(log mu + beta_bmi·(BMI-22) + (delta_sex/mu)·s, sigma_log²), s = ±0.5 or 0 if sex unknown. sigma_log is 0.15-0.20 at thin midline sites, 0.20-0.25 at lips, chin and orbital rims, 0.30-0.40 at cheek, masseter and gonion.
Inflate sigma_log by 0.05-0.10 when BMI is unknown, and on lateral and lower-face sites when priors come from supine or cadaver data.

Convert a published mean±SD with sigma_log = sqrt(ln(1+(SD/mean)²)) and mu_log = ln(mean) - sigma_log²/2; pool by n-weighted means of means within a modality, and by median or shorth across modalities.
Hard constraints: hinge penalty on skin-inside-bone signed distance, and t >= t_min (2 mm, 1.5 mm at rhinion).
Inverse use: b_i = s_i - t_i n̂_i with Σ_b = Σ_s + (mu σ)² n̂n̂ᵀ + Σ_def (1-3 mm tangential). Weight the skull TPS by g, n, rhi, pg and gn; zy, go and imal are weak hints.
Interpolate mu and sigma densely over the skull with geodesic RBF, or use dense statistics (Gietzen); report per-landmark z-scores and flag |z| > 2.5 without auto-correcting.
Treat BMI as a latent per photo session and share skull parameters across sessions; keep nose, lip and ear prediction out of the FSTT module.
takeaways: FSTT spans ~3 mm (rhinion) to ~5-6.5 mm (glabella, nasion), ~10-13 mm (lips, chin) and ~15-21 mm (buccal, masseter). SDs are ~1 mm at thin midline sites and 3-5 mm laterally, so only g, n, rhi, pg and gn pin the bone tightly.
BMI is the strongest covariate; sex effects depend on the site (men thicker on the lower midline, women equal or thicker over malar and gonion); age and ancestry effects are small and contested.
Measurement method (cadaver needle, ultrasound, CT, CBCT, MRI; supine or upright; vector convention) shifts values as much as demographics; perpendicular-to-bone is the reproducible convention.

Stephan's T-tables pool across sex, ancestry and method (first in 2008, Stephan & Simpson, J Forensic Sci). The literature now spans 139 studies and more than 19,500 adults. Rhine & Moore 1984 values come from small samples of American cadavers.
For photo work the link runs backwards: photos own the skin, and tables only place hidden bone and flag implausible sculpts. Never derive nose, lip or ear shape from depth tables.

In Blender, offset bony empties inward from skin landmarks by the Table 1 means, warp a skull template, and check with pegs, a Geometry Nodes thickness map and a Solidify envelope; collect BMI and dental status with consent.
gaps: No per-landmark T-table values were in the harvest; the consensus table and Rhine & Moore values are from expert knowledge and need verification.
De Greef 2006 per-landmark means, landmark count and BMI strata were not retrieved; only the n = 967 snippet is sourced.
Supine-versus-upright and cadaver-versus-living correction magnitudes are not sourced in this library.
BMI slopes per landmark are expert estimates; only the direction and the Iranian nasion spread are sourced.
The Greek study's sample size and the TEM attribution are unconfirmed; the Thai study's design details come only from skull-osteology.md.

There is no direct agreement study comparing MRI, CBCT, CT and ultrasound, and no dense, upright, living, multi-ancestry FSTT dataset; access terms for public paired skull-face data (e.g. NMDID) are unverified.
Sub-adult FSTT priors are deferred to child-growth.md; layer-specific (skin/fat/muscle) values from the Chinese 1174-subject study were not extracted.

sota-2025-2026.title: State of the art 2025-2026 in 3D face reconstruction
sota-2025-2026.summary:
I wrote the 2025-2026 state-of-the-art note in /home/user/minedesign/research/reconstruction/sota-2025-2026.md (about 2,800 words). It has a sources file at /home/user/minedesign/research/sources/sota-2025-2026.json and six data tables at /home/user/minedesign/research/data/sota-2025-2026.json.

Neither input existed: there was no harvest (_raw/harvests/sota-2025-2026.json) and no earlier draft. So the note is my own knowledge, reliable to about mid-2025, and carries no URLs. The 2026 papers it names (KaoLRM, the profile regressor, RealDenseFace, the multi-view Gaussian paper, Marginalized BA,
algorithmic: Tag every observation with {source, version, licence, measured|generated}. Generated (diffusion, LRM or avatar) views get weight 0 on identity beta and face vertices; for ears and occiput use a silhouette term only, at ≤0.1 of a real view's weight.

Dense UV correspondences (Pixel3DMM-style): sigma 2-3% of inter-ocular distance (IOD) per sample, stride-8 px subsampling, Cauchy or Huber loss. Drop pixels within 5 px of the silhouette or with normals over 70° from the view ray. Cap the total weight at the summed landmark term.
Face-specific normals: assume a mean angular error of 12-15° (von Mises-Fisher kappa = pi/(2m^2), about 36-23), tighter than the 20° assumed for scene-trained models.

Use VGGT or MASt3R cameras only as initialisers. Accept them only if bundle adjustment converges under 2% IOD. As soft priors use rotation sigma 3-5° and focal sigma_log 0.15-0.2, and never take scale from them.
Neutral gating: a photo is neutral when every MediaPipe blendshape is ≤0.2-0.3 and the SMIRK/TEASER expression norm is under about 1 FLAME sigma. Otherwise fit psi per view and zero it at hand-off.
Keep the sibling defaults (MICA beta sigma floor 0.3, robust residual scale 1.4 mm). Tighten to 1.2 mm only if Pixel3DMM-class gains are verified.

Evaluation harness: NoW-style median, mean and std in both similarity and metric modes; REALY-style per-region errors; leave-one-view-out reprojection (accept under 2% IOD); profile silhouette error at nose tip and chin (accept under 1-1.5 mm). Use ArcFace render-vs-photo cosine as a monitor only, never as a loss.

Backend tiers: Tier 0 is shippable (MediaPipe, numpy perspective bundle adjustment, template or 3DMM). Tier 1 is opt-in research run out of process (MICA, SMIRK/TEASER, Pixel3DMM, VGGT/MASt3R, Sapiens). Tier 2 is preview-only (avatars, diffusion, LRMs).
takeaways: The field split into a geometry track (FLAME fitting with dense prediction plus optimisation: Pixel3DMM; neural-renderer self-supervision: SMIRK, TEASER, SHeaP) and an appearance track (FLAME-bound 3D Gaussians, feed-forward or diffusion-filled avatars). Only the geometry track produces sculpt-ready likeness.

NoW is near saturation (best about 0.75-0.9 mm median against 1.53 mm for a scale-fitted average face). Gaps under 0.1 mm are noise, so judge methods with region-wise (REALY-style) and held-out-view checks.

Few-shot avatar methods (LAM, Avat3r, CAP4D, FaceLift, DiffPortrait360) sample the unseen regions (occiput, ears, far profile) from priors. Treat their output as preview or blockout only, never as identity evidence.

Geometry foundation models (VGGT, MASt3R, DA3) are useful camera initialisers for hard profile shots, but are unvalidated at the millimetre level on face-only photo sets. Landmark bundle adjustment stays authoritative.

MICA remains the default identity initialiser even in 2026 pipelines. The recommended pipeline is real photos, MediaPipe or Sapiens landmarks, our own bundle adjustment, a joint FLAME/template fit with silhouettes, optional dense Pixel3DMM terms, a clamped normal-detail layer, then Multires level 2-3 (about 120k-480k faces from FLAME).

Almost every strong 2024-2026 component is research-licensed (FLAME 2020, BFM, ArcFace/InsightFace, DUSt3R/MASt3R, early VGGT weights). Ship MediaPipe plus our own fitter, and make research backends user-installed and run out of process.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed. The note has no URL-cited facts (0 ✅ / 0 📄), and every claim needs web verification.
CVPR, SIGGRAPH and ECCV 2026 and NeurIPS 2025 programmes were not reviewed. 'Best method' claims reflect knowledge up to about mid-2025, plus 2026 items harvested by sibling notes.
There are no NoW or REALY numbers for Pixel3DMM, SHeaP, TEASER or KaoLRM, and no millimetre-level geometry benchmark for any Gaussian or diffusion avatar method.
Code availability and licences for SHeaP, Avat3r, KaoLRM, CAP4D, FaceLift, LAM, GaussianAvatars/VHAP and VGGT's commercial weights are unconfirmed.
There is no face-specific evaluation of VGGT, MASt3R or DA3 camera accuracy on 5-9 portrait photos.
Dataset subject and camera counts (NeRSemble, Ava-256, RenderMe-360, FaceScape) are recalled approximations.
Compute and VRAM figures are order-of-magnitude recall, except the tracker timing taken from the sibling multi-view-fitting note.
Venues for Pixel3DMM, SHeaP, Avat3r and FaceLift are unverified, as are the details of SAM 3D (reported November 2025).

texture-extraction.title: Building a UV texture from photos
texture-extraction.summary: Wrote the texture-extraction note (about 2,470 words in the body, 2,800 with the reference list) covering how to turn solved photos into a UV texture: UV G-buffer rasterisation, footprint-aware forward projection, three-test visibility (frame, facing angle, z-buffer with ε tied to geometry error) plus occlusion-edge erosion and face-parsing masks, view weighting (vis·cos^pθ·sharpness, Schlick specular growth), the geometric misregistration law Δs ≈ δn·tanθ, blending options (average, MRF selection with Waechter levelling and Poisson, multiband, and a recommended on-surface two-band scheme that
algorithmic: New numpy module face3d/texture/: uv_gbuffer(mesh,size) using the same fan triangulation as Mesh.triangles(); zbuffer(mesh,cam,scale) at about 1–2k px wide; view_weights; solve_gains; blend(mode in two_band|multiband|select_poisson|average); fill(order=mirror,harmonic,patch,model); delight(sh_order=2, ao_gamma=0.5).
Forward projection via Camera.project (already handles k1,k2); undistort the images upstream when the solver used a richer lens model. Sample from the image pyramid at level log2(footprint), max 3.
Weight w = vis·cos^pθ·s(footprint)·m_semantic·e_edge, with p=2 (1–4, contested), θ_max 75° hard and fade from 60°, edge erosion 5 px with a 10 px ramp, frame margin 2% of width.
Depth tolerance ε = max(1 mm, 2σ_geom): 0.5–1 mm for scans, 2–5 mm for template fits. Couple it to the fitting engine's reported per-region residual σ.
