Recommended blend: a low band as a per-vertex weighted mean shared across UV seams (Gaussian σ≈3 mm on the surface), and a high band from the best view's image minus its own low-pass. Seams at UV cuts are impossible by construction.

Gain model: log I(v,k) = log g_v + log a_k with a robust Huber loss, mean log g = 0, priors σ_log 0.05 (manual) or 0.3 (auto), WB ratio σ 0.03 (locked) or 0.15 (auto), vignetting corner σ 0.5 stop per lens; at least 3 views for the specular-suppressing median.

Outputs: linear float32 albedo, confidence in [0,1], best-view index, per-texel source flag (observed/mirrored/harmonic/patch/model/generated), and a cross-view variance map usable as a photometric residual for shape fitting after gain matching.
Template-owned assets: eye, inner-mouth, nostril and scalp vertex groups become texel masks; the symmetric vertex map becomes a mirror texel map; gutter 16 px at 4K (8 at 2K, 32 at 8K).
Photometric pose refinement (Zhou & Koltun style) only for landmark-solved cameras, with σ 0.1° and 1 mm; never move SfM-imported cameras.

Memory: stream views and keep the top 3 views per texel for a second sampling pass; a float32 RGB layer is 201 MB at 4K and 805 MB at 8K, so tile at 8K. Tests: synthetic renders with random gains and ±1 mm shape noise must recover gains within 2%, with no nose colour on occluded cheek texels.
takeaways: Seams in photo-projected textures are view-transition seams on the surface, not UV seams. They come from geometric misregistration (Δs ≈ δn·tanθ: 1 mm of normal error gives about 15 px at 45° and 0.067 mm/px) and from exposure, white-balance and specular differences.

Fix geometry before texture: averaging views over a template-only fit (2–5 mm error) doubles brows, lip lines and lid creases. Use selection or two-band blending, and treat doubling as a fitting diagnostic.
Do all blending and gain compensation in linear RGB. Solve per-image gains in log space by robust least squares, plus per-lens vignetting, with priors σ≈0.05 (manual exposure) or 0.3 (auto).
Useful texel density is capped by photo GSD. 4K whole-head (~0.12 mm/texel) suits phones; 8K whole-head or a 4K face tile (~0.058 mm) suits ≥24 MP capture. Larger maps only upsample.

Visibility needs a frame test, a facing test (θ_max ≈ 75°, fading from 60°), a z-buffer test with ε ≈ max(1 mm, 2σ_geom), occlusion-edge erosion and face-parsing masks for hair, eyes and the inner mouth.

Fill holes in order of honesty (mirror low band, harmonic/push-pull, PatchMatch, statistical albedo, generative last) and record every texel's source and confidence. Diffusion fills invent moles and pigment, and albedo priors are skewed to lighter skin.
Cross-polarisation removes only specular. De-light with order-2 SH plus partial AO division (γ≈0.5); never use high-pass 'de-lighting', which destroys real low-frequency albedo.
gaps: No web harvest or prior draft existed for this topic, so no fact is sourced or verified. Every number is expert knowledge or arithmetic pending the verification pass.
No face-specific study known for the weighting exponent p, θ_max, multiband level count or AO division γ. These defaults are taste-tuned and marked contested.
No measured evaluation of how much identity or likeness diffusion or GAN UV completion preserves or alters, and no current (late-2026) state-of-the-art face-UV completion model was identified.
Skin-tone bias of statistical albedo models and learned de-lighters is flagged but not quantified.
Current Blender bake and texture-paint operator names, defaults and margin types are recalled, not checked against 2026 versions.
Typical post-correction ΔE2000, phone effective resolution (50–70% of nominal) and lens vignetting magnitudes are ranges from memory.
Assumed head and face surface areas (0.16 m² and 0.04 m²) behind the texel-pitch table are rough estimates.

texture-projection-painting.title: Projection painting and texturing heads in Blender
texture-projection-painting.summary:
Wrote the note from expert knowledge and arithmetic only: neither the harvest file nor an earlier draft existed, so no URL is cited (the sources JSON has an empty sources list plus 14 references by name). The note is about 2,680 words (counted without table pipes); its evidence line reads 0 ✅ / 0 📄 / 73 🧠 / 18 ↔️, from a count of every badge occurrence.

It covers:
- **Head UV layout:** seams, a fixed template UV, unwrap methods and stretch checks.
- **Texture Paint mode:** what it can and cannot do.
- **Three native ways to project from a solved camera:** Apply Camera Image (`paint.project_im
algorithmic: Ship the UV layout with the template. After fitting, validate per-face log area ratio (gate |r| <= 0.25, sigma about 0.12) and conformal ratio sigma1/sigma2 (<= 1.3 on the face, <= 2 on ears) from the UV-to-surface Jacobian; on failure, relax interior UVs with SLIM or ARAP and keep island boundaries pinned.

Offer projection backends engine (default), shader_preview, apply_camera_image and uvproject_bake, and choose by runtime feature probes (bpy.ops.paint.project_image, bake margin_type enum, colour-space names such as 'Linear Rec.709' vs 'Linear'), not by version number.
Per-vertex backends enforce the edge budget L <= sqrt(4*e*z), with e = 0.05 mm; otherwise subdivide or warn.

Use a single camera convention (sensor fit HORIZONTAL, shift in width units) for solver, shader and modifier. Shader UV: u = 0.5 + k*x/(-z) + shift_x and v = 0.5 + k*(W/H)*y/(-z) + shift_y*(W/H), with k = lens/sensor_width. A unit test projects a synthetic checker through every backend and requires <= 0.5 px disagreement.

Per-view visibility comes from a Geometry Nodes Raycast toward each camera that includes extra occluders (hair, glasses, eyeballs). Weight w = vis * cos^p(theta), faded from 60 to 75 degrees, shared with the numpy engine.
Gate on landmark reprojection before projecting (median <= 1.5 px, max <= 3 px).

Bake automation: bpy.ops.object.bake(type='EMIT', margin=N//256, cage_extrusion about 2 mm, max_ray_distance about 8 mm for scan-to-template transfer, use_clear=True), with 1 sample, runnable under blender -b. Projection painting needs a 3D View context, so automated tests go through bakes.
Defaults: 4096 map (2048 for phone photos, 8192 for 24 MP or more); face-to-rest texel density 1.5; paint bleed N/512 px; pack margin 16 px at 4K; 5-7 views spaced <= 45 degrees plus one low view.
Bake EXIF orientation into the pixels before both camera solving and Blender import; write albedo as half-float linear EXR and confidence as Non-Color.
takeaways: Fix UVs once on the template, with the face as one upright, symmetric island and seams hidden at the back midline, behind the ears, inside mouth, lids and nostrils, and around the neck base; never re-unwrap per subject, and never use mirrored or overlapping UVs for a likeness.

Blender can project from a solved camera natively: Apply Camera Image (paint.project_image, from the active scene camera at the photo's render resolution), the UV Project modifier or Project From View plus an Emit bake, or a per-pixel shader built from the camera's Object texture coordinates.

Per-vertex projections (modifier, Project From View) interpolate affinely with error of about L·Δz/(4z): edges of 10 mm or less at 0.5 m keep it under 0.05 mm, while a 40–80 mm cage gives 0.5–2 mm misplacement.
Texture Paint occlusion only sees the painted object, so eyeballs, hair and glasses leak colour unless masked by face selection or a Geometry Nodes Raycast visibility attribute.

Blender has no visibility-weighted multi-photo blending or gain matching. The numpy engine should make albedo.exr and confidence.png; Blender, Substance or ArmorPaint handle preview, seam cleanup and layers.

Practical killers: EXIF orientation (believed ignored by Blender), wrong render resolution or sensor fit, UV Smooth mismatch between paint and render, bleed or margin too small for mips, unsaved painted images, and judging the photo under AgX instead of Standard.
gaps: No harvest file and no earlier draft existed, so no claim is sourced. Every fact is 🧠 or ↔️ and needs web verification.
Not known: whether Blender 5.0–5.3 changed Texture Paint, the External panel, paint.project_image or the bake margin options.
Exact behaviour of Apply Camera Image is uncertain: whether brush strength, Normal fade and Bleed apply, and whether it writes partial alpha usable as a blend weight.

Not known: whether Substance 3D Painter can import cameras for projection, and what ArmorPaint offers for projection; current licences and prices for Substance, ArmorPaint, Mari, 3DCoat and ZBrush are unverified.
Ucupaint's current status and licence are unverified, as is whether Blender has gained native paint layers.
The UV area budget and texel-density ratio are conventions with no published standard. UV distortion gate values are engineering heuristics that need tuning on real fitted heads.

Conflict with reconstruction/texture-extraction.md: it asks for edges of 2–3 mm, while the arithmetic here allows about 10 mm for interpolation error alone. The note flags this as contested; neither note has changed its value.

traditional-portrait-sculpture.title: Traditional portrait sculpture methods
traditional-portrait-sculpture.summary: Neither the harvest (/home/user/minedesign/research/_raw/harvests/traditional-portrait-sculpture.json) nor an earlier draft existed. The note was written from scratch from expert knowledge, so it cites no URLs, and it was kept consistent with the sibling notes on anthropometric norms, likeness mistakes, art-anatomy books and the Blender sculpting workflow. It covers traditional clay-portrait practice. Measurement uses calipers, dividers and a plumb line, with distances triangulated from the ear holes (tragion) to stable bony landmarks. Contour checking turns sitter and clay together through 8-
algorithmic: Coarse-to-fine stage schedule: pose and scale, then masses (10–20 parameters), then a low-order basis or planar proxy (≈100–300 faces), then features, then detail. Advance a stage only when the silhouette chamfer is under about 2–3 mm in every observed view.

Landmark tiers: A, bony (n, t, ex, en, prn, sn, pg, gn, zy, go), caliper sigma 1–2 mm. B, soft or expression-dependent (ch, sto, ls, li, al), 2–4 mm. C, hair-dependent (v, eu, op, tr), one-sided bounds only and never used for scale.
Caliper term E_cal = Σ((‖Xa−Xb‖ − d_ab − o_ab)/σ_ab)². It overrides population priors. o_ab is about +2 to +5 mm for pressed pairs (zy–zy, go–go, eu–eu).
Depth priors from the ear triangles: t–n, t–sn and t–gn with sigma 6–8 mm as population priors, tightened to 1.5–2 mm when the subject was measured.

Silhouette (profile-template) term using occluding-contour correspondences recomputed each iteration, weighted per view and per region. A visual-hull hinge penalty applies only to points outside a mask, and the hair mask is an upper bound on the scalp.
Pointing pipeline: similarity or Procrustes registration on ≥3 Tier A points, then a TPS/RBF template warp from landmarks and contours, then a Laplacian or bending regulariser.
Coverage report over 8 yaw views plus above and below, with each view tagged observed, inferred or prior-only. Sample a turntable video every 22.5°. A missing view never counts as agreement.
A caliper-sheet UI listing subject, model and Δ per pair, flagging Δ > 2 mm (Tier A) or > 3 mm (Tier B).
Monochrome compensation and expression layers are shape keys held at 0 during the identity fit. Store output_scale and material_shrink (fired clay 8–15%, bronze 1–3%) in the export metadata.
takeaways: Traditional likeness comes from two checks used together. Calipers measure between bony, expression-independent landmarks. Contour matching turns sitter and clay together through 8–16 views plus above and below. Planes explain light; they do not give the likeness.

The ear hole (tragion) is the sculptor's hub. Distances from each tragion to n, prn, sn, gn, ex and ch, taken per side, fix face depth and asymmetry, and frontal photos cannot supply them. A five-minute caliper session with consent beats any prior.

A profile template is a silhouette, not the midline, and it is valid only from a distant, yaw-controlled photo. The digital equivalent is an occluding-contour residual in a solved perspective camera, recomputed every iteration.

The pointing machine is the template-warp algorithm: register on ≥3 fixed points, transfer sparse points, then carve between them, i.e. Procrustes, then a TPS/RBF warp, then a Laplacian fill. Willème's 24-camera photosculpture is a visual hull.

Studio checks map one-to-one onto digital ones: step back = thumbnail (64–128 px), squint = blur (3–5% of face width), mirror = flip, fresh eyes = held-out photos, single studio light = one matched area light.
Monochrome material loses brow, lash, lip and iris colour, so a grey sculpt reads less like the person. Bernini-style compensation belongs on an optional layer, and only for untextured output.
Life masks, supine scans and smiling photos distort soft tissue. Use them for bony structure only.
gaps: No harvest or earlier draft existed for this topic, so there are zero cited URLs and every claim is 🧠 or ↔️.
The tragion face-depth values (t–n, t–sn, t–gn) and bitragion breadth are reconstructed from geometry and need Farkas or ANSUR values.
Caliper technical error of measurement for non-expert operators, and the compression offsets of pressed landmarks against 3D surfaces, are unquantified.
No known study compares the geometric accuracy of traditional clay portraits with 3D scans of the sitter.
Historical details are unverified: the pointing machine's inventor, Willème's camera count and dates, what Houdon measured, Bernini's exact wording in Chantelou, and Rodin's credit to Constant.
Current Asaro head variants and licence terms are time-sensitive.
There are no measured values for sitting counts, over-life scale conventions or material shrink by clay body.

youtube-likeness-blender.title: YouTube: face from photos / likeness in Blender
algorithmic: Pins as first-class constraints: Pin{view, xy_px, surface(tri,bary), sigma, source}. User pins sigma 0.75% IOD; auto pins 1.5% (corners), 2.5% (lid and lip contours), 4% (face oval); Huber delta = 2 sigma; rigidity slider lambda_shape = 10^(2r-1).
Over-pinning diagnostic: list per-pin residuals worst first, flag pins above 3 sigma after convergence as 'conflicting', cap auto-suggested pins at about 12 per view.
Jaw, cheek and ear-outline pins in non-profile views are sliding silhouette constraints, re-associated to the nearest occluding-contour vertex each iteration, never fixed vertex IDs.

Photo audit gate: read EXIF focal and orientation; detect front-camera mirroring; estimate d = f_px*63 mm / IPD_px and warn below 1.0 m; below 0.6 m use the photo for texture and 2D cues only; flag crops so the principal point is freed or the original is requested.

Blender camera export: sensor_fit AUTO; lens = f_px*36/max(W,H); shift_x = (W/2 - cx)/max(W,H), shift_y = (cy - H/2)/max(W,H); render resolution W x H; unit-test the signs by reprojecting a known landmark.

Priors: IPD N(63, 3.5^2) mm or iris N(11.7, 0.5^2) mm, overridden by a measurement (sigma 1 mm); EXIF focal log-sigma 0.03, without EXIF 50 mm-equivalent with log-sigma 0.5; symmetry sigma 1 mm in early stages, 2-3 mm per-vertex; schedule similarity, then low-frequency modes (length scale 30-40 mm), then per-vertex offsets capped near 5 mm unless 2 or more views agree.

Imported meshes become point-to-plane observations: photogrammetry sigma 0.5-1 mm (eyes and hair masked or sigma x5); multi-view pin fit 1-1.5 mm; AI image-to-3D 3-5 mm with zero profile weight unless confirmed.

Sculpt-ready output contract: fixed quad topology with stable vertex order and UVs; the fit as a shape key or Multires base; separate 24 mm eye spheres; one locked camera per photo with its Background Image; checker operators (blink, flip, thumbnail, held-out view, next camera); never remesh inside the add-on; a guided 'tutorial mode' that automates each check.
takeaways: Popular YouTube likeness tutorials mostly skip rebuilding the camera behind each photo. Sculpting over orthographic planes or in a 50 mm viewport bakes selfie perspective (nose about 1.33x relative to the ears at 0.3 m), mirroring and head tilt into the mesh.

FaceBuilder (KeenTools) is the standard Blender photo-to-head route on YouTube: auto-align, then correct pins, per-view or grouped focal, texture bake, about 51 ARKit-style keys. Every serious tutorial treats its output as a base for Multires sculpting, not a finished likeness.

Common FaceBuilder mistakes: over-pinning so pins fight and create lumps, jaw-contour pins in the front view, mixed zoom without camera groups, smiling photos treated as neutral, textures taken from profile views, and running Dyntopo or remesh on the result, which destroys its UVs and blendshapes.

Photogrammetry gives the best metric shape but heads fail on sitter motion, hair, eyes and shine. It needs 3 rings of 24-36 shots with 60-80% overlap, each ring done in 20-30 s or less, then a wrap onto a template.
AI image-to-3D videos (2024-2026) produce non-metric, untopologised meshes biased toward the average face in profile. They are useful only as blockout or as a weak prior.

Follow-along tutorials break across Blender eras: the 2.79 and older UI, workflows from before voxel remesh arrived in 2.81, brush panels from before brushes became assets in 4.3, and add-on installs from before the 4.2 extensions platform. Prefer recent videos and probe for features rather than version numbers.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so no YouTube URL, video title, transcript or view count is cited. Channel names come from expert knowledge, and some (Danny Mac 3D, Zacharias Reinhardt) are moderate confidence.
Whether each named channel is active, and whether its tutorials work on Blender 5.2 LTS or 5.3, is unknown.
Not established: which YouTube tutorials actually demonstrate perspective camera matching for portraits rather than ortho planes.
No creator or vendor has published mm-level error against a ground-truth scan for any YouTube workflow (FaceBuilder, manual sculpt, phone photogrammetry, AI).
Current FaceBuilder button names, pricing, EULA terms on exported meshes and 5.x support are unverified.
The Blender defaults in Table 3 (default voxel remesh size, symmetry default) are recalled and need checking per version.
The time estimates per route are practitioner estimates, not measured.

zbrush-to-blender-likeness.title: ZBrush likeness methods translated to Blender
algorithmic: Solve all views jointly as one least-squares problem (the computational form of ZBrush whack-a-mole). Per-view parameters: rotation and translation. Focal length is shared per device and zoom setting. Shape and scale are global.

Handle focal-depth ambiguity: parametrise with inverse depth, initialise with weak perspective, then refine under full perspective with log-normal priors on f (EXIF uncropped σ_log 0.03; physical f with guessed sensor 0.10; no EXIF median 50 mm, σ_log 0.6) and on distance (median 1.0 m, σ_log 0.7).
Principal point prior at the image centre with σ = 1% of max(W,H), loosened to 10% for cropped images. Radial distortion k1 = 0 with σ 0.02; reject ultrawide images.
Scale prior: IPD 63 ± 3.7 mm by default, or a measured distance PD ± 1 mm when the user supplies one.

Coarse-to-fine stages that mirror subdivision levels: (1) similarity transform plus 10–50 identity parameters; (2) 50–200 RBF or cage control points; (3) per-vertex offsets with Laplacian regularisation. Export each stage as a dialable shape key (slider max 1.5) to emulate ZBrush Layers.

Counter the anti-mean bias of morphable models: keep stage-3 regularisation weak enough to capture idiosyncratic shape, and offer an optional distinctiveness factor k on deviation from the template (default 1.0, range 0.9–1.2).

Treat jaw and cheek outlines in non-frontal views as sliding occluding contours fitted to silhouette points, not fixed vertex IDs. Give profile-silhouette landmarks (nasion, pronasale, subnasale, pogonion) the highest weight.
Landmark noise σ as % of inter-ocular distance: inner landmarks 2–3, brows 4–6, jaw contour 5–8. Symmetry mirror penalty σ is 0.5 mm in stages 1–2, relaxed to 2–3 mm in stage 3.
Give each view expression and jaw parameters with zero-mean priors, so small smiles and jaw drop do not distort identity.

Write to Blender: per photo, lens = f_px*36/W with Sensor Fit Horizontal; shift_x = (W/2-cx)/max(W,H); shift_y = (cy-H/2)/max(W,H); background image Depth Front, opacity 0.4, Stretch; cameras bound to timeline markers. Report per-view RMS error (px and % IOD) and flag views whose residual exceeds 2x the median (wrong focal length, mirrored image, beauty filter).
takeaways: Blender's main advantage over ZBrush for likeness work is one persistent solved camera object per photo (exact lens, sensor, shift, resolution, photo as a Depth Front background image), so the artist moves cameras, never the mesh, and flips between views. ZBrush, by contrast, re-matches its single canvas camera for each view.

Most of a likeness is settled in the primary forms at low resolution (Multires levels 0–2). The profile silhouette is the most diagnostic view, and all views must be fitted together; fitting one 'hero' photo is the classic failure.

Spotlight maps to a camera background image at Depth Front with opacity about 0.4 for checking, and to Texture Paint Stencil or the UV Project modifier for projection painting. Layers map to shape keys, whose slider max can go above 1 to exaggerate. Morph Target maps to a Basis shape key plus Blend from Shape. Stored views map to cameras bound to timeline markers.

Perspective depends only on camera distance. A phone's 1x camera framing a head tightly sits at about 0.3–0.45 m, which makes the nose about 20–33% larger relative to the ears; capture from 1.5 m or more, or at 2–3x zoom.

Possible trap: the Blender viewport's '50 mm' is believed to be about 25 mm full-frame equivalent, so sculpting in the default viewport means looking through a wide-angle lens. Sculpt through matched cameras, or set the viewport lens to about 150–200 mm (to be verified).
Work at real scale (metric, display mm). Set voxel size explicitly (2–3 mm for blocking), set clip start to 1–10 mm, and anchor absolute scale with IPD or a measured prescription PD.
gaps: No web harvest or earlier draft existed, so there are no sourced or verified claims. Every fact is expert knowledge or derived arithmetic.
Attribution of specific techniques to named teachers (Spencer, Grassetti, Muñoz Gómez, Kingslien) is not verified, and their career details are time-sensitive.
ZBrush Universal Camera defaults (focal length, which axis Angle of View refers to) and the current Spotlight and See-through UI under Maxon are unverified.

Blender viewport sensor convention (doubled sensor), native sculpt-layer status, shape-key and Multires limits, and the camera X-scale -1 flip trick all need checking against current Blender releases.
Current compatibility of the GoB add-on, and whether PureRef supports click-through overlay, are unverified.
Phone camera 35 mm-equivalent focal lengths are recalled and time-sensitive.
There is no empirical data on the millimetre tolerance that makes a sculpted likeness recognisable; the 1–2 mm working target is a heuristic.
Landmark-noise sigmas and the distinctiveness factor are expert heuristics; they have not been benchmarked against detector error or recognition studies.
